===== M0015 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DependencyOptions.setMoocherDropping(boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DependencyOptions.java
Original range: 95-98
Documentation:
/**
   * Enables or disables moocher dropping mode.
   *
   * A 'moocher' is a file that does not provide any symbols (though they
   * may require symbols). This is usually because they don't want to
   * tie themselves to a particular dependency system (e.g., Closure's
   * goog.provide, CommonJS modules). So they rely on other people to
   * manage dependencies on them.
   *
   * If true, we drop these files when we prune dependencies.
   * If false, we always keep these files an anything they depend on.
   * The default is false.
   *
   * Notice that this option only makes sense if dependency pruning is on,
   * and a set of entry points is specified.
   *
   * @return this for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
95 |   public DependencyOptions setMoocherDropping(boolean enabled) {
96 |     this.dropMoochers = enabled;
97 |     return this;
98 |   }

40 |   @Override
41 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
42 |     switch(subtree.getType()) {
43 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
44 |         return tryFoldAssignment(subtree);

46 |         return tryFoldComma(subtree);

63 |           if (condition != null) {
64 |             tryFoldForCondition(condition);
65 |           }
66 |         }

===== M0029 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.flowThrough(Node,LiveVariableLattice)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 152-171
Documentation:

Method code:
152 |   @Override
153 |   LiveVariableLattice flowThrough(Node node, LiveVariableLattice input) {
154 |     final BitSet gen = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
155 |     final BitSet kill = new BitSet(input.liveSet.size());
156 | 
157 |     // Make kills conditional if the node can end abruptly by an exception.
158 |     boolean conditional = false;
159 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> edgeList = getCfg().getOutEdges(node);
160 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> edge : edgeList) {
161 |       if (Branch.ON_EX.equals(edge.getValue())) {
162 |         conditional = true;
163 |       }
164 |     }
165 |     computeGenKill(node, gen, kill, conditional);
166 |     LiveVariableLattice result = new LiveVariableLattice(input);
167 |     // L_in = L_out - Kill + Gen
168 |     result.liveSet.andNot(kill);
169 |     result.liveSet.or(gen);
170 |     return result;
171 |   }

/**
   * Writes code to an output stream, optionally wrapping it in an arbitrary
   * wrapper that contains a placeholder where the code should be inserted.
   */
Method code:
683 |   static void writeOutput(Appendable out, Compiler compiler, String code,
684 |       String wrapper, String codePlaceholder,
685 |       @Nullable Function<String, String> escaper)
686 |       throws IOException {
687 |     int pos = wrapper.indexOf(codePlaceholder);
688 |     if (pos != -1) {
689 |       String prefix = "";
690 | 
691 |       if (pos > 0) {
692 |         prefix = wrapper.substring(0, pos);
693 |         out.append(prefix);

695 |

697 | 
698 |       int suffixStart = pos + codePlaceholder.length();
699 |       if (suffixStart != wrapper.length()) {
700 |         // Something after placeholder?
701 |         out.append(wrapper.substring(suffixStart));
702 |       }
703 |       // Make sure we always end output with a line feed.
704 |       out.append('\n');
705 | 
706 |       // If we have a source map, adjust its offsets to match
707 |       // the code WITHIN the wrapper.
708 |       if (compiler != null && compiler.getSourceMap() != null) {
709 |         compiler.getSourceMap().setWrapperPrefix(prefix);
710 |       }
711 | 
712 |     } else {
713 |       out.append(code);
714 |       out.append('\n');
715 |     }
716 |   }

===== M0036 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.ReferenceCollection.isWellDefined()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 310-333
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgment.
     */
Method code:
310 |     protected boolean isWellDefined() {
311 |       int size = references.size();
312 |       if (size == 0) {
313 |         return false;
314 |       }
315 | 
316 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
317 |       // it's not well-defined.
318 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
319 |       if (init == null) {
320 |         return false;
321 |       }
322 | 
323 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
324 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
325 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
326 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
327 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
328 |           return false;
329 |         }
330 |       }
331 | 
332 |       return true;
333 |     }

===== M0054 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 477-854
Documentation:
/**
   * This is the meat of the type checking.  It is basically one big switch,
   * with each case representing one type of parse tree node.  The individual
   * cases are usually pretty straightforward.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.
   */
Method code:
477 |   @Override
478 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
479 |     JSType childType;
480 |     JSType leftType, rightType;
481 |     Node left, right;
482 |     // To be explicitly set to false if the node is not typeable.
483 |     boolean typeable = true;
484 | 
485 |     switch (n.getType()) {
486 |       case Token.CAST:
487 |         Node expr = n.getFirstChild();
488 |         ensureTyped(t, n, getJSType(expr));
489 | 
490 |         // If the cast, tightens the type apply it, so it is available post
491 |         // normalization.
492 |         JSType castType = getJSType(n);
493 |         JSType exprType = getJSType(expr);
494 |         if (castType.isSubtype(exprType)) {
495 |           expr.setJSType(castType);
496 |         }
497 |         break;
498 | 
499 |       case Token.NAME:
500 |         typeable = visitName(t, n, parent);
501 |         break;
502 | 
503 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
504 |         typeable = false;
505 |         break;
506 | 
507 |       case Token.COMMA:
508 |         ensureTyped(t, n, getJSType(n.getLastChild()));
509 |         break;
510 | 
511 |       case Token.TRUE:
512 |       case Token.FALSE:
513 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
514 |         break;
515 | 
516 |       case Token.THIS:
517 |         ensureTyped(t, n, t.getScope().getTypeOfThis());
518 |         break;
519 | 
520 |       case Token.NULL:
521 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NULL_TYPE);
522 |         break;
523 | 
524 |       case Token.NUMBER:
525 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
526 |         break;
527 | 
528 |       case Token.STRING:
529 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
530 |         break;
531 | 
532 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
533 |         typeable = false;
534 |         break;
535 | 
536 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
537 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
538 |         // Object literal keys are handled with OBJECTLIT
539 |         break;
540 | 
541 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
542 |         ensureTyped(t, n, ARRAY_TYPE);
543 |         break;
544 | 
545 |       case Token.REGEXP:
546 |         ensureTyped(t, n, REGEXP_TYPE);
547 |         break;
548 | 
549 |       case Token.GETPROP:
550 |         visitGetProp(t, n, parent);
551 |         typeable = !(parent.isAssign() &&
552 |                      parent.getFirstChild() == n);
553 |         break;
554 | 
555 |       case Token.GETELEM:
556 |         visitGetElem(t, n);
557 |         // The type of GETELEM is always unknown, so no point counting that.
558 |         // If that unknown leaks elsewhere (say by an assignment to another
559 |         // variable), then it will be counted.
560 |         typeable = false;
561 |         break;
562 | 
563 |       case Token.VAR:
564 |         visitVar(t, n);
565 |         typeable = false;
566 |         break;
567 | 
568 |       case Token.NEW:
569 |         visitNew(t, n);
570 |         break;
571 | 
572 |       case Token.CALL:
573 |         visitCall(t, n);
574 |         typeable = !parent.isExprResult();
575 |         break;
576 | 
577 |       case Token.RETURN:
578 |         visitReturn(t, n);
579 |         typeable = false;
580 |         break;
581 | 
582 |       case Token.DEC:
583 |       case Token.INC:
584 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
585 |         checkPropCreation(t, left);
586 |         validator.expectNumber(t, left, getJSType(left), "increment/decrement");
587 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
588 |         break;
589 | 
590 |       case Token.NOT:
591 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
592 |         break;
593 | 
594 |       case Token.VOID:
595 |         ensureTyped(t, n, VOID_TYPE);
596 |         break;
597 | 
598 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
599 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
600 |         break;
601 | 
602 |       case Token.BITNOT:
603 |         childType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
604 |         if (!childType.matchesInt32Context()) {
605 |           report(t, n, BIT_OPERATION, NodeUtil.opToStr(n.getType()),
606 |               childType.toString());
607 |         }
608 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
609 |         break;
610 | 
611 |       case Token.POS:
612 |       case Token.NEG:
613 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
614 |         validator.expectNumber(t, left, getJSType(left), "sign operator");
615 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
616 |         break;
617 | 
618 |       case Token.EQ:
619 |       case Token.NE:
620 |       case Token.SHEQ:
621 |       case Token.SHNE: {
622 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
623 |         right = n.getLastChild();
624 | 
625 |         if (left.isTypeOf()) {
626 |           if (right.isString()) {
627 |             checkTypeofString(t, right, right.getString());
628 |           }
629 |         } else if (right.isTypeOf() && left.isString()) {
630 |           checkTypeofString(t, left, left.getString());
631 |         }
632 | 
633 |         leftType = getJSType(left);
634 |         rightType = getJSType(right);
635 | 
636 |         // We do not want to warn about explicit comparisons to VOID. People
637 |         // often do this if they think their type annotations screwed up.
638 |         //
639 |         // We do want to warn about cases where people compare things like
640 |         // (Array|null) == (Function|null)
641 |         // because it probably means they screwed up.
642 |         //
643 |         // This heuristic here is not perfect, but should catch cases we
644 |         // care about without too many false negatives.
645 |         JSType leftTypeRestricted = leftType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
646 |         JSType rightTypeRestricted = rightType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
647 | 
648 |         TernaryValue result = TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
649 |         if (n.getType() == Token.EQ || n.getType() == Token.NE) {
650 |           result = leftTypeRestricted.testForEquality(rightTypeRestricted);
651 |           if (n.isNE()) {
652 |             result = result.not();
653 |           }
654 |         } else {
655 |           // SHEQ or SHNE
656 |           if (!leftTypeRestricted.canTestForShallowEqualityWith(
657 |                   rightTypeRestricted)) {
658 |             result = n.getType() == Token.SHEQ ?
659 |                 TernaryValue.FALSE : TernaryValue.TRUE;
660 |           }
661 |         }
662 | 
663 |         if (result != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
664 |           report(t, n, DETERMINISTIC_TEST, leftType.toString(),
665 |               rightType.toString(), result.toString());
666 |         }
667 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
668 |         break;
669 |       }
670 | 
671 |       case Token.LT:
672 |       case Token.LE:
673 |       case Token.GT:
674 |       case Token.GE:
675 |         leftType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
676 |         rightType = getJSType(n.getLastChild());
677 |         if (rightType.isNumber()) {
678 |           validator.expectNumber(
679 |               t, n, leftType, "left side of numeric comparison");
680 |         } else if (leftType.isNumber()) {
681 |           validator.expectNumber(
682 |               t, n, rightType, "right side of numeric comparison");
683 |         } else if (leftType.matchesNumberContext() &&
684 |                    rightType.matchesNumberContext()) {
685 |           // OK.
686 |         } else {
687 |           // Whether the comparison is numeric will be determined at runtime
688 |           // each time the expression is evaluated. Regardless, both operands
689 |           // should match a string context.
690 |           String message = "left side of comparison";
691 |           validator.expectString(t, n, leftType, message);
692 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
693 |               t, n, leftType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
694 |           message = "right side of comparison";
695 |           validator.expectString(t, n, rightType, message);
696 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
697 |               t, n, rightType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
698 |         }
699 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
700 |         break;
701 | 
702 |       case Token.IN:
703 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
704 |         right = n.getLastChild();
705 |         rightType = getJSType(right);
706 |         validator.expectString(t, left, getJSType(left), "left side of 'in'");
707 |         validator.expectObject(t, n, rightType, "'in' requires an object");
708 |         if (rightType.isStruct()) {
709 |           report(t, right, IN_USED_WITH_STRUCT);
710 |         }
711 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
712 |         break;
713 | 
714 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
715 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
716 |         right = n.getLastChild();
717 |         rightType = getJSType(right).restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
718 |         validator.expectAnyObject(
719 |             t, left, getJSType(left), "deterministic instanceof yields false");
720 |         validator.expectActualObject(
721 |             t, right, rightType, "instanceof requires an object");
722 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
723 |         break;
724 | 
725 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
726 |         visitAssign(t, n);
727 |         typeable = false;
728 |         break;
729 | 
730 |       case Token.ASSIGN_LSH:
731 |       case Token.ASSIGN_RSH:
732 |       case Token.ASSIGN_URSH:
733 |       case Token.ASSIGN_DIV:
734 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MOD:
735 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITOR:
736 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR:
737 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITAND:
738 |       case Token.ASSIGN_SUB:
739 |       case Token.ASSIGN_ADD:
740 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MUL:
741 |         checkPropCreation(t, n.getFirstChild());
742 |         // fall through
743 | 
744 |       case Token.LSH:
745 |       case Token.RSH:
746 |       case Token.URSH:
747 |       case Token.DIV:
748 |       case Token.MOD:
749 |       case Token.BITOR:
750 |       case Token.BITXOR:
751 |       case Token.BITAND:
752 |       case Token.SUB:
753 |       case Token.ADD:
754 |       case Token.MUL:
755 |         visitBinaryOperator(n.getType(), t, n);
756 |         break;
757 | 
758 |       case Token.DELPROP:
759 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
760 |         break;
761 | 
762 |       case Token.CASE:
763 |         JSType switchType = getJSType(parent.getFirstChild());
764 |         JSType caseType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
765 |         validator.expectSwitchMatchesCase(t, n, switchType, caseType);
766 |         typeable = false;
767 |         break;
768 | 
769 |       case Token.WITH: {
770 |         Node child = n.getFirstChild();
771 |         childType = getJSType(child);
772 |         validator.expectObject(t, child, childType, "with requires an object");
773 |         typeable = false;
774 |         break;
775 |       }
776 | 
777 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
778 |         visitFunction(t, n);
779 |         break;
780 | 
781 |       // These nodes have no interesting type behavior.
782 |       case Token.LABEL:
783 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
784 |       case Token.SWITCH:
785 |       case Token.BREAK:
786 |       case Token.CATCH:
787 |       case Token.TRY:
788 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
789 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
790 |       case Token.BLOCK:
791 |       case Token.EMPTY:
792 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
793 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
794 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
795 |       case Token.THROW:
796 |         typeable = false;
797 |         break;
798 | 
799 |       // These nodes require data flow analysis.
800 |       case Token.DO:
801 |       case Token.IF:
802 |       case Token.WHILE:
803 |         typeable = false;
804 |         break;
805 | 
806 |       case Token.FOR:
807 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
808 |           Node obj = n.getChildAtIndex(1);
809 |           if (getJSType(obj).isStruct()) {
810 |             report(t, obj, IN_USED_WITH_STRUCT);
811 |           }
812 |         }
813 |         typeable = false;
814 |         break;
815 | 
816 |       // These nodes are typed during the type inference.
817 |       case Token.AND:
818 |       case Token.HOOK:
819 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
820 |       case Token.OR:
821 |         if (n.getJSType() != null) { // If we didn't run type inference.
822 |           ensureTyped(t, n);
823 |         } else {
824 |           // If this is an enum, then give that type to the objectlit as well.
825 |           if ((n.isObjectLit())
826 |               && (parent.getJSType() instanceof EnumType)) {
827 |             ensureTyped(t, n, parent.getJSType());
828 |           } else {
829 |             ensureTyped(t, n);
830 |           }
831 |         }
832 |         if (n.isObjectLit()) {
833 |           JSType typ = getJSType(n);
834 |           for (Node key : n.children()) {
835 |             visitObjLitKey(t, key, n, typ);
836 |           }
837 |         }
838 |         break;
839 | 
840 |       default:
841 |         report(t, n, UNEXPECTED_TOKEN, Token.name(n.getType()));
842 |         ensureTyped(t, n);
843 |         break;
844 |     }
845 | 
846 |     // Don't count externs since the user's code may not even use that part.
847 |     typeable = typeable && !inExterns;
848 | 
849 |     if (typeable) {
850 |       doPercentTypedAccounting(t, n);
851 |     }
852 | 
853 |     checkNoTypeCheckSection(n, false);
854 |   }

/** Re-arrange the passes in an optimal order. */
Method code:
387 |     private void optimizePasses() {
388 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
389 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
390 |       // results.
391 |       //
392 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end
393 |       // in an "optimal" order.
394 |       List<NamedPass> optimalPasses = Lists.newArrayList();
395 |       for (String passName : OPTIMAL_ORDER) {
396 |         for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
397 |           if (pass.name.equals(passName)) {
398 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
399 |             break;
400 |           }
401 |         }
402 |       }
403 | 
404 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
405 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
406 |     }

===== M0064 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 177-289
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
177 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
178 | 
179 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
180 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.isParamList());
181 | 
182 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
183 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
184 |     boolean changed = false;
185 | 
186 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
187 |     // array.
188 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
189 | 
190 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
191 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
192 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
193 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
194 | 
195 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
196 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
197 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
198 | 
199 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
200 | 
201 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
202 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
203 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
204 |       if (!getElem.isGetElem()) {
205 |         return false;
206 |       }
207 | 
208 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
209 | 
210 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
211 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
212 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
213 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
214 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
215 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
216 |         // it is never 'callee'.
217 |         return false; // Give up.
218 |       }
219 | 
220 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
221 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
222 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
223 |       if (getElemParent.isCall() &&
224 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
225 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
226 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
227 |         return false;
228 |       }
229 | 
230 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
231 |       // than all the one we saw before.
232 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
233 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
234 |         highestIndex = value;
235 |       }
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
239 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
240 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
241 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
242 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
243 | 
244 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
245 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
246 | 
247 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
248 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
249 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
250 |       String name = getNewName();
251 |       argNames[i] = name;
252 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(IR.name(name));
253 |       changed = true;
254 |     }
255 | 
256 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
257 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
258 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
259 | 
260 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
261 |       if (!index.isNumber()) {
262 |         continue;
263 |       }
264 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
265 | 
266 |       // Unnamed parameter.
267 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
268 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
269 |             IR.name(argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
270 |       } else {
271 | 
272 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
273 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
274 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
275 | 
276 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
277 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
278 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
279 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
280 |           name = name.getNext();
281 |         }
282 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
283 |             IR.name(name.getString()));
284 |       }
285 |       changed = true;
286 |     }
287 | 
288 |     return changed;
289 |   }

===== M0079 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 454-505
Documentation:
/**
   * Replace duplicate exits in control structures.  If the node following
   * the exit node expression has the same effect as exit node, the node can
   * be replaced or removed.
   * For example:
   *   "while (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "while (a) {break} return f();"
   *   "while (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "while (a) {break} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
454 |   private Node tryReplaceExitWithBreak(Node n) {
455 |     Node result = n.getFirstChild();
456 | 
457 |     // Find the enclosing control structure, if any, that a "break" would exit
458 |     // from.
459 |     Node breakTarget = n;
460 |     for (;!ControlFlowAnalysis.isBreakTarget(breakTarget, null /* no label */);
461 |         breakTarget = breakTarget.getParent()) {
462 |       if (breakTarget.isFunction() || breakTarget.isScript()) {
463 |         // No break target.
464 |         return n;
465 |       }
466 |     }
467 | 
468 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(breakTarget);
469 | 
470 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the break and return will
471 |     // also trigger all the finally blocks. However, the order of execution is
472 |     // slightly changed. Consider:
473 |     //
474 |     // return a() -> finally { b() } -> return a()
475 |     //
476 |     // which would call a() first. However, changing the first return to a
477 |     // break will result in calling b().
478 | 
479 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
480 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
481 | 
482 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
483 |       // There were finally clauses
484 |       if (!isPure(result)) {
485 |         // Can't defer the exit
486 |         return n;
487 |       }
488 |     }
489 | 
490 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || result != null)) {
491 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
492 |       return n;
493 |     }
494 | 
495 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
496 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
497 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
498 |       Node replacement = IR.breakNode();
499 |       n.getParent().replaceChild(n, replacement);
500 |       this.reportCodeChange();
501 |       return replacement;
502 |     }
503 | 
504 |     return n;
505 |   }

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1176 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1177 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {
1178 |       return -1;
1179 |     } else if ((charno & ~COLUMN_MASK) != 0) {
1180 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1181 |     } else {
1182 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | (charno & COLUMN_MASK);
1183 |     }
1184 |   }

639 |   private void handleReturn(Node node) {
640 |     Node lastJump = null;
641 |     for (Iterator<Node> iter = exceptionHandler.iterator(); iter.hasNext();) {
642 |       Node curHandler = iter.next();
643 |       if (curHandler.isFunction()) {
644 |         break;
645 |       }
646 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(curHandler)) {
647 |         if (lastJump == null) {
648 |           createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, curHandler.getLastChild());
649 |         } else {
650 |           finallyMap.put(lastJump,
651 |               computeFallThrough(curHandler.getLastChild()));
652 |         }
653 |         lastJump = curHandler;
654 |       }
655 |     }
656 | 
657 |     if (node.hasChildren()) {
658 |       connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(node, node.getFirstChild());
659 |     }
660 | 
661 |     if (lastJump == null) {
662 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, null);
663 |     } else {
664 |       finallyMap.put(lastJump, null);
665 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeConsumer.addNumber(double)

Method code:
240 |   void addNumber(double x) {
241 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
242 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
243 |     char prev = getLastChar();
244 |     boolean negativeZero = isNegativeZero(x);
245 |     if ((x < 0 || negativeZero) && prev == '-') {
246 |       add(" ");
247 |     }
248 | 
249 |     if (negativeZero) {
250 |       addConstant("-0");
251 |     } else if ((long) x == x) {
252 |       long value = (long) x;
253 |       long mantissa = value;
254 |       int exp = 0;
255 |       if (Math.abs(x) >= 100) {
256 |         while (mantissa / 10 * Math.pow(10, exp + 1) == value) {
257 |           mantissa /= 10;
258 |           exp++;
259 |         }
260 |       }
261 |       if (exp > 2) {
262 |         addConstant(Long.toString(mantissa) + "E" + Integer.toString(exp));
263 |       } else {
264 |         long valueAbs = Math.abs(value);
265 |         if (Long.toHexString(valueAbs).length() + 2 <
266 |             Long.toString(valueAbs).length()) {
267 |           addConstant((value < 0 ? "-" : "") + "0x" +
268 |               Long.toHexString(valueAbs));
269 |         } else {
270 |           addConstant(Long.toString(value));
271 |         }
272 |       }
273 |     } else {
274 |       addConstant(String.valueOf(x).replace(".0E", "E"));
275 |     }
276 |   }

===== M0103 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 591-631
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured variables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
591 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
592 |     switch (n.getType()) {
593 |       case Token.CAST:
594 |         return isLiteralValue(n.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions);
595 | 
596 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
597 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
598 |              child = child.getNext()) {
599 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
600 |             return false;
601 |           }
602 |         }
603 |         return true;
604 | 
605 |       case Token.REGEXP:
606 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
607 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
608 |              child = child.getNext()) {
609 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
610 |             return false;
611 |           }
612 |         }
613 |         return true;
614 | 
615 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
616 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
617 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
618 |              child = child.getNext()) {
619 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
620 |             return false;
621 |           }
622 |         }
623 |         return true;
624 | 
625 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
626 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
627 | 
628 |       default:
629 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
630 |     }
631 |   }

/**
   * Determines if n matches the type and name for the following types of
   * "exits":
   *    - return without values
   *    - continues and breaks with or without names.
   * @param n The node to inspect.
   * @param type The Token type to look for.
   * @param labelName The name that must be associated with the exit type.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks associated with labels.
   * @return Whether the node matches the specified block-exit type.
   */
Method code:
284 |   static private boolean matchingExitNode(Node n, int type, String labelName) {
285 |     if (n.getType() == type) {
286 |       if (type == Token.RETURN) {
287 |         // only returns without expressions.
288 |         return !n.hasChildren();
289 |       } else {
290 |         if (labelName == null) {
291 |           return !n.hasChildren();
292 |         } else {
293 |           return n.hasChildren()
294 |             && labelName.equals(n.getFirstChild().getString());
295 |         }
296 |       }
297 |     }
298 |     return false;
299 |   }

===== M0110 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceIf(Node)

/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
306 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {

320 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
321 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
322 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
323 |             // Transform
324 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
325 |             // to
326 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
327 |             child.detachFromParent();
328 |             child.detachChildren();
329 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
330 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
331 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
332 |             reportCodeChange();
333 |           } else if (nextElse != null
334 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
335 |             // Transform
336 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
337 |             // to
338 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
339 |             child.detachFromParent();
340 |             child.detachChildren();
341 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
342 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
343 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
344 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
345 |             reportCodeChange();
346 |           }
347 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
348 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
349 |           Node thenExpr = null;
350 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
351 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
352 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
353 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
354 |           } else {
355 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
356 |           }
357 | 
358 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
359 | 
360 |           cond.detachFromParent();
361 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
362 | 
363 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
364 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
365 |                                     .srcref(child));
366 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
367 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
368 |           reportCodeChange();
369 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
370 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
371 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
372 |           reportCodeChange();
373 |         }
374 |       }
375 |     }
376 |     return n;
377 |   }

===== M0117 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.isQualifiedNameInferred(String,Node,JSDocInfo,Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypedScopeCreator.java
Original range: 1620-1663
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether a qualified name is inferred.
     * NOTE(nicksantos): Determining whether a property is declared or not
     * is really really obnoxious.
     *
     * The problem is that there are two (equally valid) coding styles:
     *
     * (function() {
     *   /* The authoritative definition of goog.bar. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * })();
     *
     * function f() {
     *   goog.bar();
     *   /* Reset goog.bar to a no-op. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * }
     *
     * In a dynamic language with first-class functions, it's very difficult
     * to know which one the user intended without looking at lots of
     * contextual information (the second example demonstrates a small case
     * of this, but there are some really pathological cases as well).
     *
     * The current algorithm checks if either the declaration has
     * JsDoc type information, or @const with a known type,
     * or a function literal with a name we haven't seen before.
     */
Method code:
1620 |     private boolean isQualifiedNameInferred(
1621 |         String qName, Node n, JSDocInfo info,
1622 |         Node rhsValue, JSType valueType) {
1623 |       if (valueType == null) {
1624 |         return true;
1625 |       }
1626 | 
1627 |       boolean inferred = true;
1628 |       if (info != null) {
1629 |         inferred = !(info.hasType()
1630 |             || info.hasEnumParameterType()
1631 |             || (info.isConstant() && valueType != null
1632 |                 && !valueType.isUnknownType())
1633 |             || FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info));
1634 |       }
1635 | 
1636 |       if (inferred && rhsValue != null && rhsValue.isFunction()) {
1637 |         if (info != null) {
1638 |           return false;
1639 |         } else if (!scope.isDeclared(qName, false) &&
1640 |             n.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
1641 | 
1642 |           // Check if this is in a conditional block.
1643 |           // Functions assigned in conditional blocks are inferred.
1644 |           for (Node current = n.getParent();
1645 |                !(current.isScript() || current.isFunction());
1646 |                current = current.getParent()) {
1647 |             if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(current)) {
1648 |               return true;
1649 |             }
1650 |           }
1651 | 
1652 |           // Check if this is assigned in an inner scope.
1653 |           // Functions assigned in inner scopes are inferred.
1654 |           AstFunctionContents contents =
1655 |               getFunctionAnalysisResults(scope.getRootNode());
1656 |           if (contents == null ||
1657 |               !contents.getEscapedQualifiedNames().contains(qName)) {
1658 |             return false;
1659 |           }
1660 |         }
1661 |       }
1662 |       return inferred;
1663 |     }

===== M0121 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.ensureTyped(NodeTraversal,Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 1967-1995
Documentation:
/**
   * Enforces type casts, and ensures the node is typed.
   *
   * A cast in the way that we use it in JSDoc annotations never
   * alters the generated code and therefore never can induce any runtime
   * operation. What this means is that a 'cast' is really just a compile
   * time constraint on the underlying value. In the future, we may add
   * support for run-time casts for compiled tests.
   *
   * To ensure some shred of sanity, we enforce the notion that the
   * type you are casting to may only meaningfully be a narrower type
   * than the underlying declared type. We also invalidate optimizations
   * on bad type casts.
   *
   * @param t The traversal object needed to report errors.
   * @param n The node getting a type assigned to it.
   * @param type The type to be assigned.
   */
Method code:
1967 |   private void ensureTyped(NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type) {
1968 |     // Make sure FUNCTION nodes always get function type.
1969 |     Preconditions.checkState(!n.isFunction() ||
1970 |             type.isFunctionType() ||
1971 |             type.isUnknownType());
1972 |     JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1973 |     if (info != null) {
1974 |       if (info.hasType()) {
1975 |         // TODO(johnlenz): Change this so that we only look for casts on CAST
1976 |         // nodes one the misplaced type annotation warning is on by default and
1977 |         // people have been given a chance to fix them.  As is, this is here
1978 |         // simply for legacy casts.
1979 |         JSType infoType = info.getType().evaluate(t.getScope(), typeRegistry);
1980 |         validator.expectCanCast(t, n, infoType, type);
1981 |         type = infoType;
1982 |       }
1983 | 
1984 |       if (info.isImplicitCast() && !inExterns) {
1985 |         String propName = n.isGetProp() ?
1986 |             n.getLastChild().getString() : "(missing)";
1987 |         compiler.report(
1988 |             t.makeError(n, ILLEGAL_IMPLICIT_CAST, propName));
1989 |       }
1990 |     }
1991 | 
1992 |     if (n.getJSType() == null) {
1993 |       n.setJSType(type);
1994 |     }
1995 |   }

===== M0161 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LiveVariablesAnalysis.computeGenKill(Node,BitSet,BitSet,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LiveVariablesAnalysis.java
Original range: 184-275
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the GEN and KILL set.
   *
   * @param n Root node.
   * @param gen Local variables that are live because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param kill Local variables that are killed because of the instruction at
   *        {@code n} will be added to this set.
   * @param conditional {@code true} if any assignments encountered are
   *        conditionally executed. These assignments might not kill a variable.
   */
Method code:
184 |   private void computeGenKill(Node n, BitSet gen, BitSet kill,
185 |       boolean conditional) {
186 | 
187 |     switch (n.getType()) {
188 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
189 |       case Token.BLOCK:
190 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
191 |         return;
192 | 
193 |       case Token.WHILE:
194 |       case Token.DO:
195 |       case Token.IF:
196 |         computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
197 |             conditional);
198 |         return;
199 | 
200 |       case Token.FOR:
201 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
202 |           computeGenKill(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), gen, kill,
203 |               conditional);
204 |         } else {
205 |           // for(x in y) {...}
206 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
207 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
208 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
209 |             // for(var x in y) {...}
210 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild();
211 |           }
212 | 
213 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
214 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
215 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
216 |           } else {
217 |             computeGenKill(lhs, gen, kill, conditional);
218 |           }
219 | 
220 |           // rhs is executed only once so we don't go into it every loop.
221 |         }
222 |         return;
223 | 
224 |       case Token.VAR:
225 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
226 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
227 |             computeGenKill(c.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
228 |             if (!conditional) {
229 |               addToSetIfLocal(c, kill);
230 |             }
231 |           }
232 |         }
233 |         return;
234 | 
235 |       case Token.AND:
236 |       case Token.OR:
237 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
238 |         // May short circuit.
239 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
240 |         return;
241 | 
242 |       case Token.HOOK:
243 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild(), gen, kill, conditional);
244 |         // Assume both sides are conditional.
245 |         computeGenKill(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), gen, kill, true);
246 |         computeGenKill(n.getLastChild(), gen, kill, true);
247 |         return;
248 | 
249 |       case Token.NAME:
250 |         if (isArgumentsName(n)) {
251 |           markAllParametersEscaped();
252 |         } else {
253 |           addToSetIfLocal(n, gen);
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 | 
257 |       default:
258 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
259 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
260 |           if (!conditional) {
261 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, kill);
262 |           }
263 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
264 |             // assignments such as a += 1 reads a.
265 |             addToSetIfLocal(lhs, gen);
266 |           }
267 |           computeGenKill(lhs.getNext(), gen, kill, conditional);
268 |         } else {
269 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
270 |             computeGenKill(c, gen, kill, conditional);
271 |           }
272 |         }
273 |         return;
274 |     }
275 |   }

/**
   * Resolves a type by looking up its first component in the scope, and
   * subsequent components as properties. The scope must have been fully
   * parsed and a symbol table constructed.
   * @return The type of the symbol, or null if the type could not be found.
   */

269 |     if (componentNames[0].length() == 0) {

271 |     }

273 |     if (slot == null) {

277 |     // names using it should be regarded as silently 'Unknown' rather than be

292 |         return null;
293 |       }
294 |       if (componentNames[i].length() == 0) {
295 |         return null;

298 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getNameForObjLitKey(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 456-508
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the fully qualified name corresponding to an object literal key,
     * as long as it and its prefix property names are valid JavaScript
     * identifiers. The object literal may be nested inside of other object
     * literals.
     *
     * For example, if called with node {@code n} representing "z" in any of
     * the following expressions, the result would be "w.x.y.z":
     * <code> var w = {x: {y: {z: 0}}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x = {y: {z: 0}}; </code>
     * <code> w.x.y = {'a': 0, 'z': 0}; </code>
     *
     * @param n A child of an OBJLIT node
     * @return The global name, or null if {@code n} doesn't correspond to the
     *   key of an object literal that can be named
     */
Method code:
456 |     String getNameForObjLitKey(Node n) {
457 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
458 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isObjectLit());
459 | 
460 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
461 |       if (gramps == null) {
462 |         return null;
463 |       }
464 | 
465 |       Node greatGramps = gramps.getParent();
466 |       String name;
467 |       switch (gramps.getType()) {
468 |         case Token.NAME:
469 |           // VAR
470 |           //   NAME (gramps)
471 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
472 |           //       STRING (n)
473 |           if (greatGramps == null || !greatGramps.isVar()) {
474 |             return null;
475 |           }
476 |           name = gramps.getString();
477 |           break;
478 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
479 |           // ASSIGN (gramps)
480 |           //   NAME|GETPROP
481 |           //   OBJLIT (parent)
482 |           //     STRING (n)
483 |           Node lvalue = gramps.getFirstChild();
484 |           name = lvalue.getQualifiedName();
485 |           break;
486 |         case Token.STRING_KEY:
487 |           // OBJLIT
488 |           //   STRING (gramps)
489 |           //     OBJLIT (parent)
490 |           //       STRING (n)
491 |           if (greatGramps != null &&
492 |               greatGramps.isObjectLit()) {
493 |             name = getNameForObjLitKey(gramps);
494 |           } else {
495 |             return null;
496 |           }
497 |           break;
498 |         default:
499 |           return null;
500 |       }
501 |       if (name != null) {
502 |         String key = n.getString();
503 |         if (TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key)) {
504 |           return name + '.' + key;
505 |         }
506 |       }
507 |       return null;
508 |     }

2024 |     @Override public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
2025 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
2026 |         return;
2027 |       }
2028 | 
2029 |       if (n.isReturn() && n.getFirstChild() != null) {
2030 |         data.get(t.getScopeRoot()).recordNonEmptyReturn();
2031 |       }
2032 | 
2033 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() <= 1) {
2034 |         // The first-order function analyzer looks at two types of variables:
2035 |         //
2036 |         // 1) Local variables that are assigned in inner scopes ("escaped vars")
2037 |         //
2038 |         // 2) Local variables that are assigned more than once.
2039 |         //
2040 |         // We treat all global variables as escaped by default, so there's
2041 |         // no reason to do this extra computation for them.
2042 |         return;
2043 |       }
2044 |

2046 |           // Be careful of bleeding functions, which create variables

2048 |           !NodeUtil.isBleedingFunctionName(n)) {
2049 |         String name = n.getString();
2050 |         Scope scope = t.getScope();
2051 |         Var var = scope.getVar(name);
2052 |         if (var != null) {
2053 |           Scope ownerScope = var.getScope();
2054 |           if (ownerScope.isLocal()) {
2055 |             data.get(ownerScope.getRootNode()).recordAssignedName(name);
2056 |           }
2057 | 
2058 |           if (scope != ownerScope && ownerScope.isLocal()) {
2059 |             data.get(ownerScope.getRootNode()).recordEscapedVarName(name);
2060 |           }
2061 |         }
2062 |       } else if (n.isGetProp() && n.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
2063 |           NodeUtil.isLValue(n)) {
2064 |         String name = NodeUtil.getRootOfQualifiedName(n).getString();

108 |     Traversal traversal = new Traversal();

110 | 
111 |     if (!traversal.hasErrors()) {
112 | 
113 |       // Apply the aliases.
114 |       for (AliasUsage aliasUsage : traversal.getAliasUsages()) {
115 |         aliasUsage.applyAlias();
116 |       }
117 | 
118 |       // Remove the alias definitions.
119 |       for (Node aliasDefinition : traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder()) {
120 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().isVar() &&

123 |         } else {
124 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();

132 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();

140 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder().size() > 0 ||
141 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
142 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 75-115
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a expression. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   * Note: unlike getBooleanValue this function does not return UNKNOWN
   * for expressions with side-effects.
   */
Method code:
75 |   static TernaryValue getImpureBooleanValue(Node n) {
76 |     switch (n.getType()) {
77 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
78 |       case Token.COMMA:
79 |         // For ASSIGN and COMMA the value is the value of the RHS.
80 |         return getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
81 |       case Token.NOT:
82 |         TernaryValue value = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
83 |         return value.not();
84 |       case Token.AND: {
85 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
86 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
87 |         return lhs.and(rhs);
88 |       }
89 |       case Token.OR:  {
90 |         TernaryValue lhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getFirstChild());
91 |         TernaryValue rhs = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
92 |         return lhs.or(rhs);
93 |       }
94 |       case Token.HOOK:  {
95 |         TernaryValue trueValue = getImpureBooleanValue(
96 |             n.getFirstChild().getNext());
97 |         TernaryValue falseValue = getImpureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild());
98 |         if (trueValue.equals(falseValue)) {
99 |           return trueValue;
100 |         } else {
101 |           return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
102 |         }
103 |       }
104 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
105 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
106 |         // ignoring side-effects
107 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
108 | 
109 |       case Token.VOID:
110 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
111 | 
112 |       default:
113 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n);
114 |     }
115 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.getPropertyType(JSType,String,Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 1305-1355

Method code:
1305 |   private JSType getPropertyType(JSType objType, String propName,
1306 |       Node n, FlowScope scope) {
1307 |     // We often have a couple of different types to choose from for the
1308 |     // property. Ordered by accuracy, we have
1309 |     // 1) A locally inferred qualified name (which is in the FlowScope)
1310 |     // 2) A globally declared qualified name (which is in the FlowScope)
1311 |     // 3) A property on the owner type (which is on objType)
1312 |     // 4) A name in the type registry (as a last resort)
1313 |     JSType propertyType = null;
1314 |     boolean isLocallyInferred = false;
1315 | 
1316 |     // Scopes sometimes contain inferred type info about qualified names.
1317 |     String qualifiedName = n.getQualifiedName();
1318 |     StaticSlot<JSType> var = scope.getSlot(qualifiedName);
1319 |     if (var != null) {
1320 |       JSType varType = var.getType();
1321 |       if (varType != null) {
1322 |         boolean isDeclared = !var.isTypeInferred();
1323 |         isLocallyInferred = (var != syntacticScope.getSlot(qualifiedName));
1324 |         if (isDeclared || isLocallyInferred) {
1325 |           propertyType = varType;
1326 |         }
1327 |       }
1328 |     }
1329 | 
1330 |     if (propertyType == null && objType != null) {
1331 |       JSType foundType = objType.findPropertyType(propName);
1332 |       if (foundType != null) {
1333 |         propertyType = foundType;
1334 |       }
1335 |     }
1336 | 
1337 |     if ((propertyType == null || propertyType.isUnknownType())
1338 |         && qualifiedName != null) {
1339 |       // If we find this node in the registry, then we can infer its type.
1340 |       ObjectType regType = ObjectType.cast(registry.getType(qualifiedName));
1341 |       if (regType != null) {
1342 |         propertyType = regType.getConstructor();
1343 |       }
1344 |     }
1345 | 
1346 |     if (propertyType == null) {
1347 |       return unknownType;
1348 |     } else if (propertyType.isEquivalentTo(unknownType) && isLocallyInferred) {
1349 |       // If the type has been checked in this scope,
1350 |       // then use CHECKED_UNKNOWN_TYPE instead to indicate that.
1351 |       return getNativeType(CHECKED_UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1352 |     } else {
1353 |       return propertyType;
1354 |     }
1355 |   }

===== M0276 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LinkedFlowScope.equals(Object)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LinkedFlowScope.java
Original range: 258-308
Documentation:

Method code:
258 |   @Override
259 |   public boolean equals(Object other) {
260 |     if (other instanceof LinkedFlowScope) {
261 |       LinkedFlowScope that = (LinkedFlowScope) other;
262 |       if (this.optimize() == that.optimize()) {
263 |         return true;
264 |       }
265 | 
266 |       // If two flow scopes are in the same function, then they could have
267 |       // two possible function scopes: the real one and the BOTTOM scope.
268 |       // If they have different function scopes, we *should* iterate through all
269 |       // the variables in each scope and compare. However, 99.9% of the time,
270 |       // they're not equal. And the other .1% of the time, we can pretend
271 |       // they're equal--this just means that data flow analysis will have
272 |       // to propagate the entry lattice a little bit further than it
273 |       // really needs to. Everything will still come out ok.
274 |       if (this.getFunctionScope() != that.getFunctionScope()) {
275 |         return false;
276 |       }
277 | 
278 |       if (cache == that.cache) {
279 |         // If the two flow scopes have the same cache, then we can check
280 |         // equality a lot faster: by just looking at the "dirty" elements
281 |         // in the cache, and comparing them in both scopes.
282 |         for (String name : cache.dirtySymbols) {
283 |           if (diffSlots(getSlot(name), that.getSlot(name))) {
284 |             return false;
285 |           }
286 |         }
287 | 
288 |         return true;
289 |       }
290 | 
291 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> myFlowSlots = allFlowSlots();
292 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> otherFlowSlots = that.allFlowSlots();
293 | 
294 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : myFlowSlots.values()) {
295 |         if (diffSlots(slot, otherFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
296 |           return false;
297 |         }
298 |         otherFlowSlots.remove(slot.getName());
299 |       }
300 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : otherFlowSlots.values()) {
301 |         if (diffSlots(slot, myFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
302 |           return false;
303 |         }
304 |       }
305 |       return true;
306 |     }
307 |     return false;
308 |   }

181 |   void add(String newcode) {
182 |     maybeEndStatement();
183 | 
184 |     if (newcode.length() == 0) {

186 |     }
187 |

189 |     if ((isWordChar(c) || c == '\\') &&

===== M0297 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 369-406
Documentation:
/**
   * Removes unreferenced arguments from a function declaration and when
   * possible the function's callSites.
   *
   * @param fnScope The scope inside the function
   */
Method code:
369 |   private void removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs(Scope fnScope) {
370 |     // Notice that removing unreferenced function args breaks
371 |     // Function.prototype.length. In advanced mode, we don't really care
372 |     // about this: we consider "length" the equivalent of reflecting on
373 |     // the function's lexical source.
374 |     //
375 |     // Rather than create a new option for this, we assume that if the user
376 |     // is removing globals, then it's OK to remove unused function args.
377 |     //
378 |     // See http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/issues/detail?id=253
379 | 
380 |     Node function = fnScope.getRootNode();
381 | 
382 |     Preconditions.checkState(function.isFunction());
383 |     if (NodeUtil.isGetOrSetKey(function.getParent())) {
384 |       // The parameters object literal setters can not be removed.
385 |       return;
386 |     }
387 | 
388 |     Node argList = getFunctionArgList(function);
389 |     boolean modifyCallers = modifyCallSites
390 |         && callSiteOptimizer.canModifyCallers(function);
391 |     if (!modifyCallers) {
392 |       // Strip unreferenced args off the end of the function declaration.
393 |       Node lastArg;
394 |       while ((lastArg = argList.getLastChild()) != null) {
395 |         Var var = fnScope.getVar(lastArg.getString());
396 |         if (!referenced.contains(var)) {
397 |           argList.removeChild(lastArg);
398 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
399 |         } else {
400 |           break;
401 |         }
402 |       }
403 |     } else {
404 |       callSiteOptimizer.optimize(fnScope, referenced);
405 |     }
406 |   }

/**
     * Look for a type declaration on a property assignment
     * (in an ASSIGN or an object literal key).
     *
     * @param info The doc info for this property.
     * @param lValue The l-value node.
     * @param rValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.
     */
Method code:
1283 |     private JSType getDeclaredType(String sourceName, JSDocInfo info,
1284 |         Node lValue, @Nullable Node rValue) {
1285 |       if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
1286 |         return getDeclaredTypeInAnnotation(sourceName, lValue, info);
1287 |       } else if (rValue != null && rValue.isFunction() &&
1288 |           shouldUseFunctionLiteralType(
1289 |               JSType.toMaybeFunctionType(rValue.getJSType()), info, lValue)) {
1290 |         return rValue.getJSType();
1291 |       } else if (info != null) {

1298 |           }

1300 |           return createFunctionTypeFromNodes(
1301 |               rValue, lValue.getQualifiedName(), info, lValue);
1302 |         } else {
1303 |           // Check if this is constant, and if it has a known type.
1304 |           if (info.isConstant()) {

1307 |               JSDocInfo rValueInfo = rValue.getJSDocInfo();
1308 |               if (rValueInfo != null && rValueInfo.hasType()) {

1310 |                 return rValueInfo.getType().evaluate(scope, typeRegistry);

1330 |               }

128 |     @Override
129 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
130 |       // Skipping over non-name nodes and empty function names.
131 |       if (!NodeUtil.isReferenceName(n)) {
132 |         return;
133 |       }
134 | 
135 |       // We focus on shadowing local variables as their name occurs much more
136 |       // than global names.
137 |       // TODO(user): Alternatively, we could experiment with using a local
138 |       // name to shadow a global variable.
139 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
140 |         return;
141 |       }
142 | 
143 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
144 |       if (var == null) {
145 |         // extern name or undefined name.
146 |         return;
147 |       }
148 | 
149 |       if (var.getScope().isGlobal()) {
150 |         // We will not shadow a global variable name.
151 |         return;
152 |       }
153 | 
154 |       // Using the definition of upward referencing, fill in the map.
155 |       if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()) {
156 |         for (Scope s = t.getScope();
157 |             s != var.getScope() && s.isLocal(); s = s.getParent()) {
158 |           scopeUpRefMap.put(s.getRootNode(), var.name);
159 |         }
160 |       }
161 | 
162 |       if (var.getScope() == t.getScope()) {
163 |         scopeUpRefMap.put(t.getScopeRoot(), var.name);
164 |       }
165 | 
166 |       // Find in the usage map that tracks a var and all of its usage.
167 |       varToNameUsage.put(var, n);
168 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCommandLineRunner.createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String>,CompilerOptions,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 1293-1352
Documentation:
/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
1293 |   @VisibleForTesting
1294 |   static void createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String> definitions,
1295 |       CompilerOptions options, boolean tweaks) {
1296 |     // Parse the definitions
1297 |     for (String override : definitions) {
1298 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
1299 |       String defName = assignment[0];
1300 | 
1301 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
1302 |         String defValue = assignment.length == 1 ? "true" : assignment[1];
1303 | 
1304 |         boolean isTrue = defValue.equals("true");
1305 |         boolean isFalse = defValue.equals("false");
1306 |         if (isTrue || isFalse) {
1307 |           if (tweaks) {
1308 |             options.setTweakToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1309 |           } else {
1310 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1311 |           }
1312 |           continue;
1313 |         } else if (defValue.length() > 1
1314 |             && ((defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1315 |                 defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'')
1316 |                 || (defValue.charAt(0) == '\"' &&
1317 |                     defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\"'))) {
1318 |           // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1319 |           // we assume that it's a string.
1320 |           String maybeStringVal =
1321 |               defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1322 |           if (maybeStringVal.indexOf(defValue.charAt(0)) == -1) {
1323 |             if (tweaks) {
1324 |               options.setTweakToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1325 |             } else {
1326 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1327 |             }
1328 |             continue;
1329 |           }
1330 |         } else {
1331 |           try {
1332 |             double value = Double.parseDouble(defValue);
1333 |             if (tweaks) {
1334 |               options.setTweakToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1335 |             } else {
1336 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1337 |             }
1338 |             continue;
1339 |           } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1340 |             // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1341 |           }
1342 |         }
1343 |       }
1344 | 
1345 |       if (tweaks) {
1346 |         throw new RuntimeException(
1347 |             "--tweak flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1348 |       }
1349 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1350 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1351 |     }
1352 |   }

310 |     public void collect(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {

343 |               break;
344 |             case Token.SETTER_DEF:

346 |               break;

348 |               throw new IllegalStateException("unexpected:" + n);
349 |           }

354 |             switch (parent.getType()) {

358 |                 type = rvalue == null ? Name.Type.OTHER : getValueType(rvalue);
359 |                 break;

361 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
362 |                   isSet = true;
363 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
364 |                 }
365 |                 break;
366 |               case Token.GETPROP:
367 |                 return;
368 |               case Token.FUNCTION:
369 |                 Node gramps = parent.getParent();
370 |                 if (gramps == null ||
371 |                     NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) return;
372 |                 isSet = true;
373 |                 type = Name.Type.FUNCTION;
374 |                 break;
375 |               case Token.INC:

377 |                 isSet = true;
378 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
379 |                 break;
380 |               default:
381 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
382 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
383 |                   isSet = true;
384 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
385 |                 }
386 |             }
387 |           }

389 |           break;
390 |         case Token.GETPROP:
391 |           // This may be a namespaced name get or set.
392 |           if (parent != null) {
393 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
394 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
395 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
396 |                   isSet = true;

398 |                   isPropAssign = true;
399 |                 }
400 |                 break;
401 |               case Token.INC:

403 |                 isSet = true;
404 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;

407 |                 return;
408 |               default:

410 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.isFoldableExpressBlock(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 926-957
Documentation:
/**
   * @return Whether the node is a block with a single statement that is
   *     an expression.
   */
Method code:
926 |   private boolean isFoldableExpressBlock(Node n) {
927 |     if (n.isBlock()) {
928 |       if (n.hasOneChild()) {
929 |         Node maybeExpr = n.getFirstChild();
930 |         if (maybeExpr.isExprResult()) {
931 |           // IE has a bug where event handlers behave differently when
932 |           // their return value is used vs. when their return value is in
933 |           // an EXPR_RESULT. It's pretty freaking weird. See:
934 |           // http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/issues/detail?id=291
935 |           // We try to detect this case, and not fold EXPR_RESULTs
936 |           // into other expressions.
937 |           if (maybeExpr.getFirstChild().isCall()) {
938 |             Node calledFn = maybeExpr.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
939 | 
940 |             // We only have to worry about methods with an implicit 'this'
941 |             // param, or this doesn't happen.
942 |             if (calledFn.isGetElem()) {
943 |               return false;
944 |             } else if (calledFn.isGetProp() &&
945 |                        calledFn.getLastChild().getString().startsWith("on")) {
946 |               return false;
947 |             }
948 |           }
949 | 
950 |           return true;
951 |         }
952 |         return false;
953 |       }
954 |     }
955 | 
956 |     return false;
957 |   }

     * @return Whether there is a initial value.

646 |     private boolean isValidInitialization(Reference initialization) {
647 |       if (initialization == null) {
648 |         return false;
649 |       } else if (initialization.isDeclaration()) {
650 |         // The reference is a FUNCTION declaration or normal VAR declaration
651 |         // with a value.
652 |         if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(initialization.getParent())
653 |             && initialization.getNode().getFirstChild() == null) {
654 |           return false;
655 |         }
656 |       } else {
657 |         Node parent = initialization.getParent();

660 |             && parent.getFirstChild() == initialization.getNode());
661 |       }
662 |

664 |       if (n.isFunction()) {
665 |         return compiler.getCodingConvention().isInlinableFunction(n);
666 |       }
667 | 
668 |       return true;
669 |     }

456 |           report(t, n, FUNCTION_MASKS_VARIABLE, functionPrivateName);

462 |         break;

464 |     return true;

182 |   public void visit(Node n) {
183 |     Node currentVersionOfNode = n;
184 |     boolean somethingChanged = false;
185 | 
186 |     do {
187 |       somethingChanged = false;
188 |       for (AbstractPeepholeOptimization optimization : peepholeOptimizations) {
189 |         Node newVersionOfNode =
190 |             optimization.optimizeSubtree(currentVersionOfNode);
191 | 
192 |         if (newVersionOfNode != currentVersionOfNode) {
193 |           somethingChanged = true;
194 | 
195 |           currentVersionOfNode = newVersionOfNode;
196 |         }
197 | 
198 |         if (currentVersionOfNode == null) {
199 |           return;
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     } while(somethingChanged);

===== M0381 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.Loop.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 322-379
Documentation:

Method code:
322 |     @Override
323 |     public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
324 |       Preconditions.checkState(!loopMutex, "Nested loops are forbidden");
325 |       loopMutex = true;
326 |       if (randomizeLoops) {
327 |         randomizePasses();
328 |       } else {
329 |         optimizePasses();
330 |       }
331 | 
332 |       // Contains a pass iff it made changes the last time it was run.
333 |       Set<NamedPass> madeChanges = new HashSet<NamedPass>();
334 |       // Contains a pass iff it was run during the last inner loop.
335 |       Set<NamedPass> runInPrevIter = new HashSet<NamedPass>();
336 |       State s = State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER;
337 |       boolean lastIterMadeChanges;
338 |       int count = 0;
339 | 
340 |       try {
341 |         while (true) {
342 |           if (count++ > MAX_LOOPS) {
343 |             compiler.throwInternalError(OPTIMIZE_LOOP_ERROR, null);
344 |           }
345 |           lastIterMadeChanges = false;
346 |           for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
347 |             recentChange.reset();
348 |             if ((s == State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER &&
349 |                 !runInPrevIter.contains(pass)) ||
350 |                 (s == State.RUN_PASSES_THAT_CHANGED_STH_IN_PREV_ITER &&
351 |                     madeChanges.contains(pass))) {
352 |               pass.process(externs, root);
353 |               runInPrevIter.add(pass);
354 |               if (hasHaltingErrors()) {
355 |                 return;
356 |               } else if (recentChange.hasCodeChanged()) {
357 |                 madeChanges.add(pass);
358 |                 lastIterMadeChanges = true;
359 |               } else {
360 |                 madeChanges.remove(pass);
361 |               }
362 |             } else {
363 |               runInPrevIter.remove(pass);
364 |             }
365 |           }
366 |           if (s == State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER) {
367 |             if (lastIterMadeChanges) {
368 |               s = State.RUN_PASSES_THAT_CHANGED_STH_IN_PREV_ITER;
369 |             } else {
370 |               return;
371 |             }
372 |           } else if (!lastIterMadeChanges) {
373 |             s = State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER;
374 |           }
375 |         }
376 |       } finally {
377 |         loopMutex = false;
378 |       }
379 |     }

===== M0386 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 516-538
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An r-value in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
516 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
517 |       switch (n.getType()) {
518 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
519 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
520 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
521 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
522 |         case Token.OR:
523 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
524 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
525 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
526 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
527 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
528 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
529 |         case Token.HOOK:
530 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
531 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
532 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
533 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
534 |           Node third = second.getNext();
535 |           return getValueType(third);
536 |       }
537 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
538 |     }
