===== M0396 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.tryMinimizeExits(Node,int,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MinimizeExitPoints.java
Original range: 114-205
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempts to minimize the number of explicit exit points in a control
   * structure to take advantage of the implied exit at the end of the
   * structure.  This is accomplished by removing redundant statements, and
   * moving statements following a qualifying IF node into that node.
   * For example:
   *
   * function () {
   *   if (x) return;
   *   else blah();
   *   foo();
   * }
   *
   * becomes:
   *
   * function () {
   *  if (x) ;
   *  else {
   *    blah();
   *    foo();
   *  }
   *
   * @param n The execution node of a parent to inspect.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName If parent is a label the name of the label to look for,
   *   null otherwise.
   * @nullable labelName non-null only for breaks within labels.
   */
Method code:
114 |   void tryMinimizeExits(Node n, int exitType, String labelName) {
115 | 
116 |     // Just an 'exit'.
117 |     if (matchingExitNode(n, exitType, labelName)) {
118 |       NodeUtil.removeChild(n.getParent(), n);
119 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
120 |       return;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Just an 'if'.
124 |     if (n.isIf()) {
125 |       Node ifBlock = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
126 |       tryMinimizeExits(ifBlock, exitType, labelName);
127 |       Node elseBlock = ifBlock.getNext();
128 |       if (elseBlock != null) {
129 |         tryMinimizeExits(elseBlock, exitType, labelName);
130 |       }
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 | 
134 |     // Just a 'try/catch/finally'.
135 |     if (n.isTry()) {
136 |       Node tryBlock = n.getFirstChild();
137 |       tryMinimizeExits(tryBlock, exitType, labelName);
138 |       Node allCatchNodes = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(n);
139 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(allCatchNodes)) {
140 |         Preconditions.checkState(allCatchNodes.hasOneChild());
141 |         Node catchNode = allCatchNodes.getFirstChild();
142 |         Node catchCodeBlock = catchNode.getLastChild();
143 |         tryMinimizeExits(catchCodeBlock, exitType, labelName);
144 |       }
145 |       if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(n)) {
146 |         Node finallyBlock = n.getLastChild();
147 |         tryMinimizeExits(finallyBlock, exitType, labelName);
148 |       }
149 |     }
150 | 
151 |     // Just a 'label'.
152 |     if (n.isLabel()) {
153 |       Node labelBlock = n.getLastChild();
154 |       tryMinimizeExits(labelBlock, exitType, labelName);
155 |     }
156 | 
157 |     // TODO(johnlenz): The last case of SWITCH statement?
158 | 
159 |     // The rest assumes a block with at least one child, bail on anything else.
160 |     if (!n.isBlock() || n.getLastChild() == null) {
161 |       return;
162 |     }
163 | 
164 |     // Multiple if-exits can be converted in a single pass.
165 |     // Convert "if (blah) break;  if (blah2) break; other_stmt;" to
166 |     // become "if (blah); else { if (blah2); else { other_stmt; } }"
167 |     // which will get converted to "if (!blah && !blah2) { other_stmt; }".
168 |     for (Node c : n.children()) {
169 | 
170 |       // An 'if' block to process below.
171 |       if (c.isIf()) {
172 |         Node ifTree = c;
173 |         Node trueBlock, falseBlock;
174 | 
175 |         // First, the true condition block.
176 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
177 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
178 |         tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(trueBlock, falseBlock,
179 |             ifTree, exitType, labelName);
180 | 
181 |         // Now the else block.
182 |         // The if blocks may have changed, get them again.
183 |         trueBlock = ifTree.getFirstChild().getNext();
184 |         falseBlock = trueBlock.getNext();
185 |         if (falseBlock != null) {
186 |           tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(falseBlock, trueBlock,
187 |               ifTree, exitType, labelName);
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 | 
191 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
192 |         break;
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     // Now try to minimize the exits of the last child, if it is removed
197 |     // look at what has become the last child.
198 |     for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getLastChild()) {
199 |       tryMinimizeExits(c, exitType, labelName);
200 |       // If the node is still the last child, we are done.
201 |       if (c == n.getLastChild()) {
202 |         break;
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 |   }

===== M0466 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 793-938
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
793 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
794 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
795 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
796 |     // that we know to be safe
797 |     switch (n.getType()) {
798 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
799 |       case Token.CAST:
800 |       case Token.AND:
801 |       case Token.BLOCK:
802 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
803 |       case Token.HOOK:
804 |       case Token.IF:
805 |       case Token.IN:
806 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
807 |       case Token.NUMBER:
808 |       case Token.OR:
809 |       case Token.THIS:
810 |       case Token.TRUE:
811 |       case Token.FALSE:
812 |       case Token.NULL:
813 |       case Token.STRING:
814 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
815 |       case Token.SWITCH:
816 |       case Token.TRY:
817 |       case Token.EMPTY:
818 |         break;
819 | 
820 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
821 |       case Token.THROW:
822 |         return true;
823 | 
824 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
825 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
826 |           return true;
827 |         }
828 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
829 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
830 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
831 |             return true;
832 |           }
833 |         }
834 |         return false;
835 | 
836 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
837 |       case Token.REGEXP:
838 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
839 |           return true;
840 |         }
841 |         break;
842 | 
843 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
844 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
845 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
846 |           return true;
847 |         }
848 |         break;
849 | 
850 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
851 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
852 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
853 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
854 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
855 | 
856 |       case Token.NEW:
857 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
858 |           return true;
859 |         }
860 | 
861 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
862 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
863 |           // side-effects
864 |           break;
865 |         }
866 |         return true;
867 | 
868 |       case Token.CALL:
869 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
870 |         // side effect property set.
871 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
872 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
873 |           // side-effects
874 |           break;
875 |         }
876 |         return true;
877 | 
878 |       default:
879 |         if (isSimpleOperator(n)) {
880 |           break;
881 |         }
882 | 
883 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
884 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
885 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
886 |             return true;
887 |           }
888 | 
889 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
890 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
891 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
892 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
893 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
894 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
895 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
896 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
897 |             return true;
898 |           }
899 | 
900 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
901 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
902 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
903 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
904 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
905 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
906 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
907 |               return false;
908 |             }
909 | 
910 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
911 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
912 |             // other objects.
913 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
914 |             // side-effect.
915 |             while (isGet(current)) {
916 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
917 |             }
918 | 
919 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
920 |           } else {
921 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
922 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
923 |             // preserve existing behavior.
924 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
925 |           }
926 |         }
927 | 
928 |         return true;
929 |     }
930 | 
931 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
932 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
933 |         return true;
934 |       }
935 |     }
936 | 
937 |     return false;
938 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2428 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2429 |     int len = s.length();
2430 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2431 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2432 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2433 |         return false;
2434 |       }
2435 |     }
2436 |     return true;
2437 |   }

===== M0484 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MustBeReachingVariableDef.MustDefJoin.apply(MustDef,MustDef)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MustBeReachingVariableDef.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |     @Override
149 |     public MustDef apply(MustDef a, MustDef b) {
150 |       MustDef result = new MustDef();
151 |       Map<Var, Definition> resultMap = result.reachingDef;
152 | 
153 |       // Take the join of all variables that are not TOP in this.
154 |       for (Map.Entry<Var, Definition> varEntry : a.reachingDef.entrySet()) {
155 |         Var var = varEntry.getKey();
156 |         Definition aDef = varEntry.getValue();
157 | 
158 |         if (aDef == null) {
159 |           // "a" is BOTTOM implies that the variable has more than one possible
160 |           // definition. We set the join of this to be BOTTOM regardless of what
161 |           // "b" might be.
162 |           resultMap.put(var, null);
163 |           continue;
164 |         }
165 | 
166 |         Node aNode = aDef.node;
167 | 
168 |         if (b.reachingDef.containsKey(var)) {
169 |           Definition bDef = b.reachingDef.get(var);
170 | 
171 |           if (aDef.equals(bDef)) {
172 |             resultMap.put(var, aDef);
173 |           } else {
174 |             resultMap.put(var, null);
175 |           }
176 |         } else {
177 |           resultMap.put(var, aDef);
178 |         }
179 |       }
180 | 
181 |       // Take the join of all variables that are not TOP in other but it is TOP
182 |       // in this.
183 |       for (Map.Entry<Var, Definition> entry : b.reachingDef.entrySet()) {
184 |         Var var = entry.getKey();
185 |         if (!a.reachingDef.containsKey(var)) {
186 |           resultMap.put(var, entry.getValue());
187 |         }
188 |       }
189 |       return result;
190 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 35-82
Documentation:

Method code:
35 |   @Override
36 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
37 |     if (!subtree.isScript() && !subtree.isBlock()) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (!child.isVar() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (!name.isName()) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

895 | 
896 |     // Check property sets to 'object.property' when 'object' is known.

919 |       // object.prototype = ...;

931 |                                           "struct", funName));

934 |           }
935 |         }
936 |       }
937 |

939 |       // and 'property' is declared on it.

942 |           objectJsType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());

947 |           JSType expectedType = type.getPropertyType(pname);

/**
   * Infer the parameter and return types of a function from
   * the parameter and return types of the function it is overriding.
   *
   * @param oldType The function being overridden. Does nothing if this is null.
   * @param paramsParent The LP node of the function that we're assigning to.
   *     If null, that just means we're not initializing this to a function
   *     literal.
   */
Method code:
233 |   FunctionTypeBuilder inferFromOverriddenFunction(
234 |       @Nullable FunctionType oldType, @Nullable Node paramsParent) {
235 |     if (oldType == null) {
236 |       return this;
237 |     }
238 | 
239 |     returnType = oldType.getReturnType();
240 |     returnTypeInferred = oldType.isReturnTypeInferred();
241 |     if (paramsParent == null) {
242 |       // Not a function literal.
243 |       parametersNode = oldType.getParametersNode();
244 |       if (parametersNode == null) {
245 |         parametersNode = new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry).build();
246 |       }

249 |       // to each parameter of the literal.
250 |       FunctionParamBuilder paramBuilder =

253 |       boolean warnedAboutArgList = false;
254 |       boolean oldParamsListHitOptArgs = false;
255 |       for (Node currentParam = paramsParent.getFirstChild();
256 |            currentParam != null; currentParam = currentParam.getNext()) {
257 |         if (oldParams.hasNext()) {

260 |

262 |               oldParam.isVarArgs() ||

264 |

267 |           if (currentParam.getNext() != null && newParam.isVarArgs()) {

270 |           }
271 |         } else {
272 |           warnedAboutArgList |= addParameter(
273 |               paramBuilder,
274 |               typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE),
275 |               warnedAboutArgList,
276 |               codingConvention.isOptionalParameter(currentParam) ||
277 |                   oldParamsListHitOptArgs,
278 |               codingConvention.isVarArgsParameter(currentParam));
279 |         }
280 |       }
281 |

283 |       // but make them optional.
284 |       while (oldParams.hasNext()) {

286 |       }

286 |     @Override
287 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
288 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
289 |       if (refInfo != null) {
290 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
291 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
292 |         String fullName = name.getFullName();
293 |         switch (ref.type) {
294 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
295 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
296 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
297 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
298 |             if (valParent.isAssign() && name.isSimpleName() &&
299 |                 name.getDeclaration() == ref) {
300 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
301 |               // before it's declared
302 |               compiler.report(
303 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
304 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
305 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
306 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
307 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
308 | 
309 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
310 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
311 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
312 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |           default:
316 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
317 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
318 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
319 |               // or it's an error.
320 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
321 |               if (info != null) {
322 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
323 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
324 |               }
325 |             }
326 |             break;
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 | 
330 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
331 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
332 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
333 |         compiler.report(
334 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
335 |       }
336 | 
337 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
338 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
339 |         if (n.isAssign()) {
340 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
341 |           n.removeChild(last);
342 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
343 |         } else {
344 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.isName());
345 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
346 |         }
347 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
348 |       }
349 | 
350 |       if (n.isCall()) {
351 |         if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
352 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
353 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
354 |           //
355 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
356 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
357 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
358 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which
359 |           // are not. But this would be overkill, especially because
360 |           // the intended use of defines is with config_files, where
361 |           // all the defines are at the top of the bundle.
362 |           for (DefineInfo info : assignableDefines.values()) {
363 |             setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
364 |           }

1539 |                 firstChild, sourceName, scope));

1544 |                 n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope));

1547 |         return createOptionalType(

1549 |                 n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope));
1550 | 
1551 |       case Token.STAR: // The AllType
1552 |         return getNativeType(ALL_TYPE);

1571 |         return getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);

1575 |             n.getLineno(), n.getCharno());

1577 |           namedType = namedType.resolveInternal(reporter, scope);
1578 |         }

/**
   * A function is a subtype of another if their call methods are related via
   * subtyping and {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that} with regard to
   * the prototype chain.
   */
Method code:
1005 |   @Override
1006 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
1007 |     if (JSType.isSubtypeHelper(this, that)) {
1008 |       return true;
1009 |     }
1010 | 
1011 |     if (that.isFunctionType()) {
1012 |       FunctionType other = that.toMaybeFunctionType();
1013 |       if (other.isInterface()) {
1014 |         // Any function can be assigned to an interface function.
1015 |         return true;
1016 |       }
1017 |       if (isInterface()) {
1018 |         // An interface function cannot be assigned to anything.
1019 |         return false;
1020 |       }
1021 |

1023 |       // should be contravariant. However, this causes problems because
1024 |       // of the way we enforce overrides. Because function(this:SubFoo)
1025 |       // is not a subtype of function(this:Foo), our override check treats
1026 |       // this as an error. Let's punt on all this for now.
1027 |       // TODO(nicksantos): fix this.
1028 |       boolean treatThisTypesAsCovariant =
1029 |         // An interface 'this'-type is non-restrictive.
1030 |         // In practical terms, if C implements I, and I has a method m,
1031 |         // then any m doesn't necessarily have to C#m's 'this'
1032 |         // type doesn't need to match I.
1033 |         (other.typeOfThis.toObjectType() != null &&
1034 |              other.typeOfThis.toObjectType().getConstructor() != null &&
1035 |              other.typeOfThis.toObjectType().getConstructor().isInterface()) ||
1036 | 
1037 |         // If one of the 'this' types is covariant of the other,
1038 |         // then we'll treat them as covariant (see comment above).
1039 |         other.typeOfThis.isSubtype(this.typeOfThis) ||
1040 |         this.typeOfThis.isSubtype(other.typeOfThis);
1041 |       return treatThisTypesAsCovariant && this.call.isSubtype(other.call);
1042 |     }

552 |     // policies, so never run it when those policies are requested.
553 |     if (options.extractPrototypeMemberDeclarations &&
554 |         (options.propertyRenaming != PropertyRenamingPolicy.HEURISTIC &&
555 |          options.propertyRenaming !=
556 |             PropertyRenamingPolicy.AGGRESSIVE_HEURISTIC)) {
557 |       passes.add(extractPrototypeMemberDeclarations);
558 |     }
559 | 
560 |     if (options.ambiguateProperties &&
561 |         (options.propertyRenaming == PropertyRenamingPolicy.ALL_UNQUOTED)) {
562 |       passes.add(ambiguateProperties);
563 |     }
564 | 
565 |     if (options.propertyRenaming != PropertyRenamingPolicy.OFF) {
566 |       passes.add(renameProperties);
567 |     }
568 | 
569 |     // Reserve global names added to the "windows" object.
570 |     if (options.reserveRawExports) {
571 |       passes.add(gatherRawExports);
572 |     }
573 | 
574 |     // This comes after property renaming because quoted property names must
575 |     // not be renamed.
576 |     if (options.convertToDottedProperties) {
577 |       passes.add(convertToDottedProperties);
578 |     }
579 | 
580 |     // Property renaming must happen before this pass runs since this
581 |     // pass may convert dotted properties into quoted properties.  It
582 |     // is beneficial to run before alias strings, alias keywords and
583 |     // variable renaming.
584 |     if (options.rewriteFunctionExpressions) {
585 |       passes.add(rewriteFunctionExpressions);
586 |     }
587 | 
588 |     // This comes after converting quoted property accesses to dotted property
589 |     // accesses in order to avoid aliasing property names.
590 |     if (!options.aliasableStrings.isEmpty() || options.aliasAllStrings) {
591 |       passes.add(aliasStrings);
592 |     }
593 | 
594 |     if (options.aliasExternals) {
595 |       passes.add(aliasExternals);
596 |     }
597 | 
598 |     if (options.aliasKeywords) {
599 |       passes.add(aliasKeywords);
600 |     }
601 | 
602 |     // Passes after this point can no longer depend on normalized AST
603 |     // assumptions.
604 |     passes.add(markUnnormalized);
605 | 
606 |     if (options.coalesceVariableNames) {
607 |       passes.add(coalesceVariableNames);
608 | 
609 |       // coalesceVariables creates identity assignments and more redundant code
610 |       // that can be removed, rerun the peephole optimizations to clean them
611 |       // up.
612 |       if (options.foldConstants) {
613 |         passes.add(peepholeOptimizations);
614 |       }
615 |     }
616 | 
617 |     if (options.collapseVariableDeclarations) {
618 |       passes.add(exploitAssign);
619 |       passes.add(collapseVariableDeclarations);
620 |     }
621 | 
622 |     // This pass works best after collapseVariableDeclarations.
623 |     passes.add(denormalize);
624 | 
625 |     if (options.instrumentationTemplate != null) {
626 |       passes.add(instrumentFunctions);
627 |     }
628 | 
629 |     if (options.variableRenaming != VariableRenamingPolicy.ALL) {
630 |       // If we're leaving some (or all) variables with their old names,
631 |       // then we need to undo any of the markers we added for distinguishing
632 |       // local variables ("$$1").
633 |       passes.add(invertContextualRenaming);
634 |     }
635 | 
636 |     if (options.variableRenaming != VariableRenamingPolicy.OFF) {
637 |       passes.add(renameVars);
638 |     }
639 | 
640 |     if (options.groupVariableDeclarations) {
641 |       passes.add(groupVariableDeclarations);
642 |     }
643 | 
644 |     // This pass should run after names stop changing.
645 |     if (options.processObjectPropertyString) {
646 |       passes.add(objectPropertyStringPostprocess);
647 |     }
648 | 
649 |     if (options.labelRenaming) {
650 |       passes.add(renameLabels);
651 |     }
652 | 
653 |     if (options.foldConstants) {
654 |       passes.add(latePeepholeOptimizations);
655 |     }
656 | 
657 |     if (options.anonymousFunctionNaming ==
658 |         AnonymousFunctionNamingPolicy.UNMAPPED) {
659 |       passes.add(nameUnmappedAnonymousFunctions);
660 |     }
661 | 
662 |     passes.add(stripSideEffectProtection);
663 | 
664 |     if (options.renamePrefixNamespace != null) {
665 |       if (!GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMESPACE_PATTERN.matcher(
666 |           options.renamePrefixNamespace).matches()) {
667 |         throw new IllegalArgumentException(
668 |             "Illegal character in renamePrefixNamespace name: "
669 |             + options.renamePrefixNamespace);
670 |       }
671 |       passes.add(rescopeGlobalSymbols);
672 |     }
673 | 
674 |     // Safety checks
675 |     passes.add(sanityCheckAst);
676 |     passes.add(sanityCheckVars);
677 | 
678 |     return passes;
679 |   }

104 |               module, dep);
105 |         }
106 |         depth = Math.max(depth, depDepth + 1);
107 |       }
108 | 
109 |       module.setDepth(depth);
110 |       if (depth == modulesByDepth.size()) {
111 |         modulesByDepth.add(new ArrayList<JSModule>());
112 |       }
113 |       modulesByDepth.get(depth).add(module);
114 |     }

/**
   * Expect that the given variable has not been declared with a type.
   *
   * @param sourceName The name of the source file we're in.
   * @param n The node where warnings should point to.
   * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
   * @param var The variable that we're checking.
   * @param variableName The name of the variable.
   * @param newType The type being applied to the variable. Mostly just here
   *     for the benefit of the warning.
   * @return The variable we end up with. Most of the time, this will just
   *     be {@code var}, but in some rare cases we will need to declare
   *     a new var with new source info.
   */
Method code:
516 |   Var expectUndeclaredVariable(String sourceName, CompilerInput input,
517 |       Node n, Node parent, Var var, String variableName, JSType newType) {
518 |     Var newVar = var;
519 |     boolean allowDupe = false;
520 |     if (n.isGetProp() ||
521 |         NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
522 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
523 |       if (info == null) {
524 |         info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
525 |       }
526 |       allowDupe =
527 |           info != null && info.getSuppressions().contains("duplicate");
528 |     }
529 | 
530 |     JSType varType = var.getType();
531 | 
532 |     // Only report duplicate declarations that have types. Other duplicates
533 |     // will be reported by the syntactic scope creator later in the
534 |     // compilation process.
535 |     if (varType != null &&
536 |         varType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) &&
537 |         newType != null &&
538 |         newType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE)) {
539 |       // If there are two typed declarations of the same variable, that
540 |       // is an error and the second declaration is ignored, except in the
541 |       // case of native types. A null input type means that the declaration
542 |       // was made in TypedScopeCreator#createInitialScope and is a
543 |       // native type. We should redeclare it at the new input site.
544 |       if (var.input == null) {
545 |         Scope s = var.getScope();
546 |         s.undeclare(var);
547 |         newVar = s.declare(variableName, n, varType, input, false);
548 | 
549 |         n.setJSType(varType);
550 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
551 |           if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
552 |             n.getFirstChild().setJSType(varType);
553 |           }
554 |         } else {
555 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
556 |           parent.setJSType(varType);
557 |         }
558 |       } else {
559 |         // Always warn about duplicates if the overridden type does not
560 |         // match the original type.
561 |         //
562 |         // If the types match, suppress the warning iff there was a @suppress
563 |         // tag, or if the original declaration was a stub.
564 |         if (!(allowDupe ||
565 |               var.getParentNode().isExprResult()) ||
566 |             !newType.isEquivalentTo(varType)) {
567 |           report(JSError.make(sourceName, n, DUP_VAR_DECLARATION,
568 |               variableName, newType.toString(), var.getInputName(),
569 |               String.valueOf(var.nameNode.getLineno()),
570 |               varType.toString()));
571 |         }
572 |       }
573 |     }
574 |

576 |   }

1026 |         return false;

1031 |       // I create a definitionProvider that understands namespacing.

/**
   * We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
   * very deeply nested operators and run out of stack space, so we
   * just unroll the recursion when possible.
   *
   * We assume nodes are left-recursive.

===== M0638 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInferencePass.inferAllScopes(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInferencePass.java
Original range: 77-107
Documentation:
/** Entry point for type inference when running over part of the tree. */
Method code:
77 |   void inferAllScopes(Node node) {
78 |     // Type analysis happens in two major phases.
79 |     // 1) Finding all the symbols.
80 |     // 2) Propagating all the inferred types.
81 |     //
82 |     // The order of this analysis is non-obvious. In a complete inference
83 |     // system, we may need to backtrack arbitrarily far. But the compile-time
84 |     // costs would be unacceptable.
85 |     //
86 |     // We do one pass where we do typed scope creation for all scopes
87 |     // in pre-order.
88 |     //
89 |     // Then we do a second pass where we do all type inference
90 |     // (type propagation) in pre-order.
91 |     //
92 |     // We use a memoized scope creator so that we never create a scope
93 |     // more than once.
94 |     //
95 |     // This will allow us to handle cases like:
96 |     // var ns = {};
97 |     // (function() { /** JSDoc */ ns.method = function() {}; })();
98 |     // ns.method();
99 |     // In this code, we need to build the symbol table for the inner scope in
100 |     // order to propagate the type of ns.method in the outer scope.
101 |     (new NodeTraversal(
102 |         compiler, new FirstScopeBuildingCallback(), scopeCreator))
103 |         .traverseWithScope(node, topScope);
104 |     (new NodeTraversal(
105 |         compiler, new SecondScopeBuildingCallback(), scopeCreator))
106 |         .traverseWithScope(node, topScope);
107 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:

1950 |   }

   * @return Whether this node is equivalent semantically to the provided node.

1492 |         || this.getClass() != node.getClass()) {
1493 |       return false;
1494 |     }
1495 | 
1496 |     if (compareJsType && !JSType.isEquivalent(jsType, node.getJSType())) {
1497 |       return false;
1498 |     }

1502 |       int post2 = node.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP);
1503 |       if (post1 != post2) {

1505 |       }
1506 |     } else if (type == Token.STRING || type == Token.STRING_KEY) {

1510 |         if (quoted1 != quoted2) {
1511 |           return false;
1512 |         }

1516 |       int slashV2 = node.getIntProp(SLASH_V);
1517 |       if (slashV1 != slashV2) {

1519 |       }
1520 |     } else if (type == Token.CALL) {
1521 |       if (this.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL) != node.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL)) {

1535 |     }
1536 |

/**
     * Creates a new function type, based on the given nodes.
     *
     * This handles two cases that are semantically very different, but
     * are not mutually exclusive:
     * - A function literal that needs a type attached to it.
     * - An assignment expression with function-type info in the JsDoc.
     *
     * All parameters are optional, and we will do the best we can to create
     * a function type.
     *
     * This function will always create a function type, so only call it if
     * you're sure that's what you want.
     *
     * @param rValue The function node.
     * @param name the function's name
     * @param info the {@link JSDocInfo} attached to the function definition
     * @param lvalueNode The node where this function is being
     *     assigned. For example, {@code A.prototype.foo = ...} would be used to
     *     determine that this function is a method of A.prototype. May be
     *     null to indicate that this is not being assigned to a qualified name.
     */
Method code:
853 |     private FunctionType createFunctionTypeFromNodes(
854 |         @Nullable Node rValue,
855 |         @Nullable String name,
856 |         @Nullable JSDocInfo info,
857 |         @Nullable Node lvalueNode) {
858 | 
859 |       FunctionType functionType = null;
860 | 
861 |       // Global ctor aliases should be registered with the type registry.
862 |       if (rValue != null && rValue.isQualifiedName() && scope.isGlobal()) {
863 |         Var var = scope.getVar(rValue.getQualifiedName());
864 |         if (var != null && var.getType() != null &&
865 |             var.getType().isFunctionType()) {
866 |           FunctionType aliasedType  = var.getType().toMaybeFunctionType();
867 |           if ((aliasedType.isConstructor() || aliasedType.isInterface()) &&
868 |               !aliasedType.isNativeObjectType()) {
869 |             functionType = aliasedType;
870 | 
871 |             if (name != null && scope.isGlobal()) {
872 |               typeRegistry.declareType(name, functionType.getInstanceType());
873 |             }
874 |           }
875 |         }
876 |       }
877 | 
878 |       if (functionType == null) {
879 |         Node errorRoot = rValue == null ? lvalueNode : rValue;
880 |         boolean isFnLiteral =
881 |             rValue != null && rValue.isFunction();
882 |         Node fnRoot = isFnLiteral ? rValue : null;
883 |         Node parametersNode = isFnLiteral ?
884 |             rValue.getFirstChild().getNext() : null;
885 |         Node fnBlock = isFnLiteral ? parametersNode.getNext() : null;
886 | 
887 |         if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
888 |           JSType type = info.getType().evaluate(scope, typeRegistry);
889 | 
890 |           // Known to be not null since we have the FUNCTION token there.
891 |           type = type.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
892 |           if (type.isFunctionType()) {
893 |             functionType = type.toMaybeFunctionType();
894 |             functionType.setJSDocInfo(info);
895 |           }
896 |         }
897 | 
898 |         if (functionType == null) {
899 |           // Find the type of any overridden function.
900 |           Node ownerNode = NodeUtil.getBestLValueOwner(lvalueNode);
901 |           String ownerName = NodeUtil.getBestLValueName(ownerNode);
902 |           Var ownerVar = null;

904 |           ObjectType ownerType = null;
905 |           if (ownerName != null) {
906 |             ownerVar = scope.getVar(ownerName);
907 |             if (ownerVar != null) {
908 |               ownerType = ObjectType.cast(ownerVar.getType());
909 |             }
910 |             if (name != null) {
911 |               propName = name.substring(ownerName.length() + 1);
912 |             }
913 |           }

917 |             overriddenType = findOverriddenFunction(ownerType, propName);

922 |                   scope)

924 |               .inferFromOverriddenFunction(overriddenType, parametersNode)
925 |               .inferTemplateTypeName(info)

935 |             searchedForThisType = true;
936 |           } else if (ownerNode != null && ownerNode.isThis()) {
937 |             // If 'this' has a type, use that instead.
938 |             // This is a hack, necessary because CollectProperties (below)
939 |             // doesn't run with the scope that it's building,
940 |             // so scope.getTypeOfThis() will be wrong.

===== M0702 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1129-1309
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1129 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1130 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1131 | 
1132 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1133 |       case Token.NOT:
1134 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1135 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1136 |           case Token.NOT: {
1137 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1138 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1139 |               reportCodeChange();
1140 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1141 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1142 |               return newRoot;
1143 |             }
1144 |           case Token.AND:
1145 |           case Token.OR: {
1146 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1147 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1148 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1149 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1150 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1151 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1152 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1153 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1154 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1155 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1156 |               Node left, right;
1157 | 
1158 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1159 |               // due to the added ()
1160 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1161 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1162 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1163 |                 // If an expression has higher precedence than && or ||,
1164 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1165 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1166 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1167 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1168 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1169 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1170 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1171 |                   return n;
1172 |                 }
1173 |               }
1174 | 
1175 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1176 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1177 |               } else {
1178 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1179 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1180 |               }
1181 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1182 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1183 |               } else {
1184 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1185 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1186 |               }
1187 | 
1188 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1189 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1190 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1191 |               reportCodeChange();
1192 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1193 |               // AND and OR children below.
1194 |               return newRoot;
1195 |             }
1196 | 
1197 |            default:
1198 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1199 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1200 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1201 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1202 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1203 |              }
1204 |         }
1205 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1206 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1207 |         return n;
1208 | 
1209 |       case Token.OR:
1210 |       case Token.AND: {
1211 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1212 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1213 | 
1214 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1215 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1216 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1217 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1218 | 
1219 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1220 |         // Handle four cases:
1221 |         //   x || false --> x
1222 |         //   x || true  --> true
1223 |         //   x && true --> x
1224 |         //   x && false  --> false
1225 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1226 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1227 |           int type = n.getType();
1228 |           Node replacement = null;
1229 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1230 | 
1231 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1232 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1233 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1234 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1235 |             replacement = left;
1236 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1237 |             replacement = right;
1238 |           }
1239 | 
1240 |           if (replacement != null) {
1241 |             n.detachChildren();
1242 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1243 |             reportCodeChange();
1244 |             return replacement;
1245 |           }
1246 |         }
1247 |         return n;
1248 |       }
1249 | 
1250 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1251 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1252 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1253 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1254 | 
1255 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1256 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1257 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1258 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1259 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1260 | 
1261 |         // Handle four cases:
1262 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1263 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1264 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1265 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1266 |         Node replacement = null;
1267 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1268 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1269 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1270 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1271 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1272 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1273 |           replacement = condition;
1274 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1275 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1276 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1277 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1278 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1279 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1280 |           // Remove useless true case.
1281 |           n.detachChildren();
1282 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1283 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1284 |           // Remove useless false case
1285 |           n.detachChildren();
1286 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1287 |         }
1288 | 
1289 |         if (replacement != null) {
1290 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1291 |           n = replacement;
1292 |           reportCodeChange();
1293 |         }
1294 | 
1295 |         return n;
1296 |       }
1297 | 
1298 |       default:
1299 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1300 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1301 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1302 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1303 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1304 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1305 |         }
1306 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1307 |         return n;
1308 |     }
1309 |   }

260 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
261 |         return;

263 |       case Token.HOOK:
264 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
265 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
266 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
267 |         return;
268 | 
269 |       case Token.VAR:
270 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
271 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
272 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
273 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
274 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
275 |           }
276 |         }
277 |         return;
278 | 
279 |       default:
280 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
281 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
282 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
283 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
284 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
285 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
286 |             return;

301 |           escapeParameters(output);

     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name.
     *
     * @param t The traversal

632 |       if (maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(t, n, parent, name)) return;
633 |

635 |       if (parent != null) {
636 |         switch (parent.getType()) {
637 |           case Token.IF:
638 |           case Token.TYPEOF:
639 |           case Token.VOID:
640 |           case Token.NOT:
641 |           case Token.BITNOT:
642 |           case Token.POS:

159 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
160 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
161 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
162 |       case Token.BLOCK:
163 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
164 |       case Token.TRY:
165 |         return true;
166 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
167 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
168 |         // bleeds into the local scope and parameters are assigned
169 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
170 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
171 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
172 |         // control is going into the function's body, represented by the second
173 |         // child.
174 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
175 |       case Token.WHILE:
176 |       case Token.DO:
177 |       case Token.IF:
178 |         // These control structures are represented by a node that holds the
179 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
180 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
181 | 
182 |       case Token.FOR:
183 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structures in that
184 |         // it has an initialization and an increment statement. Those
185 |         // two statements have corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
186 |         // The FOR node only represents the condition check for each iteration.
187 |         // That way the following:
188 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
189 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
190 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
191 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
192 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
193 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |         } else {
195 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
196 |         }
197 |       case Token.SWITCH:
198 |       case Token.CASE:
199 |       case Token.CATCH:
200 |       case Token.WITH:
201 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
202 |       default:
203 |         return false;
204 |     }
205 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.SortedDependencies(List<INPUT>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java
Original range: 64-108
Documentation:

Method code:
64 |   public SortedDependencies(List<INPUT> inputs)
65 |       throws CircularDependencyException {
66 |     this.inputs = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
67 |     noProvides = Lists.newArrayList();
68 | 
69 |     // Collect all symbols provided in these files.
70 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
71 |       Collection<String> currentProvides = input.getProvides();
72 |       if (currentProvides.isEmpty()) {
73 |         noProvides.add(input);
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       for (String provide : currentProvides) {
77 |         provideMap.put(provide, input);
78 |       }
79 |     }
80 | 
81 |     // Get the direct dependencies.
82 |     final Multimap<INPUT, INPUT> deps = HashMultimap.create();
83 |     for (INPUT input : inputs) {
84 |       for (String req : input.getRequires()) {
85 |         INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
86 |         if (dep != null && dep != input) {
87 |           deps.put(input, dep);
88 |         }
89 |       }
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     // Sort the inputs by sucking in 0-in-degree nodes until we're done.
93 |     sortedList = topologicalStableSort(inputs, deps);
94 | 
95 |     // The dependency graph of inputs has a cycle iff sortedList is a proper
96 |     // subset of inputs. Also, it has a cycle iff the subgraph
97 |     // (inputs - sortedList) has a cycle. It's fairly easy to prove this
98 |     // by the lemma that a graph has a cycle iff it has a subgraph where
99 |     // no nodes have out-degree 0. I'll leave the proof of this as an exercise
100 |     // to the reader.
101 |     if (sortedList.size() < inputs.size()) {
102 |       List<INPUT> subGraph = Lists.newArrayList(inputs);
103 |       subGraph.removeAll(sortedList);
104 | 
105 |       throw new CircularDependencyException(
106 |           cycleToString(findCycle(subGraph, deps)));
107 |     }
108 |   }

===== M0759 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal,Node,Node,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 769-807
Documentation:
/**
     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
769 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
770 |         String name) {
771 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
772 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
773 |       // assignments.
774 | 
775 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
776 |       String prefix;
777 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
778 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
779 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
780 |       } else {
781 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
782 |         if (i == -1) {
783 |           return false;
784 |         }
785 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
786 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
787 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
788 |         while (i >= 0) {
789 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
790 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
791 |         }
792 |       }
793 | 
794 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
795 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
796 |         // key, so we're done.
797 |         return true;
798 |       }
799 | 
800 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
801 |         parent = n;
802 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
803 |       }
804 | 
805 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
806 |       return true;
807 |     }

===== M0780 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

/**
   * Determines whether this node is used as an L-value. Notice that sometimes
   * names are used as both L-values and R-values.
   *
   * We treat "var x;" as a pseudo-L-value, which kind of makes sense if you
   * treat it as "assignment to 'undefined' at the top of the scope". But if
   * we're honest with ourselves, it doesn't make sense, and we only do this
   * because it makes sense to treat this as syntactically similar to
   * "var x = 0;".

   * @return True if n is an L-value.
   */

===== M0805 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 124-178
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block, n);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child, n);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }
178 |   }

===== M0816 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.traverseName(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 670-723
Documentation:

Method code:
670 |   private FlowScope traverseName(Node n, FlowScope scope) {
671 |     String varName = n.getString();
672 |     Node value = n.getFirstChild();
673 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
674 |     if (value != null) {
675 |       scope = traverse(value, scope);
676 |       updateScopeForTypeChange(scope, n, n.getJSType() /* could be null */,
677 |           getJSType(value));
678 |       return scope;
679 |     } else {
680 |       StaticSlot<JSType> var = scope.getSlot(varName);
681 |       if (var != null) {
682 |         // There are two situations where we don't want to use type information
683 |         // from the scope, even if we have it.
684 | 
685 |         // 1) The var is escaped and assigned in an inner scope, e.g.,
686 |         // function f() { var x = 3; function g() { x = null } (x); }
687 |         boolean isInferred = var.isTypeInferred();
688 |         boolean unflowable = isInferred &&
689 |             isUnflowable(syntacticScope.getVar(varName));
690 | 
691 |         // 2) We're reading type information from another scope for an
692 |         // inferred variable. That variable is assigned more than once,
693 |         // and we can't know which type we're getting.
694 |         //
695 |         // var t = null; function f() { (t); } doStuff(); t = {};
696 |         //
697 |         // Notice that this heuristic isn't perfect. For example, you might
698 |         // have:
699 |         //
700 |         // function f() { (t); } f(); var t = 3;
701 |         //
702 |         // In this case, we would infer the first reference to t as
703 |         // type {number}, even though it's undefined.
704 |         boolean nonLocalInferredSlot = false;
705 |         if (isInferred && syntacticScope.isLocal()) {
706 |           Var maybeOuterVar = syntacticScope.getParent().getVar(varName);
707 |           if (var == maybeOuterVar &&
708 |               !maybeOuterVar.isMarkedAssignedExactlyOnce()) {
709 |             nonLocalInferredSlot = true;
710 |           }
711 |         }
712 | 
713 |         if (!unflowable && !nonLocalInferredSlot) {

/**
   * Gets the value of a node as a String, or null if it cannot be converted.
   * When it returns a non-null String, this method effectively emulates the
   * <code>String()</code> JavaScript cast function.
   */
Method code:
176 |   static String getStringValue(Node n) {
177 |     // TODO(user): regex literals as well.
178 |     switch (n.getType()) {
179 |       case Token.STRING:
180 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
181 |         return n.getString();

204 |       case Token.VOID:

===== M0841 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.canInline(Reference,Reference,Reference)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 519-583
Documentation:
/**
     * @return true if the provided reference and declaration can be safely
     *         inlined according to our criteria
     */
Method code:
519 |     private boolean canInline(
520 |         Reference declaration,
521 |         Reference initialization,
522 |         Reference reference) {
523 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(declaration)
524 |           || !isValidInitialization(initialization)
525 |           || !isValidReference(reference)) {
526 |         return false;
527 |       }
528 | 
529 |       // If the value is read more than once, skip it.
530 |       // VAR declarations and EXPR_RESULT don't need the value, but other
531 |       // ASSIGN expressions parents do.
532 |       if (declaration != initialization &&
533 |           !initialization.getGrandparent().isExprResult()) {
534 |         return false;
535 |       }
536 | 
537 |       // Be very conservative and do no cross control structures or
538 |       // scope boundaries
539 |       if (declaration.getBasicBlock() != initialization.getBasicBlock()
540 |           || declaration.getBasicBlock() != reference.getBasicBlock()) {
541 |         return false;
542 |       }
543 | 
544 |       // Do not inline into a call node. This would change
545 |       // the context in which it was being called. For example,
546 |       //   var a = b.c;
547 |       //   a();
548 |       // should not be inlined, because it calls a in the context of b
549 |       // rather than the context of the window.
550 |       //   var a = b.c;
551 |       //   f(a)
552 |       // is OK.
553 |       Node value = initialization.getAssignedValue();
554 |       Preconditions.checkState(value != null);
555 |       if (value.isGetProp()
556 |           && reference.getParent().isCall()
557 |           && reference.getParent().getFirstChild() == reference.getNode()) {
558 |         return false;
559 |       }
560 | 
561 |       if (value.isFunction()) {
562 |         Node callNode = reference.getParent();
563 |         if (reference.getParent().isCall()) {
564 |           CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
565 |           // Bug 2388531: Don't inline subclass definitions into class defining
566 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
567 |           SubclassRelationship relationship =
568 |               convention.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
569 |           if (relationship != null) {
570 |             return false;
571 |           }
572 | 
573 |           // issue 668: Don't inline singleton getter methods
574 |           // calls as this confused class removing logic.
575 |           if (convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(callNode) != null) {
576 |             return false;
577 |           }
578 |         }
579 |       }
580 | 
581 |       return canMoveAggressively(value) ||
582 |           canMoveModerately(initialization, reference);
583 |     }

===== M0842 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSModuleGraph.manageDependencies(DependencyOptions,List<CompilerInput>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/JSModuleGraph.java
Original range: 354-433
Documentation:
/**
   * Apply the dependency options to the list of sources, returning a new
   * source list re-ordering and dropping files as necessary.
   * This module graph will be updated to reflect the new list.
   *
   * @param inputs The original list of sources. Used to ensure that the sort
   *     is stable.
   * @throws CircularDependencyException if there is a circular dependency
   *     between the provides and requires.
   * @throws MissingProvideException if an entry point was not provided
   *     by any of the inputs.
   * @see DependencyOptions for more info on how this works.
   */
Method code:
354 |   public List<CompilerInput> manageDependencies(
355 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
356 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs)
357 |       throws CircularDependencyException, MissingProvideException {
358 | 
359 |     SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter =
360 |         new SortedDependencies<CompilerInput>(inputs);
361 |     Set<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
362 |     if (depOptions.shouldPruneDependencies()) {
363 |       if (!depOptions.shouldDropMoochers()) {
364 |         entryPointInputs.addAll(sorter.getInputsWithoutProvides());
365 |       }
366 | 
367 |       for (String entryPoint : depOptions.getEntryPoints()) {
368 |         entryPointInputs.add(sorter.getInputProviding(entryPoint));
369 |       }
370 | 
371 |       CompilerInput baseJs = sorter.maybeGetInputProviding("goog");
372 |       if (baseJs != null) {
373 |         entryPointInputs.add(baseJs);
374 |       }
375 |     } else {
376 |       entryPointInputs.addAll(inputs);
377 |     }
378 | 
379 |     // The order of inputs, sorted independently of modules.
380 |     List<CompilerInput> absoluteOrder =
381 |         sorter.getDependenciesOf(inputs, depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
382 | 
383 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module.
384 |     ListMultimap<JSModule, CompilerInput> entryPointInputsPerModule =
385 |         LinkedListMultimap.create();
386 |     for (CompilerInput input : entryPointInputs) {
387 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
388 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(module);
389 |       entryPointInputsPerModule.put(module, input);
390 |     }
391 | 
392 |     // Clear the modules of their inputs. This also nulls out
393 |     // the input's reference to its module.
394 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
395 |       module.removeAll();
396 |     }
397 | 
398 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module, or in one
399 |     // of that module's dependencies.
400 |     for (JSModule module : entryPointInputsPerModule.keySet()) {
401 |       List<CompilerInput> transitiveClosure =
402 |           sorter.getDependenciesOf(
403 |               entryPointInputsPerModule.get(module),
404 |               depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
405 |       for (CompilerInput input : transitiveClosure) {
406 |         JSModule oldModule = input.getModule();
407 |         if (oldModule == null) {
408 |           input.setModule(module);
409 |         } else {
410 |           input.setModule(null);
411 |           input.setModule(
412 |               getDeepestCommonDependencyInclusive(oldModule, module));
413 |         }
414 |       }
415 |     }
416 | 
417 |     // All the inputs are pointing to the modules that own them. Yeah!
418 |     // Update the modules to reflect this.
419 |     for (CompilerInput input : absoluteOrder) {
420 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
421 |       if (module != null) {
422 |         module.add(input);
423 |       }
424 |     }
425 | 
426 |     // Now, generate the sorted result.
427 |     List<CompilerInput> result = Lists.newArrayList();
428 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
429 |       result.addAll(module.getInputs());
430 |     }
431 | 
432 |     return result;
433 |   }

/**
   * Returns the index within the scope stack.
   * e.g. function Foo(a) { var b; function c(d) { } }
   * a = 0, b = 1, c = 2, d = 3

936 |     static Assign maybeCreateAssign(Node assignNode) {
937 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(assignNode));
938 | 
939 |       // Skip one level of GETPROPs or GETELEMs.
940 |       //

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Original range: 83-131

Method code:
83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
86 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.
89 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||
90 |         n.isComma()) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (parent == null) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     // Do not try to remove a block or an expr result. We already handle
99 |     // these cases when we visit the child, and the peephole passes will
100 |     // fix up the tree in more clever ways when these are removed.
101 |     if (n.isExprResult() || n.isBlock()) {
102 |       return;
103 |     }
104 | 
105 |     // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
106 |     // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
107 |     if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
108 |       return;
109 |     }
110 | 
111 |     boolean isResultUsed = NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(n);
112 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperator(n);
113 |     if (!isResultUsed &&
114 |         (isSimpleOp || !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler()))) {
115 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
116 |       if (n.isString()) {
117 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
118 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
119 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Token.name(n.getType()).toLowerCase() +
120 |             "' operator is not being used.";
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       t.getCompiler().report(
124 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
125 |       // TODO(johnlenz): determine if it is necessary to
126 |       // try to protect side-effect free statements as well.
127 |       if (!NodeUtil.isStatement(n)) {
128 |         problemNodes.add(n);
129 |       }
130 |     }
131 |   }

===== M0932 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseVariableDeclarations.applyCollapses()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseVariableDeclarations.java
Original range: 213-249
Documentation:

Method code:
213 |   private void applyCollapses() {
214 |     for (Collapse collapse : collapses) {
215 | 
216 |       Node var = new Node(Token.VAR);
217 |       var.copyInformationFrom(collapse.startNode);
218 |       collapse.parent.addChildBefore(var, collapse.startNode);
219 | 
220 |       boolean redeclaration = false;
221 |       for (Node n = collapse.startNode; n != collapse.endNode;) {
222 |         Node next = n.getNext();
223 | 
224 |         Preconditions.checkState(var.getNext() == n);
225 |         collapse.parent.removeChildAfter(var);
226 | 
227 |         if (n.isVar()) {
228 |           while(n.hasChildren()) {
229 |             var.addChildToBack(n.removeFirstChild());
230 |           }
231 |         } else {
232 |           Node assign = n.getFirstChild();
233 |           Node lhs = assign.getFirstChild();
234 |           Preconditions.checkState(lhs.isName());
235 |           Node rhs = assign.getLastChild();
236 |           lhs.addChildToBack(rhs.detachFromParent());
237 |           var.addChildToBack(lhs.detachFromParent());
238 |           redeclaration = true;
239 |         }
240 |         n = next;
241 |       }
242 | 
243 |       if (redeclaration) {
244 |         JSDocInfo info = new JSDocInfo();
245 |         info.addSuppression("duplicate");
246 |         var.setJSDocInfo(info);
247 |       }
248 |     }
