===== M0964 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.ON_EX, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

/**
   * Visits a NAME node.

Method code:
1344 |   boolean visitName(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
1345 |     // At this stage, we need to determine whether this is a leaf
1346 |     // node in an expression (which therefore needs to have a type

1348 |     // can safely ignore.  Function names, arguments (children of LP nodes) and

===== M0983 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 192-305
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
192 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
193 |     int type = n.getType();
194 |     Var var = null;
195 |     switch (type) {
196 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
197 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
198 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
199 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
200 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
201 |         }
202 | 
203 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
204 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
205 |         } else {
206 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
207 |         }
208 |         return;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
211 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
212 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
213 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
214 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
215 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
216 |           if (var != null) {
217 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
218 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
219 | 
220 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
221 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
222 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
223 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
224 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
225 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
226 |               return;
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         break;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.CALL:
233 |         Var modifiedVar = null;
234 | 
235 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
236 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
237 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
238 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
239 |           modifiedVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
240 |         } else {
241 |           // Look for calls to addSingletonGetter calls.
242 |           String className = codingConvention.getSingletonGetterClassName(n);
243 |           if (className != null) {
244 |             modifiedVar = scope.getVar(className);
245 |           }
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
249 |         // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
250 |         // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
251 |         // easier and mostly the same.
252 |         if (modifiedVar != null && modifiedVar.isGlobal()
253 |             && !referenced.contains(modifiedVar)) {
254 |           // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
255 |           classDefiningCalls.put(modifiedVar, parent);
256 |           continuations.put(modifiedVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
257 |           return;
258 |         }
259 |         break;
260 | 
261 |       case Token.NAME:
262 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
263 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
264 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
265 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
266 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value, compiler)) {
267 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
268 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
269 |             // of traversing immediately.
270 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
271 |             return;
272 |           }
273 |         } else {
274 | 
275 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
276 |           // on all the parameters.
277 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
278 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
279 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
280 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
281 |             }
282 |           }
283 | 
284 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
285 |           // are references to other vars.
286 |           if (var != null) {
287 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
288 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
289 |             // for now.
290 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
291 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
292 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
293 |               }
294 |             } else {
295 |               markReferencedVar(var);
296 |             }
297 |           }
298 |         }
299 |         break;
300 |     }
301 | 
302 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
303 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
304 |     }
305 |   }

   * Creates a scope with all types declared. Declares newly discovered types

198 |   public Scope createScope(Node root, Scope parent) {

200 |     // inner scopes, because only global scopes can contain named classes that

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType,Node)

Documentation:

Method code:
396 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
397 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
398 |     // two cases:
399 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
400 |     // and
401 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
402 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
403 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
404 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
405 |     //
406 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
407 |     //
408 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
409 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
410 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
411 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
412 |     //
413 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
414 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
415 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
416 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
417 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
418 |           registry, getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
419 |     }
420 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);
421 |   }

===== M1019 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.ensurePropertyDefined(Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 580-628
Documentation:
/**
   * Defines a property if the property has not been defined yet.
   */
Method code:
580 |   private void ensurePropertyDefined(Node getprop, JSType rightType) {
581 |     String propName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
582 |     Node obj = getprop.getFirstChild();
583 |     JSType nodeType = getJSType(obj);
584 |     ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(
585 |         nodeType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
586 |     if (objectType == null) {
587 |       registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, nodeType);
588 |     } else {
589 |       // Don't add the property to @struct objects outside a constructor
590 |       if (nodeType.isStruct() && !objectType.hasProperty(propName)) {
591 |         if (!(obj.isThis() &&
592 |               getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor())) {
593 |           return;
594 |         }
595 |       }
596 | 
597 |       if (ensurePropertyDeclaredHelper(getprop, objectType)) {
598 |         return;
599 |       }
600 | 
601 |       if (!objectType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propName)) {
602 |         // We do not want a "stray" assign to define an inferred property
603 |         // for every object of this type in the program. So we use a heuristic
604 |         // approach to determine whether to infer the property.
605 |         //
606 |         // 1) If the property is already defined, join it with the previously
607 |         //    inferred type.
608 |         // 2) If this isn't an instance object, define it.
609 |         // 3) If the property of an object is being assigned in the constructor,
610 |         //    define it.
611 |         // 4) If this is a stub, define it.
612 |         // 5) Otherwise, do not define the type, but declare it in the registry
613 |         //    so that we can use it for missing property checks.
614 |         if (objectType.hasProperty(propName) || !objectType.isInstanceType()) {
615 |           if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
616 |             objectType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
617 |           } else {
618 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
619 |           }
620 |         } else if (obj.isThis() &&
621 |                    getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor()) {
622 |           objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
623 |         } else {
624 |           registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, objectType);
625 |         }
626 |       }
627 |     }
628 |   }

204 |       FlowState<MustDef> state = graphNode.getAnnotation();
205 |       final MustDef defs = state.getIn();
206 |       final Node cfgNode = n;
207 |       AbstractCfgNodeTraversalCallback gatherCb =
208 |           new AbstractCfgNodeTraversalCallback() {
209 | 
210 |         @Override
211 |         public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
212 |           if (n.isName()) {
213 | 
214 |             // n.getParent() isn't null. This just the case where n is the root
215 |             // node that gatherCb started at.
216 |             if (parent == null) {
217 |               return;
218 |             }
219 | 
220 |             // Make sure that the name node is purely a read.
221 |             if ((NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) && parent.getFirstChild() == n)
222 |                 || parent.isVar() || parent.isInc() || parent.isDec() ||
223 |                 parent.isParamList() || parent.isCatch()) {
224 |               return;
225 |             }
226 | 
227 |             String name = n.getString();
228 |             if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(name)) {
229 |               return;
230 |             }
231 | 
232 |             Definition def = reachingDef.getDef(name, cfgNode);
233 |             // TODO(nicksantos): We need to add some notion of @const outer
234 |             // scope vars. We can inline those just fine.
235 |             if (def != null &&
236 |                 !reachingDef.dependsOnOuterScopeVars(def)) {
237 |               candidates.add(new Candidate(name, def, n, cfgNode));
238 |             }
239 |           }
240 |         }
241 |       };
242 | 
243 |       NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, cfgNode, gatherCb);
244 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeReplaceKnownMethods.tryFoldArrayJoin(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeReplaceKnownMethods.java
Original range: 393-507
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
393 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {
394 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
395 | 
396 |     if (callTarget == null || !callTarget.isGetProp()) {
397 |       return n;
398 |     }
399 | 
400 |     Node right = callTarget.getNext();
401 |     if (right != null) {
402 |       if (right.getNext() != null || !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
403 |         return n;
404 |       }
405 |     }
406 | 
407 |     Node arrayNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
408 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
409 | 
410 |     if (!arrayNode.isArrayLit() ||
411 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
412 |       return n;
413 |     }
414 | 
415 |     if (right != null && right.isString()
416 |         && ",".equals(right.getString())) {
417 |       // "," is the default, it doesn't need to be explicit
418 |       n.removeChild(right);
419 |       reportCodeChange();
420 |     }
421 | 
422 |     String joinString = (right == null) ? "," : NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
423 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
424 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
425 |     int foldedSize = 0;
426 |     Node prev = null;
427 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
428 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
429 |     while (elem != null) {
430 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem) || elem.isEmpty()) {
431 |         if (sb == null) {
432 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
433 |         } else {
434 |           sb.append(joinString);
435 |         }
436 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getArrayElementStringValue(elem));
437 |       } else {
438 |         if (sb != null) {
439 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
440 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
441 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
442 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
443 |               IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
444 |           sb = null;
445 |         }
446 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
447 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
448 |       }
449 |       prev = elem;
450 |       elem = elem.getNext();
451 |     }
452 | 
453 |     if (sb != null) {
454 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
455 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
456 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
457 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
458 |           IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
459 |     }
460 |     // one for each comma.
461 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
462 | 
463 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
464 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
465 |       case 0:
466 |         Node emptyStringNode = IR.string("");
467 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
468 |         reportCodeChange();
469 |         return emptyStringNode;
470 |       case 1:
471 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
472 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
473 |           return n;
474 |         }
475 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
476 |         if (!foldedStringNode.isString()) {
477 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
478 |           // it is coerced to a string.
479 |           Node replacement = IR.add(
480 |               IR.string("").srcref(n),
481 |               foldedStringNode);
482 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
483 |         }
484 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
485 |         reportCodeChange();
486 |         return foldedStringNode;
487 |       default:
488 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
489 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
490 |           return n;
491 |         }
492 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
493 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
494 |         foldedSize += (right != null) ? InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right) : 0;
495 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
496 |           return n;
497 |         }
498 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
499 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
500 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
501 |         }
502 |         reportCodeChange();
503 |         break;
504 |     }
505 | 
506 |     return n;
507 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(NodeTraversal,ControlFlowGraph<Node>,Set<Var>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 212-305
Documentation:

Method code:
212 |   private UndiGraph<Var, Void> computeVariableNamesInterferenceGraph(
213 |       NodeTraversal t, ControlFlowGraph<Node> cfg, Set<Var> escaped) {
214 |     UndiGraph<Var, Void> interferenceGraph =
215 |         LinkedUndirectedGraph.create();
216 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
217 | 
218 |     // First create a node for each non-escaped variable.
219 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = scope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
220 |       Var v = i.next();
221 |       if (!escaped.contains(v)) {
222 | 
223 |         // TODO(user): In theory, we CAN coalesce function names just like
224 |         // any variables. Our Liveness analysis captures this just like it as
225 |         // described in the specification. However, we saw some zipped and
226 |         // and unzipped size increase after this. We are not totally sure why
227 |         // that is but, for now, we will respect the dead functions and not play
228 |         // around with it.
229 |         if (!v.getParentNode().isFunction()) {
230 |           interferenceGraph.createNode(v);
231 |         }
232 |       }
233 |     }
234 | 
235 |     // Go through each variable and try to connect them.
236 |     for (Iterator<Var> i1 = scope.getVars(); i1.hasNext();) {
237 |       Var v1 = i1.next();
238 | 
239 |       NEXT_VAR_PAIR:
240 |       for (Iterator<Var> i2 = scope.getVars(); i2.hasNext();) {
241 |         Var v2 = i2.next();
242 | 
243 |         // Skip duplicate pairs.
244 |         if (v1.index >= v2.index) {
245 |           continue;
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         if (!interferenceGraph.hasNode(v1) ||
249 |             !interferenceGraph.hasNode(v2)) {
250 |           // Skip nodes that were not added. They are globals and escaped
251 |           // locals. Also avoid merging a variable with itself.
252 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
253 |         }
254 | 
255 |         if (v1.getParentNode().isParamList() &&
256 |             v2.getParentNode().isParamList()) {
257 |           interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
258 |           continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
259 |         }
260 | 
261 |         // Go through every CFG node in the program and look at
262 |         // this variable pair. If they are both live at the same
263 |         // time, add an edge between them and continue to the next pair.
264 |         NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE:
265 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
266 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
267 |             continue NEXT_CROSS_CFG_NODE;
268 |           }
269 | 
270 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
271 |           // Check the live states and add edge when possible.
272 |           if ((state.getIn().isLive(v1) && state.getIn().isLive(v2)) ||
273 |               (state.getOut().isLive(v1) && state.getOut().isLive(v2))) {
274 |             interferenceGraph.connectIfNotFound(v1, null, v2);
275 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
276 |           }
277 |         }
278 | 
279 |         // v1 and v2 might not have an edge between them! woohoo. there's
280 |         // one last sanity check that we have to do: we have to check
281 |         // if there's a collision *within* the cfg node.
282 |         NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE:
283 |         for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> cfgNode : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
284 |           if (cfg.isImplicitReturn(cfgNode)) {
285 |             continue NEXT_INTRA_CFG_NODE;
286 |           }
287 | 
288 |           FlowState<LiveVariableLattice> state = cfgNode.getAnnotation();
289 |           boolean v1OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v1);
290 |           boolean v2OutLive = state.getOut().isLive(v2);
291 |           CombinedLiveRangeChecker checker = new CombinedLiveRangeChecker(
292 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v1, v2OutLive ? null : v2),
293 |               new LiveRangeChecker(v2, v1OutLive ? null : v1));
294 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(
295 |               compiler,
296 |               cfgNode.getValue(),
297 |               checker);
298 |           if (checker.connectIfCrossed(interferenceGraph)) {
299 |             continue NEXT_VAR_PAIR;
300 |           }
301 |         }
302 |       }
303 |     }
304 |     return interferenceGraph;
305 |   }

===== M1107 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // OK, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some JavaScript parsers (such
101 |       // as the PlayStation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 120-203

Method code:
120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

1206 |     private void finishConstructorDefinition(
1207 |         Node n, String variableName, FunctionType fnType,
1208 |         Scope scopeToDeclareIn, CompilerInput input, Var newVar) {
1209 |       // Declare var.prototype in the scope chain.
1210 |       FunctionType superClassCtor = fnType.getSuperClassConstructor();
1211 |       Property prototypeSlot = fnType.getSlot("prototype");
1212 | 
1213 |       // When we declare the function prototype implicitly, we
1214 |       // want to make sure that the function and its prototype
1215 |       // are declared at the same node. We also want to make sure
1216 |       // that the if a symbol has both a Var and a JSType, they have
1217 |       // the same node.
1218 |       //
1219 |       // This consistency is helpful to users of SymbolTable,
1220 |       // because everything gets declared at the same place.
1221 |       prototypeSlot.setNode(n);
1222 | 
1223 |       String prototypeName = variableName + ".prototype";
1224 | 
1225 |       // There are some rare cases where the prototype will already
1226 |       // be declared. See TypedScopeCreatorTest#testBogusPrototypeInit.
1227 |       // Fortunately, other warnings will complain if this happens.
1228 |       Var prototypeVar = scopeToDeclareIn.getVar(prototypeName);
1229 |       if (prototypeVar != null && prototypeVar.scope == scopeToDeclareIn) {
1230 |         scopeToDeclareIn.undeclare(prototypeVar);
1231 |       }
1232 | 
1233 |       scopeToDeclareIn.declare(prototypeName,
1234 |           n, prototypeSlot.getType(), input,
1235 |           /* declared iff there's an explicit supertype */
1236 |           superClassCtor == null ||
1237 |           superClassCtor.getInstanceType().isEquivalentTo(
1238 |               getNativeType(OBJECT_TYPE)));
1239 | 
1240 |       // Make sure the variable is initialized to something if
1241 |       // it constructs itself.
1242 |       if (newVar.getInitialValue() == null &&
1243 |           !n.isFromExterns()) {
1244 |         compiler.report(
1245 |             JSError.make(sourceName, n,
1246 |                 fnType.isConstructor() ?
1247 |                 CTOR_INITIALIZER : IFACE_INITIALIZER,
1248 |                 variableName));
1249 |       }

254 |     private void inlineNonConstants(
255 |         Var v, ReferenceCollection referenceInfo,
256 |         boolean maybeModifiedArguments) {
257 |       int refCount = referenceInfo.references.size();
258 |       Reference declaration = referenceInfo.references.get(0);
259 |       Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReference();
260 |       int firstRefAfterInit = (declaration == init) ? 2 : 3;
261 | 
262 |       if (refCount > 1 &&
263 |           isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(v, referenceInfo)) {
264 |         // if the variable is referenced more than once, we can only
265 |         // inline it if it's immutable and never defined before referenced.
266 |         Node value;
267 |         if (init != null) {
268 |           value = init.getAssignedValue();
269 |         } else {
270 |           // Create a new node for variable that is never initialized.
271 |           Node srcLocation = declaration.getNode();
272 |           value = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(srcLocation);
273 |         }
274 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
275 |         inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
276 |         staleVars.add(v);
277 |       } else if (refCount == firstRefAfterInit) {
278 |         // The variable likely only read once, try some more
279 |         // complex inlining heuristics.
280 |         Reference reference = referenceInfo.references.get(
281 |             firstRefAfterInit - 1);
282 |         if (canInline(declaration, init, reference)) {
283 |           inline(v, declaration, init, reference);
284 |           staleVars.add(v);
285 |         }
286 |       } else if (declaration != init && refCount == 2) {
287 |         if (isValidDeclaration(declaration) && isValidInitialization(init)) {
288 |           // The only reference is the initialization, remove the assignment and
289 |           // the variable declaration.
290 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
291 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
292 |           inlineWellDefinedVariable(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
293 |           staleVars.add(v);
294 |         }
295 |       }
296 | 
297 |       // If this variable was not inlined normally, check if we can
298 |       // inline an alias of it. (If the variable was inlined, then the
299 |       // reference data is out of sync. We're better off just waiting for
300 |       // the next pass.)
301 |       if (!maybeModifiedArguments &&
302 |           !staleVars.contains(v) && referenceInfo.isWellDefined() &&
303 |           referenceInfo.isAssignedOnceInLifetime()) {
304 |         List<Reference> refs = referenceInfo.references;
305 |         for (int i = 1 /* start from a read */; i < refs.size(); i++) {
306 |           Node nameNode = refs.get(i).getNode();
307 |           if (aliasCandidates.containsKey(nameNode)) {
308 |             AliasCandidate candidate = aliasCandidates.get(nameNode);
309 |             if (!staleVars.contains(candidate.alias) &&
310 |                 !isVarInlineForbidden(candidate.alias)) {
311 |               Reference aliasInit;
312 |               aliasInit = candidate.refInfo.getInitializingReference();
313 |               Node value = aliasInit.getAssignedValue();
314 |               Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
315 |               inlineWellDefinedVariable(candidate.alias,
316 |                   value,
317 |                   candidate.refInfo.references);
318 |               staleVars.add(candidate.alias);
319 |             }
320 |           }
321 |         }
322 |       }
323 |     }

/**
   * Emit a warning if we can prove that a property cannot possibly be
   * defined on an object. Note the difference between JS and a strictly
   * statically typed language: we're checking if the property
   * *cannot be defined*, whereas a java compiler would check if the
   * property *can be undefined*.
   */
Method code:
1408 |   private void checkPropertyAccess(JSType childType, String propName,
1409 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
1410 |     // If the property type is unknown, check the object type to see if it
1411 |     // can ever be defined. We explicitly exclude CHECKED_UNKNOWN (for
1412 |     // properties where we've checked that it exists, or for properties on
1413 |     // objects that aren't in this binary).
1414 |     JSType propType = getJSType(n);
1415 |     if (propType.isEquivalentTo(typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE))) {
1416 |       childType = childType.autobox();
1417 |       ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(childType);
1418 |       if (objectType != null) {
1419 |         // We special-case object types so that checks on enums can be
1420 |         // much stricter, and so that we can use hasProperty (which is much
1421 |         // faster in most cases).
1422 |         if (!objectType.hasProperty(propName) ||
1423 |             objectType.isEquivalentTo(
1424 |                 typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE))) {
1425 |           if (objectType instanceof EnumType) {
1426 |             report(t, n, INEXISTENT_ENUM_ELEMENT, propName);
1427 |           } else {
1428 |             checkPropertyAccessHelper(objectType, propName, t, n);
1429 |           }
1430 |         }
1431 | 
1432 |       } else {
1433 |         checkPropertyAccessHelper(childType, propName, t, n);
1434 |       }
1435 |     }
1436 |   }

112 |           // NOTE: "enterScope" is called after we need to pick up this name.
113 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldUnaryOperator(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 338-428
Documentation:

Method code:
338 |   private Node tryFoldUnaryOperator(Node n) {
339 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
340 | 
341 |     Node left = n.getFirstChild();
342 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
343 | 
344 |     if (left == null) {
345 |       return n;
346 |     }
347 | 
348 |     TernaryValue leftVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(left);
349 |     if (leftVal == TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
350 |       return n;
351 |     }
352 | 
353 |     switch (n.getType()) {
354 |       case Token.NOT:
355 |         // Don't fold !0 and !1 back to false.
356 |         if (late && left.isNumber()) {
357 |           double numValue = left.getDouble();
358 |           if (numValue == 0 || numValue == 1) {
359 |             return n;
360 |           }
361 |         }
362 |         Node replacementNode = NodeUtil.booleanNode(!leftVal.toBoolean(true));
363 |         parent.replaceChild(n, replacementNode);
364 |         reportCodeChange();
365 |         return replacementNode;
366 |       case Token.POS:
367 |         if (NodeUtil.isNumericResult(left)) {
368 |           // POS does nothing to numeric values.
369 |           parent.replaceChild(n, left.detachFromParent());
370 |           reportCodeChange();
371 |           return left;
372 |         }
373 |         return n;
374 |       case Token.NEG:
375 |         if (left.isName()) {
376 |           if (left.getString().equals("Infinity")) {
377 |             // "-Infinity" is valid and a literal, don't modify it.
378 |             return n;
379 |           } else if (left.getString().equals("NaN")) {
380 |             // "-NaN" is "NaN".
381 |             n.removeChild(left);
382 |             parent.replaceChild(n, left);
383 |             reportCodeChange();
384 |             return left;
385 |           }
386 |         }
387 | 
388 |         if (left.isNumber()) {
389 |           double negNum = -left.getDouble();
390 | 
391 |           Node negNumNode = IR.number(negNum);
392 |           parent.replaceChild(n, negNumNode);
393 |           reportCodeChange();
394 |           return negNumNode;
395 |         } else {
396 |           // left is not a number node, so do not replace, but warn the
397 |           // user because they can't be doing anything good
398 |           report(NEGATING_A_NON_NUMBER_ERROR, left);
399 |           return n;
400 |         }
401 |       case Token.BITNOT:
402 |         try {
403 |           double val = left.getDouble();
404 |           if (val >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && val <= Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
405 |             int intVal = (int) val;
406 |             if (intVal == val) {
407 |               Node notIntValNode = IR.number(~intVal);
408 |               parent.replaceChild(n, notIntValNode);
409 |               reportCodeChange();
410 |               return notIntValNode;
411 |             } else {
412 |               report(FRACTIONAL_BITWISE_OPERAND, left);
413 |               return n;
414 |             }
415 |           } else {
416 |             report(BITWISE_OPERAND_OUT_OF_RANGE, left);
417 |             return n;
418 |           }
419 |         } catch (UnsupportedOperationException ex) {
420 |           // left is not a number node, so do not replace, but warn the
421 |           // user because they can't be doing anything good
422 |           report(NEGATING_A_NON_NUMBER_ERROR, left);
423 |           return n;
424 |         }
425 |         default:
426 |           return n;
427 |     }
428 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.StatementFusion.fuseIntoOneStatement(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 85-119
Documentation:

Method code:
85 |   private void fuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
86 |     Node cur = block.removeFirstChild();
87 | 
88 |     // Starts building a tree.
89 |     Node commaTree = cur.removeFirstChild();
90 | 
91 | 
92 |     while (block.hasMoreThanOneChild()) {
93 |       Node next = block.removeFirstChild().removeFirstChild();
94 |       commaTree = fuseExpressionIntoExpression(commaTree, next);
95 |     }
96 | 
97 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.hasOneChild());
98 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
99 | 
100 |     // Now we are just left with two statements. The comma tree of the first
101 |     // n - 1 statements (which can be used in an expression) and the last
102 |     // statement. We perform specific fusion based on the last statement's type.
103 |     switch(last.getType()) {
104 |       case Token.IF:
105 |       case Token.RETURN:
106 |       case Token.THROW:
107 |       case Token.SWITCH:
108 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
109 |         fuseExpresssonIntoFirstChild(commaTree, last);
110 |         return;
111 |       case Token.FOR:
112 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(last)) {
113 |           fuseExpresssonIntoSecondChild(commaTree, last);
114 |         }
115 |         return ;
116 |       default:
117 |         throw new IllegalStateException("Statement fusion missing.");
118 |     }
119 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2924-2990
Documentation:
/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2924 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2925 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2926 |       case Token.CAST:
2927 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2928 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2929 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2930 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2931 |         // value is immutable.
2932 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2933 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2934 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2935 |       case Token.COMMA:
2936 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2937 |       case Token.AND:
2938 |       case Token.OR:
2939 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2940 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2941 |       case Token.HOOK:
2942 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2943 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2944 |       case Token.INC:
2945 |       case Token.DEC:
2946 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2947 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2948 |         } else {
2949 |           return true;
2950 |         }
2951 |       case Token.THIS:
2952 |         return locals.apply(value);
2953 |       case Token.NAME:
2954 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2955 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2956 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2957 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2958 |         return locals.apply(value);
2959 |       case Token.CALL:
2960 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2961 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2962 |             || locals.apply(value);
2963 |       case Token.NEW:
2964 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2965 |                || locals.apply(value);
2966 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2967 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2968 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2969 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2970 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2971 |         return true;
2972 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2973 |       case Token.IN:
2974 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2975 |         return true;
2976 |       default:
2977 |         // Other op force a local value:
2978 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2979 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2980 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2981 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2982 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2983 |           return true;
2984 |         }
2985 | 
2986 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2987 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2988 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2989 |     }
2990 |   }

703 |     boolean provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock thatBlock) {

===== M1189 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1332-1334
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
1332 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
1333 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
1334 |   }

157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 |

179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.

181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }

187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineObjectLiterals.InliningBehavior.isInlinableObject(List<Reference>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineObjectLiterals.java
Original range: 155-256
Documentation:
/**
     * Counts the number of direct (full) references to an object.
     * Specifically, we check for references of the following type:
     * <pre>
     *   x;
     *   x.fn();
     * </pre>
     */
Method code:
155 |     private boolean isInlinableObject(List<Reference> refs) {
156 |       boolean ret = false;
157 |       Set<String> validProperties = Sets.newHashSet();
158 |       for (Reference ref : refs) {
159 |         Node name = ref.getNode();
160 |         Node parent = ref.getParent();
161 |         Node gramps = ref.getGrandparent();
162 | 
163 |         // Ignore most indirect references, like x.y (but not x.y(),
164 |         // since the function referenced by y might reference 'this').
165 |         //
166 |         if (parent.isGetProp()) {
167 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.getFirstChild() == name);
168 |           // A call target may be using the object as a 'this' value.
169 |           if (gramps.isCall()
170 |               && gramps.getFirstChild() == parent) {
171 |             return false;
172 |           }
173 | 
174 |           // Deleting a property has different semantics from deleting
175 |           // a variable, so deleted properties should not be inlined.
176 |           if (gramps.isDelProp()) {
177 |             return false;
178 |           }
179 | 
180 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): This pass's object-splitting algorithm has
181 |           // a blind spot. It assumes that if a property isn't defined on an
182 |           // object, then the value is undefined. This is not true, because
183 |           // Object.prototype can have arbitrary properties on it.
184 |           //
185 |           // We short-circuit this problem by bailing out if we see a reference
186 |           // to a property that isn't defined on the object literal. This
187 |           // isn't a perfect algorithm, but it should catch most cases.
188 |           String propName = parent.getLastChild().getString();
189 |           if (!validProperties.contains(propName)) {
190 |             if (NodeUtil.isVarOrSimpleAssignLhs(parent, gramps)) {
191 |               validProperties.add(propName);
192 |             } else {
193 |               return false;
194 |             }
195 |           }
196 |           continue;
197 |         }
198 | 
199 |         // Only rewrite VAR declarations or simple assignment statements
200 |         if (!isVarOrAssignExprLhs(name)) {
201 |            return false;
202 |         }
203 | 
204 |         Node val = ref.getAssignedValue();
205 |         if (val == null) {
206 |           // A var with no assignment.
207 |           continue;
208 |         }
209 | 
210 |         // We're looking for object literal assignments only.
211 |         if (!val.isObjectLit()) {
212 |           return false;
213 |         }
214 | 
215 |         // Make sure that the value is not self-referential. IOW,
216 |         // disallow things like x = {b: x.a}.
217 |         //
218 |         // TODO: Only exclude unorderable self-referential
219 |         // assignments. i.e. x = {a: x.b, b: x.a} is not orderable,
220 |         // but x = {a: 1, b: x.a} is.
221 |         //
222 |         // Also, ES5 getters/setters aren't handled by this pass.
223 |         for (Node child = val.getFirstChild(); child != null;
224 |              child = child.getNext()) {
225 |           if (child.isGetterDef() ||
226 |               child.isSetterDef()) {
227 |             // ES5 get/set not supported.
228 |             return false;
229 |           }
230 | 
231 |           validProperties.add(child.getString());
232 | 
233 |           Node childVal = child.getFirstChild();
234 |           // Check if childVal is the parent of any of the passed in
235 |           // references, as that is how self-referential assignments
236 |           // will happen.
237 |           for (Reference t : refs) {
238 |             Node refNode = t.getParent();
239 |             while (!NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(refNode)) {
240 |               if (refNode == childVal) {
241 |                 // There's a self-referential assignment
242 |                 return false;
243 |               }
244 |               refNode = refNode.getParent();
245 |             }
246 |           }
247 |         }
248 | 
249 | 
250 |         // We have found an acceptable object literal assignment. As
251 |         // long as there are no other assignments that mess things up,
252 |         // we can inline.
253 |         ret = true;
254 |       }
255 |       return ret;
256 |     }

===== M1216 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 721-770
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
721 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
722 |     boolean changes = false;
723 |     do {
724 |       changes = false;
725 | 
726 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
727 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
728 |       // we traverse it.
729 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
730 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
731 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
732 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
733 |           current--;
734 |         } else {
735 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
736 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
737 | 
738 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
739 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
740 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
741 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
742 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
743 |           } else {
744 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
745 |             // or a for...in variable.
746 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
747 |           }
748 | 
749 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
750 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
751 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
752 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
753 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
754 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
755 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
756 |             }
757 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
758 |               maybeEscaped = true;
759 |             }
760 |           }
761 | 
762 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
763 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
764 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
765 |             current--;
766 |           }
767 |         }
768 |       }
769 |     } while (changes);
770 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InferJSDocInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InferJSDocInfo.java
Original range: 92-189
Documentation:

Method code:
92 |   @Override
93 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
94 |     JSDocInfo docInfo;
95 | 
96 |     switch (n.getType()) {
97 |       // Infer JSDocInfo on types of all type declarations on variables.
98 |       case Token.NAME:
99 |         if (parent == null) {
100 |           return;
101 |         }
102 | 
103 |         // Only allow JSDoc on VARs, function declarations, and assigns.
104 |         if (!parent.isVar() &&
105 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent) &&
106 |             !(parent.isAssign() &&
107 |               n == parent.getFirstChild())) {
108 |           return;
109 |         }
110 | 
111 |         // There are four places the doc info could live.
112 |         // 1) A FUNCTION node.
113 |         // /** ... */ function f() { ... }
114 |         // 2) An ASSIGN parent.
115 |         // /** ... */ x = function () { ... }
116 |         // 3) A NAME parent.
117 |         // var x, /** ... */ y = function() { ... }
118 |         // 4) A VAR gramps.
119 |         // /** ... */ var x = function() { ... }
120 |         docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
121 |         if (docInfo == null &&
122 |             !(parent.isVar() &&
123 |                 !parent.hasOneChild())) {
124 |           docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
125 |         }
126 | 
127 |         // Try to find the type of the NAME.
128 |         JSType varType = n.getJSType();
129 |         if (varType == null && parent.isFunction()) {
130 |           varType = parent.getJSType();
131 |         }
132 | 
133 |         // If we have no type to attach JSDocInfo to, then there's nothing
134 |         // we can do.
135 |         if (varType == null || docInfo == null) {
136 |           return;
137 |         }
138 | 
139 |         // Dereference the type. If the result is not an object, or already
140 |         // has docs attached, then do nothing.
141 |         ObjectType objType = dereferenceToObject(varType);
142 |         if (objType == null || objType.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
143 |           return;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(objType, docInfo, n.getString());
147 |         break;
148 | 
149 |       case Token.GETPROP:
150 |         // Infer JSDocInfo on properties.
151 |         // There are two ways to write doc comments on a property.
152 |         //
153 |         // 1)
154 |         // /** @deprecated */
155 |         // obj.prop = ...
156 |         //
157 |         // 2)
158 |         // /** @deprecated */
159 |         // obj.prop;
160 |         if (parent.isExprResult() ||
161 |             (parent.isAssign() &&
162 |              parent.getFirstChild() == n)) {
163 |           docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
164 |           if (docInfo == null) {
165 |             docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
166 |           }
167 |           if (docInfo != null) {
168 |             ObjectType lhsType =
169 |                 dereferenceToObject(n.getFirstChild().getJSType());
170 |             if (lhsType != null) {
171 |               // Put the JSDoc in the property slot, if there is one.
172 |               String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
173 |               if (lhsType.hasOwnProperty(propName)) {
174 |                 lhsType.setPropertyJSDocInfo(propName, docInfo);
175 |               }
176 | 
177 |               // Put the JSDoc in any constructors or function shapes as well.
178 |               ObjectType propType =
179 |                   dereferenceToObject(lhsType.getPropertyType(propName));
180 |               if (propType != null) {
181 |                 attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(
182 |                     propType, docInfo, n.getQualifiedName());
183 |               }
184 |             }
185 |           }
186 |         }
187 |         break;
188 |     }
189 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType,EquivalenceMethod)

/**
   * An equivalence visitor.
   */
Method code:
654 |   boolean checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType that, EquivalenceMethod eqMethod) {
655 |     if (this == that) {
656 |       return true;
657 |     }
658 | 
659 |     boolean thisUnknown = isUnknownType();
660 |     boolean thatUnknown = that.isUnknownType();
661 |     if (thisUnknown || thatUnknown) {
662 |       if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.INVARIANT) {
663 |         // If we're checking for invariance, the unknown type is invariant
664 |         // with everyone.
665 |         return true;
666 |       } else if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.DATA_FLOW) {
667 |         // If we're checking data flow, then two types are the same if they're
668 |         // both unknown.
669 |         return thisUnknown && thatUnknown;
670 |       } else if (thisUnknown && thatUnknown &&
671 |           (isNominalType() ^ that.isNominalType())) {
672 |         // If they're both unknown, but one is a nominal type and the other
673 |         // is not, then we should fail out immediately. This ensures that
674 |         // we won't unbox the unknowns further down.
675 |         return false;
676 |       }
677 |     }
678 | 
679 |     if (isUnionType() && that.isUnionType()) {
680 |       return toMaybeUnionType().checkUnionEquivalenceHelper(
681 |           that.toMaybeUnionType(), eqMethod);
682 |     }
683 | 
684 |     if (isFunctionType() && that.isFunctionType()) {
685 |       return toMaybeFunctionType().checkFunctionEquivalenceHelper(
686 |           that.toMaybeFunctionType(), eqMethod);
687 |     }
688 | 
689 |     if (isRecordType() && that.isRecordType()) {
690 |       return toMaybeRecordType().checkRecordEquivalenceHelper(
691 |           that.toMaybeRecordType(), eqMethod);
692 |     }
693 | 
694 |     ParameterizedType thisParamType = toMaybeParameterizedType();
695 |     ParameterizedType thatParamType = that.toMaybeParameterizedType();
696 |     if (thisParamType != null || thatParamType != null) {
697 |       // Check if one type is parameterized, but the other is not.
698 |       boolean paramsMatch = false;
699 |       if (thisParamType != null && thatParamType != null) {
700 |         paramsMatch = thisParamType.getParameterType().checkEquivalenceHelper(
701 |             thatParamType.getParameterType(), eqMethod);
702 |       } else if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.IDENTITY) {
703 |         paramsMatch = false;
704 |       } else {
705 |         // If one of the type parameters is unknown, but the other is not,
706 |         // then we consider these the same for the purposes of data flow
707 |         // and invariance.
708 |         paramsMatch = true;
709 |       }
710 | 
711 |       JSType thisRootType = thisParamType == null ?
712 |           this : thisParamType.getReferencedTypeInternal();
713 |       JSType thatRootType = thatParamType == null ?
714 |           that : thatParamType.getReferencedTypeInternal();
715 |       return paramsMatch &&
716 |           thisRootType.checkEquivalenceHelper(thatRootType, eqMethod);
717 |     }
718 | 
719 |     if (isNominalType() && that.isNominalType()) {
720 |       return toObjectType().getReferenceName().equals(
721 |           that.toObjectType().getReferenceName());
722 |     }
723 | 
724 |     // Unbox other proxies.
725 |     if (this instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
726 |       return ((ProxyObjectType) this)
727 |           .getReferencedTypeInternal().checkEquivalenceHelper(
728 |               that, eqMethod);
729 |     }
730 | 
731 |     if (that instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
732 |       return checkEquivalenceHelper(
733 |           ((ProxyObjectType) that).getReferencedTypeInternal(),
734 |           eqMethod);
735 |     }
736 | 
737 |     // Relies on the fact that for the base {@link JSType}, only one
738 |     // instance of each sub-type will ever be created in a given registry, so
739 |     // there is no need to verify members. If the object pointers are not
740 |     // identical, then the type member must be different.
741 |     return this == that;
742 |   }

567 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
568 | 
569 |     Node result = null;
570 | 
571 |     int type = n.getType();
572 | 
573 |     TernaryValue leftVal = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(left);
574 | 
575 |     if (leftVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
576 |       boolean lval = leftVal.toBoolean(true);
577 | 
578 |       // (TRUE || x) => TRUE (also, (3 || x) => 3)
579 |       // (FALSE && x) => FALSE
580 |       if (lval && type == Token.OR ||
581 |           !lval && type == Token.AND) {
582 |         result = left;
583 | 
584 |       } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
585 |         // (FALSE || x) => x

588 |       }

592 |     // PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax#tryMinimizeCondition
593 |

595 |       // Fold it!
596 |       n.removeChild(result);
597 |       parent.replaceChild(n, result);
598 |       reportCodeChange();
599 | 
600 |       return result;
601 |     } else {
602 |       return n;
603 |     }
604 |   }

/**
   * Look for exits (returns, breaks, or continues, depending on the context) at
   * the end of a block and removes them by moving the if node's siblings,
   * if any, into the opposite condition block.
   *
   * @param srcBlock The block to inspect.
   * @param destBlock The block to move sibling nodes into.
   * @param ifNode The if node to work with.
   * @param exitType The type of exit to look for.
   * @param labelName The name associated with the exit, if any.
   * @nullable labelName null for anything excepted for named-break associated
   *           with a label.
   */
Method code:
220 |   private void tryMinimizeIfBlockExits(Node srcBlock, Node destBlock,
221 |       Node ifNode, int exitType, String labelName) {
222 |     Node exitNodeParent = null;
223 |     Node exitNode = null;
224 | 
225 |     // Pick an exit node candidate.
226 |     if (srcBlock.isBlock()) {
227 |       if (!srcBlock.hasChildren()) {
228 |         return;
229 |       }
230 |       exitNodeParent = srcBlock;
231 |       exitNode = exitNodeParent.getLastChild();
232 |     } else {
233 |       // Just a single statement, if it isn't an exit bail.
234 |       exitNodeParent = ifNode;
235 |       exitNode = srcBlock;
236 |     }
237 | 
238 |     // Verify the candidate.
239 |     if (!matchingExitNode(exitNode, exitType, labelName)) {
240 |       return;
241 |     }
242 | 
243 |     // Take case of the if nodes siblings, if any.
244 |     if (ifNode.getNext() != null) {
245 |       // Move siblings of the if block into the opposite
246 |       // logic block of the exit.
247 |       Node newDestBlock = IR.block().srcref(ifNode);
248 |       if (destBlock == null) {
249 |         // Only possible if this is the false block.
250 |         ifNode.addChildToBack(newDestBlock);
251 |       } else if (destBlock.isEmpty()) {
252 |         // Use the new block.
253 |         ifNode.replaceChild(destBlock, newDestBlock);
254 |       } else if (destBlock.isBlock()) {
255 |         // Reuse the existing block.
256 |         newDestBlock = destBlock;
257 |       } else {
258 |         // Add the existing statement to the new block.
259 |         ifNode.replaceChild(destBlock, newDestBlock);
260 |         newDestBlock.addChildToBack(destBlock);
261 |       }
262 | 
263 |       // Move all the if node's following siblings.
264 |       moveAllFollowing(ifNode, ifNode.getParent(), newDestBlock);
265 |     }
266 | 
267 |     // Get rid of the "exit", replace with an empty item if needed.
268 |     NodeUtil.removeChild(exitNodeParent, exitNode);
269 | 
270 |     compiler.reportCodeChange();
271 |   }

52 |   public CheckLevel level(JSError error) {

56 |            current != null;
57 |            current = current.getParent()) {
58 |         int type = current.getType();
59 |         JSDocInfo info = null;
60 |

62 |         // level. Otherwise, the @suppress annotation has an implicit

71 |           if (rhs.isFunction()) {

81 |             // may not have a warnings guard.

84 |               if (newLevel != null) {
85 |                 return newLevel;

87 |             }
88 |           }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.getOrCreateConstructor()

/**
   * Returns a constructor function either by returning it from the
   * registry if it exists or creating and registering a new type. If
   * there is already a type, then warn if the existing type is
   * different than the one we are creating, though still return the
   * existing function if possible.  The primary purpose of this is
   * that registering a constructor will fail for all built-in types
   * that are initialized in {@link JSTypeRegistry}.  We a) want to
   * make sure that the type information specified in the externs file
   * matches what is in the registry and b) annotate the externs with
   * the {@link JSType} from the registry so that there are not two
   * separate JSType objects for one type.
   */
Method code:
665 |   private FunctionType getOrCreateConstructor() {
666 |     FunctionType fnType = typeRegistry.createConstructorType(
667 |         fnName, contents.getSourceNode(), parametersNode, returnType, null);
668 |     JSType existingType = typeRegistry.getType(fnName);
669 | 
670 |     if (makesStructs) {
671 |       fnType.setStruct();
672 |     } else if (makesDicts) {
673 |       fnType.setDict();
674 |     }
675 |     if (existingType != null) {
676 |       boolean isInstanceObject = existingType.isInstanceType();
677 |       if (isInstanceObject || fnName.equals("Function")) {
678 |         FunctionType existingFn =
679 |             isInstanceObject ?
680 |             existingType.toObjectType().getConstructor() :
681 |             typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType(FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE);
682 | 
683 |         if (existingFn.getSource() == null) {
684 |           existingFn.setSource(contents.getSourceNode());
685 |         }
686 | 
687 |         if (!existingFn.hasEqualCallType(fnType)) {
688 |           reportWarning(TYPE_REDEFINITION, fnName,
689 |               fnType.toString(), existingFn.toString());
690 |         }
691 | 
692 |         return existingFn;
693 |       } else {
694 |         // We fall through and return the created type, even though it will fail
695 |         // to register. We have no choice as we have to return a function. We
696 |         // issue an error elsewhere though, so the user should fix it.
697 |       }
698 |     }
699 | 
700 |     maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
701 | 
702 |     if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
703 |       typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
704 |     }
705 |     return fnType;
706 |   }

/**
     * Declare the symbol for a qualified name in the global scope.
     *
     * @param info The doc info for this property.
     * @param n A top-level GETPROP node (it should not be contained inside
     *     another GETPROP).
     * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
     * @param rhsValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.
     */
Method code:
1484 |     void maybeDeclareQualifiedName(NodeTraversal t, JSDocInfo info,
1485 |         Node n, Node parent, Node rhsValue) {
1486 |       Node ownerNode = n.getFirstChild();
1487 |       String ownerName = ownerNode.getQualifiedName();
1488 |       String qName = n.getQualifiedName();
1489 |       String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
1490 |       Preconditions.checkArgument(qName != null && ownerName != null);
1491 | 
1492 |       // Precedence of type information on GETPROPs:
1493 |       // 1) @type annotation / @enum annotation
1494 |       // 2) ASSIGN to FUNCTION literal
1495 |       // 3) @param/@return annotation (with no function literal)
1496 |       // 4) ASSIGN to something marked @const
1497 |       // 5) ASSIGN to anything else
1498 |       //
1499 |       // 1, 3, and 4 are declarations, 5 is inferred, and 2 is a declaration iff
1500 |       // the function has JsDoc or has not been declared before.
1501 |       //
1502 |       // FUNCTION literals are special because TypedScopeCreator is very smart
1503 |       // about getting as much type information as possible for them.
1504 | 
1505 |       // Determining type for #1 + #2 + #3 + #4
1506 |       JSType valueType = getDeclaredType(t.getSourceName(), info, n, rhsValue);
1507 |       if (valueType == null && rhsValue != null) {
1508 |         // Determining type for #5
1509 |         valueType = rhsValue.getJSType();
1510 |       }
1511 | 
1512 |       // Function prototypes are special.
1513 |       // It's a common JS idiom to do:
1514 |       // F.prototype = { ... };
1515 |       // So if F does not have an explicitly declared super type,
1516 |       // allow F.prototype to be redefined arbitrarily.
1517 |       if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
1518 |         Var qVar = scope.getVar(qName);
1519 |         if (qVar != null) {
1520 |           // If the programmer has declared that F inherits from Super,
1521 |           // and they assign F.prototype to an object literal,
1522 |           // then they are responsible for making sure that the object literal's
1523 |           // implicit prototype is set up appropriately. We just obey
1524 |           // the @extends tag.
1525 |           ObjectType qVarType = ObjectType.cast(qVar.getType());
1526 |           if (qVarType != null &&
1527 |               rhsValue != null &&
1528 |               rhsValue.isObjectLit()) {
1529 |             typeRegistry.resetImplicitPrototype(
1530 |                 rhsValue.getJSType(), qVarType.getImplicitPrototype());
1531 |           } else if (!qVar.isTypeInferred()) {
1532 |             // If the programmer has declared that F inherits from Super,
1533 |             // and they assign F.prototype to some arbitrary expression,
1534 |             // there's not much we can do. We just ignore the expression,
1535 |             // and hope they've annotated their code in a way to tell us
1536 |             // what props are going to be on that prototype.
1537 |             return;
1538 |           }
1539 |           if (qVar.getScope() == scope) {
1540 |             scope.undeclare(qVar);
1541 |           }
1542 |         }
1543 |       }
1544 | 
1545 |       if (valueType == null) {
1546 |         if (parent.isExprResult()) {
1547 |           stubDeclarations.add(new StubDeclaration(
1548 |               n,
1549 |               t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern(),
1550 |               ownerName));
1551 |         }
1552 | 
1553 |         return;
1554 |       }
1555 | 
1556 |       boolean inferred = isQualifiedNameInferred(
1557 |           qName, n, info, rhsValue, valueType);
1558 |       if (!inferred) {
1559 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1560 |         if (ownerType != null) {
1561 |           // Only declare this as an official property if it has not been
1562 |           // declared yet.
1563 |           boolean isExtern = t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern();
1564 |           if ((!ownerType.hasOwnProperty(propName) ||
1565 |                ownerType.isPropertyTypeInferred(propName)) &&
1566 |               ((isExtern && !ownerType.isNativeObjectType()) ||
1567 |                !ownerType.isInstanceType())) {
1568 |             // If the property is undeclared or inferred, declare it now.
1569 |             ownerType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, valueType, n);
1570 |           }
1571 |         }
1572 | 
1573 |         // If the property is already declared, the error will be
1574 |         // caught when we try to declare it in the current scope.
1575 |         defineSlot(n, parent, valueType, inferred);
1576 |       } else if (rhsValue != null && rhsValue.isTrue()) {
1577 |         // We declare these for delegate proxy method properties.
1578 |         FunctionType ownerType =
1579 |             JSType.toMaybeFunctionType(getObjectSlot(ownerName));
1580 |         if (ownerType != null) {
1581 |           JSType ownerTypeOfThis = ownerType.getTypeOfThis();
1582 |           String delegateName = codingConvention.getDelegateSuperclassName();
1583 |           JSType delegateType = delegateName == null ?
1584 |               null : typeRegistry.getType(delegateName);
1585 |           if (delegateType != null &&
1586 |               ownerTypeOfThis.isSubtype(delegateType)) {
1587 |             defineSlot(n, parent, getNativeType(BOOLEAN_TYPE), true);
1588 |           }
1589 |         }
1590 |       }
