Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getBestJSDocInfo(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 3046-3074
Documentation:
/** Find the best JSDoc for the given node. */
Method code:
3046 |   static JSDocInfo getBestJSDocInfo(Node n) {
3047 |     JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
3048 |     if (info == null) {
3049 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
3050 |       if (parent == null) {
3051 |         return null;
3052 |       }
3053 | 
3054 |       if (parent.isName()) {
3055 |         return getBestJSDocInfo(parent);
3056 |       } else if (parent.isAssign()) {
3057 |         return parent.getJSDocInfo();
3058 |       } else if (isObjectLitKey(parent, parent.getParent())) {
3059 |         return parent.getJSDocInfo();
3060 |       } else if (parent.isFunction()) {
3061 |         return parent.getJSDocInfo();
3062 |       } else if (parent.isVar() && parent.hasOneChild()) {
3063 |         return parent.getJSDocInfo();
3064 |       } else if ((parent.isHook() && parent.getFirstChild() != n) ||
3065 |                  parent.isOr() ||
3066 |                  parent.isAnd() ||
3067 |                  (parent.isComma() && parent.getFirstChild() != n)) {
3068 |         return getBestJSDocInfo(parent);
3069 |       } else if (parent.isCast()) {
3070 |         return parent.getJSDocInfo();
3071 |       }
3072 |     }
3073 |     return info;
3074 |   }

395 |     @Override
396 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
397 |       if (isCallToScopeMethod(n)) {
398 |         validateScopeCall(t, n, n.getParent());
399 |       }
400 | 
401 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() < 2) {
402 |         return;
403 |       }
404 | 
405 |       int type = n.getType();
406 |       Var aliasVar = null;
407 |       if (type == Token.NAME) {
408 |         String name = n.getString();
409 |         Var lexicalVar = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
410 |         if (lexicalVar != null && lexicalVar == aliases.get(name)) {
411 |           aliasVar = lexicalVar;
412 |         }
413 |       }
414 | 
415 |       // Validate the top-level of the goog.scope block.
416 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() == 2) {
417 |         if (aliasVar != null && NodeUtil.isLValue(n)) {
418 |           if (aliasVar.getNode() == n) {
419 |             aliasDefinitionsInOrder.add(n);
420 | 
421 |             // Return early, to ensure that we don't record a definition
422 |             // twice.
423 |             return;
424 |           } else {
425 |             report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_ALIAS_REDEFINED, n.getString());
426 |           }
427 |         }
428 | 
429 |         if (type == Token.RETURN) {
430 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_RETURN);
431 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
432 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_REFERENCES_THIS);
433 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
434 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
435 |         }
436 |       }
437 | 
438 |       // Validate all descendent scopes of the goog.scope block.
439 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {
440 |         // Check if this name points to an alias.
441 |         if (aliasVar != null) {
442 |           // Note, to support the transitive case, it's important we don't
443 |           // clone aliasedNode here.  For example,
444 |           // var g = goog; var d = g.dom; d.createElement('DIV');
445 |           // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the
446 |           // changes pass above with "goog".  If we cloned here, we'd end up
447 |           // with <code>g.dom.createElement('DIV')</code>.
448 |           Node aliasedNode = aliasVar.getInitialValue();
449 |           aliasUsages.add(new AliasedNode(n, aliasedNode));
450 |         }
451 | 
452 |         JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
453 |         if (info != null) {
454 |           for (Node node : info.getTypeNodes()) {
455 |             fixTypeNode(node);

386 |       }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.JsFileParser.parseLine(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/JsFileParser.java
Original range: 137-188
Documentation:
/**
   * Parses a line of JavaScript, extracting goog.provide and goog.require
   * information.
   */
Method code:
137 |   @Override
138 |   protected boolean parseLine(String line) throws ParseException {
139 |     boolean lineHasProvidesOrRequires = false;
140 | 
141 |     // Quick sanity check that will catch most cases. This is a performance
142 |     // win for people with a lot of JS.
143 |     if (line.indexOf("provide") != -1 ||
144 |         line.indexOf("require") != -1 ||
145 |         line.indexOf("addDependency") != -1) {
146 |       // Iterate over the provides/requires.
147 |       googMatcher.reset(line);
148 |       while (googMatcher.find()) {
149 |         lineHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
150 | 
151 |         if (includeGoogBase && !fileHasProvidesOrRequires) {
152 |           fileHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
153 |           requires.add("goog");
154 |         }
155 | 
156 |         // See if it's a require or provide.
157 |         char firstChar = googMatcher.group(1).charAt(0);
158 |         boolean isProvide = firstChar == 'p';
159 |         boolean isRequire = firstChar == 'r';
160 | 
161 |         if (isProvide || isRequire) {
162 |           // Parse the param.
163 |           String arg = parseJsString(googMatcher.group(2));
164 | 
165 |           // Add the dependency.
166 |           if (isRequire) {
167 |             // goog is always implicit.
168 |             // TODO(nicksantos): I'm pretty sure we don't need this anymore.
169 |             // Remove this later.
170 |             if (!"goog".equals(arg)) {
171 |               requires.add(arg);
172 |             }
173 |           } else {
174 |             provides.add(arg);
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 |     } else if (includeGoogBase && line.startsWith(BASE_JS_START) &&
179 |                provides.isEmpty() && requires.isEmpty()) {
180 |       provides.add("goog");
181 | 
182 |       // base.js can't provide or require anything else.
183 |       return false;
184 |     }
185 | 
186 |     return !shortcutMode || lineHasProvidesOrRequires ||
187 |         CharMatcher.WHITESPACE.matchesAllOf(line);
188 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureCodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureCodingConvention.java
Original range: 94-153
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>Understands several different inheritance patterns that occur in
   * Google code (various uses of {@code inherits} and {@code mixin}).
   */
Method code:
94 |   @Override
95 |   public SubclassRelationship getClassesDefinedByCall(Node callNode) {
96 |     SubclassRelationship relationship =
97 |         super.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
98 |     if (relationship != null) return relationship;
99 | 
100 |     Node callName = callNode.getFirstChild();
101 |     SubclassType type = typeofClassDefiningName(callName);
102 |     if (type != null) {
103 |       Node subclass = null;
104 |       Node superclass = callNode.getLastChild();
105 | 
106 |       // There are six possible syntaxes for a class-defining method:
107 |       // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
108 |       // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
109 |       // goog$inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
110 |       // SubClass.mixin(SuperClass.prototype)
111 |       // goog.mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
112 |       // goog$mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
113 |       boolean isDeprecatedCall = callNode.getChildCount() == 2 &&
114 |           callName.isGetProp();
115 |       if (isDeprecatedCall) {
116 |         // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
117 |         subclass = callName.getFirstChild();
118 |       } else if (callNode.getChildCount() == 3) {
119 |         // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
120 |         subclass = callName.getNext();
121 |       } else {
122 |         return null;
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       if (type == SubclassType.MIXIN) {
126 |         // Only consider mixins that mix two prototypes as related to
127 |         // inheritance.
128 |         if (!endsWithPrototype(superclass)) {
129 |           return null;
130 |         }
131 |         if (!isDeprecatedCall) {
132 |           if (!endsWithPrototype(subclass)) {
133 |             return null;
134 |           }
135 |           // Strip off the prototype from the name.
136 |           subclass = subclass.getFirstChild();
137 |         }
138 |         superclass = superclass.getFirstChild();
139 |       }
140 | 
141 |       // bail out if either of the side of the "inherits"
142 |       // isn't a real class name. This prevents us from
143 |       // doing something weird in cases like:
144 |       // goog.inherits(MySubClass, cond ? SuperClass1 : BaseClass2)
145 |       if (subclass != null &&
146 |           subclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
147 |           superclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
148 |         return new SubclassRelationship(type, subclass, superclass);
149 |       }
150 |     }
151 | 
152 |     return null;
153 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node)

Original range: 1367-1415
Documentation:
/**
   * Replaces a new Array or Object node with an object literal, unless the
   * call to Array or Object is to a local function with the same name.
   */
Method code:
1367 |   private Node tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node n) {
1368 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isCall()
1369 |         || n.isNew());
1370 | 
1371 |     Node constructorNameNode = n.getFirstChild();
1372 | 
1373 |     Node newLiteralNode = null;
1374 | 
1375 |     // We require the AST to be normalized to ensure that, say,
1376 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor
1377 |     // and not a user-defined constructor with the same name.
1378 | 
1379 |     if (isASTNormalized() && Token.NAME == constructorNameNode.getType()) {
1380 | 
1381 |       String className = constructorNameNode.getString();
1382 | 
1383 |       if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
1384 |         // "RegExp("boo", "g")" --> /boo/g
1385 |         return tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(n);
1386 |       } else {
1387 |         boolean constructorHasArgs = constructorNameNode.getNext() != null;
1388 | 
1389 |         if ("Object".equals(className) && !constructorHasArgs) {
1390 |           // "Object()" --> "{}"
1391 |           newLiteralNode = IR.objectlit();
1392 |         } else if ("Array".equals(className)) {
1393 |           // "Array(arg0, arg1, ...)" --> "[arg0, arg1, ...]"
1394 |           Node arg0 = constructorNameNode.getNext();
1395 |           FoldArrayAction action = isSafeToFoldArrayConstructor(arg0);
1396 | 
1397 |           if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS ||
1398 |               action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITHOUT_ARGS) {
1399 |             newLiteralNode = IR.arraylit();
1400 |             n.removeChildren();
1401 |             if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS) {
1402 |               newLiteralNode.addChildrenToFront(arg0);
1403 |             }
1404 |           }
1405 |         }
1406 | 
1407 |         if (newLiteralNode != null) {
1408 |           n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newLiteralNode);
1409 |           reportCodeChange();
1410 |           return newLiteralNode;
1411 |         }
1412 |       }
1413 |     }
1414 |     return n;
1415 |   }

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get
   * JsDoc descriptions.

2385 |   private boolean lookAheadForTypeAnnotation() {

2390 |       if (c == ' ') {
2391 |         continue;

2393 |         matchedLc = true;
2394 |         break;
2395 |       } else {

2397 |       }
2398 |     }

672 |   private Node tryFoldIf(Node n) {
673 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isIf());
674 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
675 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(parent);
676 |     int type = n.getType();
677 |     Node cond = n.getFirstChild();
678 |     Node thenBody = cond.getNext();
679 |     Node elseBody = thenBody.getNext();
680 | 
681 |     // if (x) { .. } else { } --> if (x) { ... }
682 |     if (elseBody != null && !mayHaveSideEffects(elseBody)) {
683 |       n.removeChild(elseBody);
684 |       elseBody = null;
685 |       reportCodeChange();
686 |     }
687 | 
688 |     // if (x) { } else { ... } --> if (!x) { ... }
689 |     if (!mayHaveSideEffects(thenBody) && elseBody != null) {
690 |       n.removeChild(elseBody);
691 |       n.replaceChild(thenBody, elseBody);
692 |       Node notCond = new Node(Token.NOT);
693 |       n.replaceChild(cond, notCond);
694 |       notCond.addChildToFront(cond);
695 |       cond = notCond;
696 |       thenBody = cond.getNext();
697 |       elseBody = null;
698 |       reportCodeChange();
699 |     }
700 | 
701 |     // if (x()) { }
702 |     if (!mayHaveSideEffects(thenBody) && elseBody == null) {
703 |       if (mayHaveSideEffects(cond)) {
704 |         // x() has side effects, just leave the condition on its own.
705 |         n.removeChild(cond);
706 |         Node replacement = NodeUtil.newExpr(cond);
707 |         parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
708 |         reportCodeChange();
709 |         return replacement;
710 |       } else {
711 |         // x() has no side effects, the whole tree is useless now.
712 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, n);
713 |         reportCodeChange();
714 |         return null;
715 |       }
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // Try transforms that apply to both IF and HOOK.
719 |     TernaryValue condValue = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(cond);
720 |     if (condValue == TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
721 |       return n;  // We can't remove branches otherwise!
722 |     }
723 | 
724 |     if (mayHaveSideEffects(cond)) {
725 |       // Transform "if (a = 2) {x =2}" into "if (true) {a=2;x=2}"
726 |       boolean newConditionValue = condValue == TernaryValue.TRUE;
727 |       // Add an elseBody if it is needed.
728 |       if (!newConditionValue && elseBody == null) {
729 |         elseBody = IR.block().srcref(n);
730 |         n.addChildToBack(elseBody);
731 |       }
732 |       Node newCond = NodeUtil.booleanNode(newConditionValue);
733 |       n.replaceChild(cond, newCond);
734 |       Node branchToKeep = newConditionValue ? thenBody : elseBody;
735 |       branchToKeep.addChildToFront(IR.exprResult(cond).srcref(cond));
736 |       reportCodeChange();
737 |       cond = newCond;
738 |     }
739 | 
740 |     boolean condTrue = condValue.toBoolean(true);
741 |     if (n.getChildCount() == 2) {
742 |       Preconditions.checkState(type == Token.IF);
743 | 
744 |       if (condTrue) {
745 |         // Replace "if (true) { X }" with "X".
746 |         Node thenStmt = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
747 |         n.removeChild(thenStmt);
748 |         parent.replaceChild(n, thenStmt);
749 |         reportCodeChange();
750 |         return thenStmt;
751 |       } else {
752 |         // Remove "if (false) { X }" completely.
753 |         NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch(n);
754 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, n);
755 |         reportCodeChange();
756 |         return null;
757 |       }
758 |     } else {
759 |       // Replace "if (true) { X } else { Y }" with X, or
760 |       // replace "if (false) { X } else { Y }" with Y.
761 |       Node trueBranch = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
762 |       Node falseBranch = trueBranch.getNext();
763 |       Node branchToKeep = condTrue ? trueBranch : falseBranch;
764 |       Node branchToRemove = condTrue ? falseBranch : trueBranch;
765 |       NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch(branchToRemove);
766 |       n.removeChild(branchToKeep);
767 |       parent.replaceChild(n, branchToKeep);
768 |       reportCodeChange();
769 |       return branchToKeep;
770 |     }
771 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

477 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
478 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
479 |     int type = n.getType();

===== M1466 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.java
Original range: 124-170
Documentation:

Method code:
124 |   @Override
125 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
126 | 
127 |     if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
128 |       return; // Don't even brother. All global variables are likely escaped.
129 |     }
130 | 
131 |     if (LiveVariablesAnalysis.MAX_VARIABLES_TO_ANALYZE <
132 |         t.getScope().getVarCount()) {
133 |       return;
134 |     }
135 | 
136 |     // Compute the forward reaching definition.
137 |     ControlFlowAnalysis cfa = new ControlFlowAnalysis(compiler, false, true);
138 |     // Process the body of the function.
139 |     Preconditions.checkState(t.getScopeRoot().isFunction());
140 |     cfa.process(null, t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
141 |     cfg = cfa.getCfg();
142 |     reachingDef = new MustBeReachingVariableDef(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
143 |     reachingDef.analyze();
144 |     candidates = Lists.newLinkedList();
145 | 
146 |     // Using the forward reaching definition search to find all the inline
147 |     // candidates
148 |     new NodeTraversal(compiler, new GatherCandiates()).traverse(
149 |         t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
150 | 
151 |     // Compute the backward reaching use. The CFG can be reused.
152 |     reachingUses = new MaybeReachingVariableUse(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
153 |     reachingUses.analyze();
154 |     for (Candidate c : candidates) {
155 |       if (c.canInline(t.getScope())) {
156 |         c.inlineVariable();
157 | 
158 |         // If definition c has dependencies, then inlining it may have
159 |         // introduced new dependencies for our other inlining candidates.
160 |         //
161 |         // MustBeReachingVariableDef uses this dependency graph in its
162 |         // analysis, so some of these candidates may no longer be valid.
163 |         // We keep track of when the variable dependency graph changed
164 |         // so that we can back off appropriately.
165 |         if (!c.defMetadata.depends.isEmpty()) {
166 |           inlinedNewDependencies.add(t.getScope().getVar(c.varName));
167 |         }
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalVarReferenceMap.updateGlobalVarReferences(Map<Var, ReferenceCollection>,Node)

Documentation:
/**
   * Updates the internal reference map based on the provided parameters. If
   * {@code scriptRoot} is not SCRIPT, it basically replaces the internal map
   * with the new one, otherwise it replaces all the information associated to
   * the given script.
   *
   * @param refMapPatch The reference map result of a
   *     {@link ReferenceCollectingCallback} pass which might be collected from
   *     the whole AST or just a sub-tree associated to a SCRIPT node.
   * @param root AST sub-tree root on which reference collection was done.
   */
Method code:
100 |   void updateGlobalVarReferences(Map<Var, ReferenceCollection>
101 |       refMapPatch, Node root) {
102 |     if (refMap == null || !root.isScript()) {
103 |       resetGlobalVarReferences(refMapPatch);
104 |       return;
105 |     }
106 | 
107 |     InputId inputId = root.getInputId();
108 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
109 |     // Note there are two assumptions here (i) the order of compiler inputs
110 |     // has not changed and (ii) all references are in the order they appear
111 |     // in AST (this is enforced in ReferenceCollectionCallback).
112 |     removeScriptReferences(inputId);
113 |     for (Entry<Var, ReferenceCollection> entry : refMapPatch.entrySet()) {
114 |       Var var = entry.getKey();
115 |       if (var.isGlobal()) {
116 |         replaceReferences(var.getName(), inputId, entry.getValue());
117 |       }
118 |     }
119 |   }

   * Detects a cycle in the implicit prototype chain. This method accesses
   * the {@link #getImplicitPrototype()} method and must therefore be
   * invoked only after the object is sufficiently initialized to respond to
   * calls to this method.<p>
   *
   * @return True iff an implicit prototype cycle was detected.
   */
Method code:
170 |   final boolean detectImplicitPrototypeCycle() {
171 |     // detecting cycle
172 |     this.visited = true;
173 |     ObjectType p = getImplicitPrototype();
174 |     while (p != null) {
175 |       if (p.visited) {
176 |         return true;
177 |       } else {
178 |         p.visited = true;
179 |       }
180 |       p = p.getImplicitPrototype();
181 |     }
182 | 
183 |     // clean up
184 |     p = this;
185 |     do {
186 |       p.visited = false;
187 |       p = p.getImplicitPrototype();
188 |     } while (p != null);
189 |     return false;

326 |       // union types, so we don't need to check those again.

348 |       Iterable<ObjectType> thisInterfaces = getCtorImplementedInterfaces();

350 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
351 |           return true;

===== M1487 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 169-254
Documentation:

Method code:
169 |   private void computeMayUse(
170 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
171 |     switch (n.getType()) {
172 | 
173 |       case Token.BLOCK:
174 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
175 |         return;
176 | 
177 |       case Token.NAME:
178 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
179 |         return;
180 | 
181 |       case Token.WHILE:
182 |       case Token.DO:
183 |       case Token.IF:
184 |         computeMayUse(
185 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.FOR:
189 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
190 |           computeMayUse(
191 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
192 |         } else {
193 |           // for(x in y) {...}
194 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
195 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
196 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
197 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
198 |           }
199 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
200 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
201 |           }
202 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
203 |         }
204 |         return;
205 | 
206 |       case Token.AND:
207 |       case Token.OR:
208 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
209 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       case Token.HOOK:
213 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
214 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
215 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
216 |         return;
217 | 
218 |       case Token.VAR:
219 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
220 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
221 | 
222 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
223 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
224 |           if (!conditional) {
225 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
226 |           }
227 |         }
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       default:
231 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
232 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
233 |           if (!conditional) {
234 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
235 |           }
236 | 
237 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
238 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
239 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
240 |           }
241 | 
242 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
243 |         } else {
244 |           /*
245 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
246 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
247 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
248 |            */
249 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
250 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
251 |           }
252 |         }
253 |     }
254 |   }

===== M1520 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.toSource(CodeBuilder,int,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 1725-1787
Documentation:
/**
   * Writes out JS code from a root node. If printing input delimiters, this
   * method will attach a comment to the start of the text indicating which
   * input the output derived from. If there were any preserve annotations
   * within the root's source, they will also be printed in a block comment
   * at the beginning of the output.
   */
Method code:
1725 |   public void toSource(final CodeBuilder cb,
1726 |                        final int inputSeqNum,
1727 |                        final Node root) {
1728 |     runInCompilerThread(new Callable<Void>() {
1729 |       @Override
1730 |       public Void call() throws Exception {
1731 |         if (options.printInputDelimiter) {
1732 |           if ((cb.getLength() > 0) && !cb.endsWith("\n")) {
1733 |             cb.append("\n");  // Make sure that the label starts on a new line
1734 |           }
1735 |           Preconditions.checkState(root.isScript());
1736 | 
1737 |           String delimiter = options.inputDelimiter;
1738 | 
1739 |           String inputName = root.getInputId().getIdName();
1740 |           String sourceName = root.getSourceFileName();
1741 |           Preconditions.checkState(sourceName != null);
1742 |           Preconditions.checkState(!sourceName.isEmpty());
1743 | 
1744 |           delimiter = delimiter
1745 |               .replaceAll("%name%", Matcher.quoteReplacement(inputName))
1746 |               .replaceAll("%num%", String.valueOf(inputSeqNum));
1747 | 
1748 |           cb.append(delimiter)
1749 |             .append("\n");
1750 |         }
1751 |         if (root.getJSDocInfo() != null &&
1752 |             root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense() != null) {
1753 |           cb.append("/*\n")
1754 |             .append(root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense())
1755 |             .append("*/\n");
1756 |         }
1757 | 
1758 |         // If there is a valid source map, then indicate to it that the current
1759 |         // root node's mappings are offset by the given string builder buffer.
1760 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
1761 |           sourceMap.setStartingPosition(
1762 |               cb.getLineIndex(), cb.getColumnIndex());
1763 |         }
1764 | 
1765 |         // if LanguageMode is ECMASCRIPT5_STRICT, only print 'use strict'
1766 |         // for the first input file
1767 |         String code = toSource(root, sourceMap, inputSeqNum == 0);
1768 |         if (!code.isEmpty()) {
1769 |           cb.append(code);
1770 | 
1771 |           // In order to avoid parse ambiguity when files are concatenated
1772 |           // together, all files should end in a semi-colon. Do a quick
1773 |           // heuristic check if there's an obvious semi-colon already there.
1774 |           int length = code.length();
1775 |           char lastChar = code.charAt(length - 1);
1776 |           char secondLastChar = length >= 2 ?
1777 |               code.charAt(length - 2) : '\0';
1778 |           boolean hasSemiColon = lastChar == ';' ||
1779 |               (lastChar == '\n' && secondLastChar == ';');
1780 |           if (!hasSemiColon) {
1781 |             cb.append(";");
1782 |           }
1783 |         }
1784 |         return null;
1785 |       }
1786 |     });
1787 |   }

/**
   * Try turning IF nodes into smaller HOOKs

638 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
639 | 
640 |     Node cond = n.getFirstChild();
641 | 
642 |     /* If the condition is a literal, we'll let other
643 |      * optimizations try to remove useless code.
644 |      */
645 |     if (NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(cond, true)) {
646 |       return n;
647 |     }
648 | 
649 |     Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
650 |     Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
651 | 
652 |     if (elseBranch == null) {
653 |       if (isFoldableExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
654 |         Node expr = getBlockExpression(thenBranch);
655 |         if (!late && isPropertyAssignmentInExpression(expr)) {
656 |           // Keep opportunities for CollapseProperties such as
657 |           // a.longIdentifier || a.longIdentifier = ... -> var a = ...;
658 |           // until CollapseProperties has been run.

686 |           // there is no immediate code size win. However, two extra pair of
687 |           // {}, we would have to think twice. (unless we know for sure the
688 |           // we can further optimize its parent.
689 |           return n;
690 |         }

743 |       n.addChildToBack(thenBranch);

746 |     }

751 |       Node elseExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(elseBranch);

484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {

487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&

166 |           return result;
167 |         }
168 |         return tryFoldLeftChildOp(subtree, left, right);
169 | 
170 |       case Token.LT:
171 |       case Token.GT:

173 |       case Token.GE:
174 |       case Token.EQ:
175 |       case Token.NE:
176 |       case Token.SHEQ:
177 |       case Token.SHNE:
178 |         return tryFoldComparison(subtree, left, right);
179 | 
180 |       default:

182 |     }

===== M1575 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CoalesceVariableNames.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CoalesceVariableNames.java
Original range: 147-210
Documentation:

Method code:
147 |   @Override
148 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
149 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !n.isName() ||
150 |         parent.isFunction()) {
151 |       // Don't rename named functions.
152 |       return;
153 |     }
154 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
155 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
156 |     if (vNode == null) {
157 |       // This is not a local.
158 |       return;
159 |     }
160 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
161 | 
162 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
163 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
164 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
165 |         return;
166 |       }
167 | 
168 |       // Rename.
169 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
170 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
171 | 
172 |       if (parent.isVar()) {
173 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
174 |       }
175 |     } else {
176 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
177 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
178 |       // make this fast.
179 |       String pseudoName = null;
180 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
181 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
182 |         Var iVar = i.next();
183 | 
184 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
185 |         // and it is merged with the current coalescedVar.
186 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
187 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
188 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
189 |         }
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       // Keep its original name.
193 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
194 |         return;
195 |       }
196 | 
197 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
198 | 
199 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
200 |         pseudoName += "$";
201 |       }
202 | 
203 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
204 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
205 | 
206 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && parent.isVar()) {
207 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
208 |       }
209 |     }
210 |   }

236 |   private Node tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(Node n) {
237 |     // Rewriting "(fn.bind(a,b))()" to "fn.call(a,b)" makes it inlinable
238 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isCall());
239 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
240 |     Bind bind = getCodingConvention().describeFunctionBind(callTarget, false);
241 |     if (bind != null) {

248 |       addParameterAfter(bind.parameters, callTarget);
249 | 
250 |       // add the this value before the parameters if necessary
251 |       if (bind.thisValue != null && !NodeUtil.isUndefined(bind.thisValue)) {
252 |         // rewrite from "fn(a, b)" to "fn.call(thisValue, a, b)"

256 |         n.replaceChild(callTarget, newCallTarget);
257 |         n.addChildAfter(bind.thisValue.cloneTree(), newCallTarget);

===== M1617 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 564-611
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
564 |     private void extractForInitializer(
565 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
566 | 
567 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
568 |         next = c.getNext();
569 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
570 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
571 |         switch (c.getType()) {
572 |           case Token.LABEL:
573 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
574 |             break;
575 |           case Token.FOR:
576 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
577 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
578 |               if (first.isVar()) {
579 |                 // Transform:
580 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
581 |                 // to:
582 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
583 |                 Node newStatement = first;
584 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
585 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
586 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
587 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
588 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
589 |               }
590 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
591 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
592 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
593 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
594 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
595 | 
596 |               Node newStatement;
597 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
598 |               // but are handled differently.
599 |               if (init.isVar()) {
600 |                 newStatement = init;
601 |               } else {
602 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
603 |               }
604 | 
605 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
606 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
607 |             }
608 |             break;
609 |         }
610 |       }
611 |     }

===== M1624 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

   * Finds all defines, and creates a {@link DefineInfo} data structure for
   * each one.

172 |   private Map<String, DefineInfo> collectDefines(Node root,
173 |       GlobalNamespace namespace) {
174 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
175 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
176 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
177 |       Ref decl = name.getDeclaration();

183 |         } else {

202 |           }
203 |

205 |             allDefines.add(name);
206 |             break;
207 |           }
208 |         }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.DoShadowVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)

Method code:
174 |     @Override
175 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
176 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
177 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
178 |         return;
179 |       }
180 | 
181 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
182 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
183 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
184 |         return;
185 |       }
186 | 
187 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
188 |         Var var = vars.next();
189 | 
190 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
191 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
192 |           continue;
193 |         }
194 | 
195 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
196 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
197 |           continue;
198 |         }
199 | 
200 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
201 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
202 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
203 |           continue;
204 |         }
205 | 
206 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
207 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
208 | 
209 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
210 |         // shadowed variable.
211 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
212 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
213 |         }
214 | 
215 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
216 | 
217 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
218 |           String targetPseudoName =
219 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
220 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
221 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
222 |           }
223 |         }
224 |       }
225 |     }

===== M1670 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.removeChild(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1801-1854
Documentation:
/** Safely remove children while maintaining a valid node structure. */
Method code:
1801 |   static void removeChild(Node parent, Node node) {
1802 |     if (isTryFinallyNode(parent, node)) {
1803 |       if (NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(getCatchBlock(parent))) {
1804 |         // A finally can only be removed if there is a catch.
1805 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1806 |       } else {
1807 |         // Otherwise, only its children can be removed.
1808 |         node.detachChildren();
1809 |       }
1810 |     } else if (node.isCatch()) {
1811 |       // The CATCH can can only be removed if there is a finally clause.
1812 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent().getParent();
1813 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1814 |       node.detachFromParent();
1815 |     } else if (isTryCatchNodeContainer(node)) {
1816 |       // The container node itself can't be removed, but the contained CATCH
1817 |       // can if there is a 'finally' clause
1818 |       Node tryNode = node.getParent();
1819 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.hasFinally(tryNode));
1820 |       node.detachChildren();
1821 |     } else if (node.isBlock()) {
1822 |       // Simply empty the block.  This maintains source location and
1823 |       // "synthetic"-ness.
1824 |       node.detachChildren();
1825 |     } else if (isStatementBlock(parent)
1826 |         || isSwitchCase(node)) {
1827 |       // A statement in a block can simply be removed.
1828 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1829 |     } else if (parent.isVar()) {
1830 |       if (parent.hasMoreThanOneChild()) {
1831 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1832 |       } else {
1833 |         // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1834 |         parent.removeChild(node);
1835 |         // This would leave an empty VAR, remove the VAR itself.
1836 |         removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1837 |       }
1838 |     } else if (parent.isLabel()
1839 |         && node == parent.getLastChild()) {
1840 |       // Remove the node from the parent, so it can be reused.
1841 |       parent.removeChild(node);
1842 |       // A LABEL without children can not be referred to, remove it.
1843 |       removeChild(parent.getParent(), parent);
1844 |     } else if (parent.isFor()
1845 |         && parent.getChildCount() == 4) {
1846 |       // Only Token.FOR can have an Token.EMPTY other control structure
1847 |       // need something for the condition. Others need to be replaced
1848 |       // or the structure removed.
1849 |       parent.replaceChild(node, IR.empty());
1850 |     } else {
1851 |       throw new IllegalStateException("Invalid attempt to remove node: " +
1852 |           node.toString() + " of " + parent.toString());
1853 |     }
1854 |   }

130 |     @Override
131 |     public int color() {
132 |       graph.clearNodeAnnotations();
133 |       List<GraphNode<N, E>> worklist = Lists.newArrayList(graph.getNodes());
134 | 
135 |       // Sort nodes by degree.
136 |       Collections.sort(worklist, new Comparator<GraphNode<N, E>>() {
137 |         @Override
138 |         public int compare(GraphNode<N, E> o1, GraphNode<N, E> o2) {
139 |           int result = graph.getWeight(o2.getValue())
140 |               - graph.getWeight(o1.getValue());
141 |           return result == 0 && tieBreaker != null ?
142 |               tieBreaker.compare(o1.getValue(), o2.getValue()) : result;
143 |         }
144 |       });
145 | 
146 |       // Idea: From the highest to lowest degree, assign any uncolored node with
147 |       // a unique color if none of its neighbor has been assigned that color.
148 |       int count = 0;
149 |       do {
150 |         Color color = new Color(count);
151 |         SubGraph<N, E> subgraph = graph.newSubGraph();
152 |         for (Iterator<GraphNode<N, E>> i = worklist.iterator(); i.hasNext();) {
153 |           GraphNode<N, E> node = i.next();
154 |           if (subgraph.isIndependentOf(node.getValue())) {
155 |             subgraph.addNode(node.getValue());
156 |             node.setAnnotation(color);
157 |             i.remove();
158 |           }
159 |         }
160 |         count++;
161 |       } while (!worklist.isEmpty());
162 |       @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
163 |       N[] map = (N[]) new Object[count];
164 |       colorToNodeMap = map;
165 |       return count;
166 |     }

     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first

462 |   private Node tryFoldAssign(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
463 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isAssign());
464 | 
465 |     if (!late) {
466 |       return n;
467 |     }
468 | 
469 |     // Tries to convert x = x + y -> x += y;
470 |     if (!right.hasChildren() ||
471 |         right.getFirstChild().getNext() != right.getLastChild()) {
472 |       // RHS must have two children.
473 |       return n;
474 |     }
475 | 
476 |     if (mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
477 |       return n;
478 |     }
479 | 
480 |     Node newRight;
481 |     if (areNodesEqualForInlining(left, right.getFirstChild())) {
482 |       newRight = right.getLastChild();
483 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isCommutative(right.getType()) &&
484 |           areNodesEqualForInlining(left, right.getLastChild())) {
485 |       newRight = right.getFirstChild();
486 |     } else {
487 |       return n;
488 |     }
489 | 
490 |     int newType = -1;
491 |     switch (right.getType()) {
492 |       case Token.ADD:
493 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_ADD;
494 |         break;
495 |       case Token.BITAND:
496 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITAND;
497 |         break;
498 |       case Token.BITOR:
499 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITOR;
500 |         break;
501 |       case Token.BITXOR:
502 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR;
503 |         break;
504 |       case Token.DIV:
505 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_DIV;
506 |         break;
507 |       case Token.LSH:
508 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_LSH;
509 |         break;
510 |       case Token.MOD:
511 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_MOD;
512 |         break;
513 |       case Token.MUL:
514 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_MUL;
515 |         break;
516 |       case Token.RSH:
517 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_RSH;
518 |         break;
519 |       case Token.SUB:
520 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_SUB;
521 |         break;
522 |       case Token.URSH:
523 |         newType = Token.ASSIGN_URSH;
524 |         break;
525 |       default:
526 |         return n;
527 |     }
528 | 
529 |     Node newNode = new Node(newType,
530 |         left.detachFromParent(), newRight.detachFromParent());
531 |     n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newNode);
532 | 
533 |     reportCodeChange();
534 |

===== M1761 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.EliminationPass.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 131-180
Documentation:
/**
     * Tries to remove n if it is an unconditional branch node (break, continue,
     * or return) and the target of n is the same as the the follow of n.
     * That is, if removing n preserves the control flow. Also if n targets
     * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to remove
     * the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this removal
     * is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
     *
     * break -> break -> break
     *
     * where all 3 breaks are useless, then the order of removal matters. When we
     * first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd break.
     * However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes useless and
     * finally the first break becomes useless as well.
     *
     * @return The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
     *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
     */
Method code:
131 |     @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
132 |     private Node tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
133 |       /*
134 |        * For each unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
135 |        * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
136 |        * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
137 |        *
138 |        * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
139 |        * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
140 |        * much more nicely.
141 |        */
142 | 
143 |       // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
144 |       if (n == null) {
145 |          return n;
146 |       }
147 | 
148 |       DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
149 | 
150 |       if (gNode == null) {
151 |         return n;
152 |       }
153 | 
154 |       switch (n.getType()) {
155 |         case Token.RETURN:
156 |           if (n.hasChildren()) {
157 |             break;
158 |           }
159 |         case Token.BREAK:
160 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
161 | 
162 |           // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
163 |           // branches to the same node. If after removing it control still
164 |           // branches to the same node, it is safe to remove.
165 |           List<DiGraphEdge<Node,Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
166 |           if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
167 |               // If there is a next node, there is no chance this jump is useless.
168 |               (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
169 | 
170 |             Preconditions.checkState(outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
171 |             Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
172 |             Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
173 |             if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
174 |               removeDeadExprStatementSafely(n);
175 |               return fallThrough;
176 |             }
177 |           }
178 |       }
179 |       return n;
180 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.computeEscaped(Scope,Set<Var>,AbstractCompiler)

Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in JavaScript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
555 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

Method code:
203 |   private boolean isConnectedInDirection(N n1, Predicate<E> edgeMatcher, N n2) {
204 |     // Verify the nodes.
205 |     DiGraphNode<N, E> dNode1 = getNodeOrFail(n1);
206 |     DiGraphNode<N, E> dNode2 = getNodeOrFail(n2);
207 |     for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> outEdge : dNode1.getOutEdges()) {
208 |       if (outEdge.getDestination() == dNode2 &&
209 |           edgeMatcher.apply(outEdge.getValue())) {
210 |         return true;
211 |       }
212 |     }
213 | 
214 |     return false;
215 |   }

   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getImpureBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.

136 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
137 | 
138 |       case Token.VOID:
139 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
140 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
141 |         }
142 |         break;
143 | 
144 |       case Token.NAME:
145 |         String name = n.getString();
146 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
147 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
148 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
149 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
150 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
151 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
152 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
153 |         }
154 |         break;
155 | 
156 |       case Token.TRUE:
157 |       case Token.REGEXP:
158 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
162 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
163 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
164 |         }
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
169 |   }

/**
   * Updates the scope according to the result of a type change, like
   * an assignment or a type cast.

Method code:
532 |   private void updateScopeForTypeChange(
533 |       FlowScope scope, Node left, JSType leftType, JSType resultType) {
534 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(resultType);
535 |     switch (left.getType()) {
536 |       case Token.NAME:
537 |         String varName = left.getString();
538 |         Var var = syntacticScope.getVar(varName);
539 | 
540 |         // When looking at VAR initializers for declared VARs, we trust
541 |         // the declared type over the type it's being initialized to.
542 |         // This has two purposes:
543 |         // 1) We avoid re-declaring declared variables so that built-in
544 |         //    types defined in externs are not redeclared.
545 |         // 2) When there's a lexical closure like
546 |         //    /** @type {?string} */ var x = null;
547 |         //    function f() { x = 'xyz'; }
548 |         //    the inference will ignore the lexical closure,
549 |         //    which is just wrong. This bug needs to be fixed eventually.
550 |         boolean isVarDeclaration = left.hasChildren();
551 |         if (!isVarDeclaration || var == null || var.isTypeInferred()) {
552 |           redeclareSimpleVar(scope, left, resultType);
553 |         }
554 |         left.setJSType(isVarDeclaration || leftType == null ?
555 |             resultType : null);
556 | 
557 |         if (var != null && var.isTypeInferred()) {
558 |           JSType oldType = var.getType();
559 |           var.setType(oldType == null ?
560 |               resultType : oldType.getLeastSupertype(resultType));
561 |         }
562 |         break;
563 |       case Token.GETPROP:
564 |         String qualifiedName = left.getQualifiedName();
565 |         if (qualifiedName != null) {
566 |           scope.inferQualifiedSlot(left, qualifiedName,
567 |               leftType == null ? unknownType : leftType,
568 |               resultType);
569 |         }

210 |     @Override
211 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
212 |       if (!n.isName()) {
213 |         return;
214 |       }
215 | 
216 |       String name = n.getString();
217 | 
218 |       // Ignore anonymous functions
219 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
220 |         return;
221 |       }
222 | 
223 |       // Is this local or Global?
224 |       // Bleeding functions should be treated as part of their outer
225 |       // scope, because IE has bugs in how it handles bleeding
226 |       // functions.
227 |       Scope.Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
228 |       boolean local = (var != null) && var.isLocal() &&
229 |           (!var.scope.getParent().isGlobal() ||
230 |            !var.isBleedingFunction());
231 | 
232 |       // Are we renaming global variables?
233 |       if (!local && localRenamingOnly) {
234 |         reservedNames.add(name);
235 |         return;
236 |       }
237 | 
238 |       // Are we renaming function expression names?
239 |       if (preserveFunctionExpressionNames && var != null
240 |           && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(var.getParentNode())) {
241 |         reservedNames.add(name);
242 |         return;
243 |       }
244 | 
245 |       // Check if we can rename this.
246 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
247 |         if (local) {
248 |           // Blindly de-uniquify for the Prototype library for issue 103.
249 |           String newName = MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter
250 |               .getOrginalName(name);
251 |           if (!newName.equals(name)) {
252 |             n.setString(newName);
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 |       }
257 | 
258 |       if (isExternsPass_) {
259 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
260 |         if (!local) {
261 |           externNames.add(name);
262 |         }
263 |         return;
264 |       }
265 | 
266 |       if (pseudoNameMap != null) {
267 |         recordPseudoName(n);
268 |       }
269 | 
270 |       if (local) {
271 |         // Local var: assign a new name
272 |         String tempName = LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX + getLocalVarIndex(var);
273 |         incCount(tempName);
274 |         localNameNodes.add(n);
275 |         n.setString(tempName);
276 |       } else if (var != null) { // Not an extern

214 |     if (callTarget != null && callTarget.isName() &&
215 |           callTarget.getString().equals("String")) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var,ReferenceCollection)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 683-733
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether the reference collection describes a variable that
     * is initialized to an immutable value, never modified, and defined before
     * every reference.
     */
Method code:
683 |     private boolean isImmutableAndWellDefinedVariable(Var v,
684 |         ReferenceCollection refInfo) {
685 |       List<Reference> refSet = refInfo.references;
686 |       int startingReadRef = 1;
687 |       Reference refDecl = refSet.get(0);
688 |       if (!isValidDeclaration(refDecl)) {
689 |         return false;
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       boolean isNeverAssigned = refInfo.isNeverAssigned();
693 |       // For values that are never assigned, only the references need to be
694 |       // checked.
695 |       if (!isNeverAssigned) {
696 |         Reference refInit = refInfo.getInitializingReference();
697 |         if (!isValidInitialization(refInit)) {
698 |           return false;
699 |         }
700 | 
701 |         if (refDecl != refInit) {
702 |           Preconditions.checkState(refInit == refSet.get(1));
703 |           startingReadRef = 2;
704 |         }
705 | 
706 |         if (!refInfo.isWellDefined()) {
707 |           return false;
708 |         }
709 | 
710 |         Node value = refInit.getAssignedValue();
711 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(value);
712 | 
713 |         boolean isImmutableValueWorthInlining =
714 |             NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value) &&
715 |             (!value.isString() ||
716 |                 isStringWorthInlining(v, refInfo.references));
717 |         boolean isInlinableThisAlias =
718 |             value.isThis() &&
719 |             !refInfo.isEscaped();
720 |         if (!isImmutableValueWorthInlining && !isInlinableThisAlias) {
721 |           return false;
722 |         }
723 |       }
724 | 
725 |       for (int i = startingReadRef; i < refSet.size(); i++) {
726 |         Reference ref = refSet.get(i);
727 |         if (!isValidReference(ref)) {
728 |           return false;
729 |         }
730 |       }
731 | 
732 |       return true;
733 |     }

46 |   private boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (!block.isBlock()) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!c.isExprResult() && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:

70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;

743 |       node.addChildToBack(newName);
744 |       Node lp = newNode(Token.PARAM_LIST);
745 |       // The left paren's complicated because it's not represented by an
746 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
747 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
748 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
749 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
750 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
751 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
752 |       if (fnName != null) {
753 |         lp.setLineno(fnName.getLineno());
754 |       } else {
755 |         lp.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
756 |       }
757 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
758 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
759 | 
760 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
761 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
762 |         Node paramNode = transform(param);
763 |         // When in ideMode Rhino can generate a param list with only a single
764 |         // ErrorNode. This is transformed into an EMPTY node. Drop this node in
765 |         // ideMode to keep the AST in a valid state.
766 |         if (paramNode.isName()) {
767 |           lp.addChildToBack(paramNode);
768 |         } else {
769 |           // We expect this in ideMode or when there is an error handling
770 |           // destructuring parameter assignments which aren't supported
771 |           // (an error has already been reported).
772 |           Preconditions.checkState(
773 |               config.isIdeMode
774 |               || paramNode.isObjectLit()
775 |               || paramNode.isArrayLit());
776 |         }
777 |       }
778 |       node.addChildToBack(lp);
779 | 
780 |       Node bodyNode = transform(functionNode.getBody());
781 |       if (!bodyNode.isBlock()) {
782 |         // When in ideMode Rhino tries to parse some constructs the compiler
783 |         // doesn't support, repair it here. see Rhino's
784 |         // Parser#parseFunctionBodyExpr.
785 |         Preconditions.checkState(config.isIdeMode);
786 |         bodyNode = IR.block();
787 |       }
788 |       parseDirectives(bodyNode);
789 |       node.addChildToBack(bodyNode);
790 |      return node;
791 |     }

===== M1903 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ExploitAssigns.collapseAssignEqualTo(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ExploitAssigns.java
Original range: 108-199
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse the given assign expression into the expression directly
   * following it, if possible.
   *
   * @param expr The expression that may be moved.
   * @param exprParent The parent of {@code expr}.
   * @param value The value of this expression, expressed as a node. Each
   *     expression may have multiple values, so this function may be called
   *     multiple times for the same expression. For example,
   *     <code>
   *     a = true;
   *     </code>
   *     is equal to the name "a" and the boolean "true".
   * @return Whether the expression was collapsed successfully.
   */
Method code:
108 |   private boolean collapseAssignEqualTo(Node expr, Node exprParent,
109 |       Node value) {
110 |     Node assign = expr.getFirstChild();
111 |     Node parent = exprParent;
112 |     Node next = expr.getNext();
113 |     while (next != null) {
114 |       switch (next.getType()) {
115 |         case Token.AND:
116 |         case Token.OR:
117 |         case Token.HOOK:
118 |         case Token.IF:
119 |         case Token.RETURN:
120 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
121 |           // Dive down the left side
122 |           parent = next;
123 |           next = next.getFirstChild();
124 |           break;
125 | 
126 |         case Token.VAR:
127 |           if (next.getFirstChild().hasChildren()) {
128 |             parent = next.getFirstChild();
129 |             next = parent.getFirstChild();
130 |             break;
131 |           }
132 |           return false;
133 | 
134 |         case Token.GETPROP:
135 |         case Token.NAME:
136 |           if (next.isQualifiedName()) {
137 |             String nextName = next.getQualifiedName();
138 |             if (value.isQualifiedName() &&
139 |                 nextName.equals(value.getQualifiedName())) {
140 |               // If the previous expression evaluates to value of a
141 |               // qualified name, and that qualified name is used again
142 |               // shortly, then we can exploit the assign here.
143 | 
144 |               // Verify the assignment doesn't change its own value.
145 |               if (!isSafeReplacement(next, assign)) {
146 |                 return false;
147 |               }
148 | 
149 |               exprParent.removeChild(expr);
150 |               expr.removeChild(assign);
151 |               parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
152 |               return true;
153 |             }
154 |           }
155 |           return false;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.ASSIGN:
158 |           // Assigns are really tricky. In lots of cases, we want to inline
159 |           // into the right side of the assign. But the left side of the
160 |           // assign is evaluated first, and it may have convoluted logic:
161 |           //   a = null;
162 |           //   (a = b).c = null;
163 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign. Similarly:
164 |           //   a.b = null;
165 |           //   a.b.c = null;
166 |           // We don't want to exploit the first assign either.
167 |           //
168 |           // To protect against this, we simply only inline when the left side
169 |           // is guaranteed to evaluate to the same L-value no matter what.
170 |           Node leftSide = next.getFirstChild();
171 |           if (leftSide.isName() ||
172 |               leftSide.isGetProp() &&
173 |               leftSide.getFirstChild().isThis()) {
174 |             // Dive down the right side of the assign.
175 |             parent = next;
176 |             next = leftSide.getNext();
177 |             break;
178 |           } else {
179 |             return false;
180 |           }
181 | 
182 |         default:
183 |           if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(next)
184 |               && next.isEquivalentTo(value)) {
185 |             // If the r-value of the expr assign is an immutable value,
186 |             // and the value is used again shortly, then we can exploit
187 |             // the assign here.
188 |             exprParent.removeChild(expr);
189 |             expr.removeChild(assign);
190 |             parent.replaceChild(next, assign);
191 |             return true;
192 |           }
193 |           // Return without inlining a thing
194 |           return false;
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 | 
198 |     return false;
199 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1723-1766
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1723 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1724 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1725 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1726 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1727 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1728 |       // {?} - right curly
1729 |       // {?=} - equals
1730 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1731 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1732 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1733 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1734 |       // {Array.<?>} - greater than
1735 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1736 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1737 |       token = next();
1738 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1739 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1740 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1741 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1742 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1743 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE ||
1744 |           token == JsDocToken.GT) {
1745 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1746 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1747 |       }
1748 | 
1749 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1750 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1751 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1752 |     } else {
1753 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1754 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1755 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1756 |           next();
1757 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1758 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1759 |           next();
1760 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1761 |         }
1762 |       }
1763 | 
1764 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1765 |     }
1766 |   }

   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping

1340 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
1341 |     // unknown
1342 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
1343 |       return true;
1344 |     }
1345 |     // all type
1346 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
1347 |       return true;
1348 |     }
1349 |     // equality
1350 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
1351 |       return true;
1352 |     }
1353 |     // unions
1354 |     if (thatType.isUnionType()) {
1355 |       UnionType union = thatType.toMaybeUnionType();
1356 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
1357 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
1358 |           return true;
1359 |         }
1360 |       }
1361 |       return false;
1362 |     }
1363 | 
1364 |     // parameterized types.
1365 |     if (thisType.isParameterizedType()) {
1366 |       return thisType.toMaybeParameterizedType().isParameterizeSubtypeOf(
1367 |           thatType);
1368 |     }
1369 | 
1370 |     // proxy types
1371 |     if (thatType instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
1372 |       return thisType.isSubtype(
1373 |           ((ProxyObjectType) thatType).getReferencedTypeInternal());
1374 |     }
1375 |     return false;
1376 |   }

194 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
195 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
196 |               Node arg = left.getNext();

199 |                 if (dot == -1) {

201 |                 } else {
202 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
203 |                 }
204 |               }

206 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
207 |               List<String> typeDecls =

212 |                 }

220 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);

235 |         break;

239 |         // error. Hoisted functions will explode if they're provided.
240 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&

244 |           if (pn != null) {

247 |         }
248 |         break;
249 |

255 |           reportBadBaseClassUse(t, n, "May only be called directly.");
256 |         }
257 |         break;
258 |     }
259 |   }

     * Replace the provide statement.

892 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();

894 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);

Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
70 |   @Override
71 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
72 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
73 |       return false;
74 |     }
75 | 
76 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
77 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
78 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
79 |     if (pos >= 0) {
80 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
81 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
82 |         return false;
83 |       }
84 |     }
85 | 
86 |     return isConstantKey(name);
87 |   }

64 |     //
65 |     // In user-defined types, we would deal with this case by creating
66 |     // a NamedType with the name "Error" and then resolve it later.
67 |     //
68 |     // For native types, we don't really want the native types to
69 |     // depend on type-resolution. So we just set the return type manually
70 |     // at the end of construction.
71 |     //
72 |     // There's similar logic in JSTypeRegistry for Array and RegExp.
73 |     getInternalArrowType().returnType = getInstanceType();
74 |   }
