Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1609-1644
Documentation:
/**
   * ParamTypeExpressionAnnotation :=
   *     '{' OptionalParameterType '}' |
   *     '{' TopLevelTypeExpression '}' |
   *     '{' '...' TopLevelTypeExpression '}'
   *
   * OptionalParameterType :=
   *     TopLevelTypeExpression '='
   */
Method code:
1609 |   private Node parseParamTypeExpressionAnnotation(JsDocToken token) {
1610 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(token == JsDocToken.LC);
1611 | 
1612 |     skipEOLs();
1613 | 
1614 |     boolean restArg = false;
1615 |     token = next();
1616 |     if (token == JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS) {
1617 |       token = next();
1618 |       if (token == JsDocToken.RC) {
1619 |         // EMPTY represents the UNKNOWN type in the Type AST.
1620 |         return wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, IR.empty());
1621 |       }
1622 |       restArg = true;
1623 |     }
1624 | 
1625 |     Node typeNode = parseTopLevelTypeExpression(token);
1626 |     if (typeNode != null) {
1627 |       skipEOLs();
1628 |       if (restArg) {
1629 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.ELLIPSIS, typeNode);
1630 |       } else if (match(JsDocToken.EQUALS)) {
1631 |         next();
1632 |         skipEOLs();
1633 |         typeNode = wrapNode(Token.EQUALS, typeNode);
1634 |       }
1635 | 
1636 |       if (!match(JsDocToken.RC)) {
1637 |         reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.rc");
1638 |       } else {
1639 |         next();
1640 |       }
1641 |     }
1642 | 
1643 |     return typeNode;
1644 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.checkDeclaredPropertyInheritance(NodeTraversal,Node,FunctionType,String,JSDocInfo,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 1150-1268
Documentation:
/**
   * Given a constructor type and a property name, check that the property has
   * the JSDoc annotation @override iff the property is declared on a
   * superclass. Several checks regarding inheritance correctness are also
   * performed.
   */
Method code:
1150 |   private void checkDeclaredPropertyInheritance(
1151 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n, FunctionType ctorType, String propertyName,
1152 |       JSDocInfo info, JSType propertyType) {
1153 |     // If the supertype doesn't resolve correctly, we've warned about this
1154 |     // already.
1155 |     if (hasUnknownOrEmptySupertype(ctorType)) {
1156 |       return;
1157 |     }
1158 | 
1159 |     FunctionType superClass = ctorType.getSuperClassConstructor();
1160 |     boolean superClassHasProperty = superClass != null &&
1161 |         superClass.getInstanceType().hasProperty(propertyName);
1162 |     boolean superClassHasDeclaredProperty = superClass != null &&
1163 |         superClass.getInstanceType().isPropertyTypeDeclared(propertyName);
1164 | 
1165 |     // For interface
1166 |     boolean superInterfaceHasProperty = false;
1167 |     boolean superInterfaceHasDeclaredProperty = false;
1168 |     if (ctorType.isInterface()) {
1169 |       for (ObjectType interfaceType : ctorType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1170 |         superInterfaceHasProperty =
1171 |             superInterfaceHasProperty ||
1172 |             interfaceType.hasProperty(propertyName);
1173 |         superInterfaceHasDeclaredProperty =
1174 |             superInterfaceHasDeclaredProperty ||
1175 |             interfaceType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propertyName);
1176 |       }
1177 |     }
1178 |     boolean declaredOverride = info != null && info.isOverride();
1179 | 
1180 |     boolean foundInterfaceProperty = false;
1181 |     if (ctorType.isConstructor()) {
1182 |       for (JSType implementedInterface :
1183 |           ctorType.getAllImplementedInterfaces()) {
1184 |         if (implementedInterface.isUnknownType() ||
1185 |             implementedInterface.isEmptyType()) {
1186 |           continue;
1187 |         }
1188 |         FunctionType interfaceType =
1189 |             implementedInterface.toObjectType().getConstructor();
1190 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(interfaceType);
1191 | 
1192 |         boolean interfaceHasProperty =
1193 |             interfaceType.getPrototype().hasProperty(propertyName);
1194 |         foundInterfaceProperty = foundInterfaceProperty ||
1195 |             interfaceHasProperty;
1196 |         if (reportMissingOverride.isOn()
1197 |             && !declaredOverride
1198 |             && interfaceHasProperty) {
1199 |           // @override not present, but the property does override an interface
1200 |           // property
1201 |           compiler.report(t.makeError(n, reportMissingOverride,
1202 |               HIDDEN_INTERFACE_PROPERTY, propertyName,
1203 |               interfaceType.getTopMostDefiningType(propertyName).toString()));
1204 |         }
1205 |       }
1206 |     }
1207 | 
1208 |     if (!declaredOverride
1209 |         && !superClassHasProperty
1210 |         && !superInterfaceHasProperty) {
1211 |       // nothing to do here, it's just a plain new property
1212 |       return;
1213 |     }
1214 | 
1215 |     ObjectType topInstanceType = superClassHasDeclaredProperty ?
1216 |         superClass.getTopMostDefiningType(propertyName) : null;
1217 |     boolean declaredLocally =
1218 |         ctorType.isConstructor() &&
1219 |         (ctorType.getPrototype().hasOwnProperty(propertyName) ||
1220 |          ctorType.getInstanceType().hasOwnProperty(propertyName));
1221 |     if (reportMissingOverride.isOn()
1222 |         && !declaredOverride
1223 |         && superClassHasDeclaredProperty
1224 |         && declaredLocally) {
1225 |       // @override not present, but the property does override a superclass
1226 |       // property
1227 |       compiler.report(t.makeError(n, reportMissingOverride,
1228 |           HIDDEN_SUPERCLASS_PROPERTY, propertyName,
1229 |           topInstanceType.toString()));
1230 |     }
1231 | 
1232 |     // @override is present and we have to check that it is ok
1233 |     if (superClassHasDeclaredProperty) {
1234 |       // there is a superclass implementation
1235 |       JSType superClassPropType =
1236 |           superClass.getInstanceType().getPropertyType(propertyName);
1237 |       if (!propertyType.isSubtype(superClassPropType)) {
1238 |         compiler.report(
1239 |             t.makeError(n, HIDDEN_SUPERCLASS_PROPERTY_MISMATCH,
1240 |                 propertyName, topInstanceType.toString(),
1241 |                 superClassPropType.toString(), propertyType.toString()));
1242 |       }
1243 |     } else if (superInterfaceHasDeclaredProperty) {
1244 |       // there is an super interface property
1245 |       for (ObjectType interfaceType : ctorType.getExtendedInterfaces()) {
1246 |         if (interfaceType.hasProperty(propertyName)) {
1247 |           JSType superPropertyType =
1248 |               interfaceType.getPropertyType(propertyName);
1249 |           if (!propertyType.isSubtype(superPropertyType)) {
1250 |             topInstanceType = interfaceType.getConstructor().
1251 |                 getTopMostDefiningType(propertyName);
1252 |             compiler.report(
1253 |                 t.makeError(n, HIDDEN_SUPERCLASS_PROPERTY_MISMATCH,
1254 |                     propertyName, topInstanceType.toString(),
1255 |                     superPropertyType.toString(),
1256 |                     propertyType.toString()));
1257 |           }
1258 |         }
1259 |       }
1260 |     } else if (!foundInterfaceProperty
1261 |         && !superClassHasProperty
1262 |         && !superInterfaceHasProperty) {
1263 |       // there is no superclass nor interface implementation
1264 |       compiler.report(
1265 |           t.makeError(n, UNKNOWN_OVERRIDE,
1266 |               propertyName, ctorType.getInstanceType().toString()));
1267 |     }
1268 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ArrowType.hasEqualParameters(ArrowType,EquivalenceMethod)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/ArrowType.java
Original range: 177-211
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if our parameter spec is equal to {@code that}'s parameter
   *     spec.
   */
Method code:
177 |   boolean hasEqualParameters(ArrowType that, EquivalenceMethod eqMethod) {
178 |     Node thisParam = parameters.getFirstChild();
179 |     Node otherParam = that.parameters.getFirstChild();
180 |     while (thisParam != null && otherParam != null) {
181 |       JSType thisParamType = thisParam.getJSType();
182 |       JSType otherParamType = otherParam.getJSType();
183 |       if (thisParamType != null) {
184 |         // Both parameter lists give a type for this param, it should be equal
185 |         if (otherParamType != null &&
186 |             !thisParamType.checkEquivalenceHelper(
187 |                 otherParamType, eqMethod)) {
188 |           return false;
189 |         }
190 |       } else {
191 |         if (otherParamType != null) {
192 |           return false;
193 |         }
194 |       }
195 | 
196 |       // Check var_args/optionality
197 |       if (thisParam.isOptionalArg() != otherParam.isOptionalArg()) {
198 |         return false;
199 |       }
200 | 
201 |       if (thisParam.isVarArgs() != otherParam.isVarArgs()) {
202 |         return false;
203 |       }
204 | 
205 |       thisParam = thisParam.getNext();
206 |       otherParam = otherParam.getNext();
207 |     }
208 |     // One of the parameters is null, so the types are only equal if both
209 |     // parameter lists are null (they are equal).
210 |     return thisParam == otherParam;
211 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 133-153
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 1 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. The passes will run until they are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * The PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and frequency of multi-run
   * passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
133 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
134 |     Loop currentLoop = new Loop();
135 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
136 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
137 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
138 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
139 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
140 |           currentLoop = new Loop();
141 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
142 |         }
143 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
144 |       } else {
145 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
146 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
147 |       }
148 |     }
149 | 
150 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
151 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
152 |     }
153 |   }

===== M2020 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 189-301
Documentation:

Method code:
189 |   @Override
190 |   @SuppressWarnings({"fallthrough", "incomplete-switch"})
191 |   List<FlowScope> branchedFlowThrough(Node source, FlowScope input) {
192 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, we just treat ON_EX edges like UNCOND
193 |     // edges. If we wanted to be perfect, we'd actually JOIN all the out
194 |     // lattices of this flow with the in lattice, and then make that the out
195 |     // lattice for the ON_EX edge. But it's probably to expensive to be
196 |     // worthwhile.
197 |     FlowScope output = flowThrough(source, input);
198 |     Node condition = null;
199 |     FlowScope conditionFlowScope = null;
200 |     BooleanOutcomePair conditionOutcomes = null;
201 | 
202 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> branchEdges = getCfg().getOutEdges(source);
203 |     List<FlowScope> result = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(branchEdges.size());
204 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> branchEdge : branchEdges) {
205 |       Branch branch = branchEdge.getValue();
206 |       FlowScope newScope = output;
207 | 
208 |       switch (branch) {
209 |         case ON_TRUE:
210 |           if (NodeUtil.isForIn(source)) {
211 |             // item is assigned a property name, so its type should be string.
212 |             Node item = source.getFirstChild();
213 |             Node obj = item.getNext();
214 | 
215 |             FlowScope informed = traverse(obj, output.createChildFlowScope());
216 | 
217 |             if (item.isVar()) {
218 |               item = item.getFirstChild();
219 |             }
220 |             if (item.isName()) {
221 |               JSType iterKeyType = getNativeType(STRING_TYPE);
222 |               ObjectType objType = getJSType(obj).dereference();
223 |               JSType objIndexType = objType == null ?
224 |                   null : objType.getIndexType();
225 |               if (objIndexType != null && !objIndexType.isUnknownType()) {
226 |                 JSType narrowedKeyType =
227 |                     iterKeyType.getGreatestSubtype(objIndexType);
228 |                 if (!narrowedKeyType.isEmptyType()) {
229 |                   iterKeyType = narrowedKeyType;
230 |                 }
231 |               }
232 |               redeclareSimpleVar(informed, item, iterKeyType);
233 |             }
234 |             newScope = informed;
235 |             break;
236 |           }
237 | 
238 |           // FALL THROUGH
239 | 
240 |         case ON_FALSE:
241 |           if (condition == null) {
242 |             condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(source);
243 |             if (condition == null && source.isCase()) {
244 |               condition = source;
245 | 
246 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
247 |               // of the loop.
248 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
249 |                 conditionFlowScope = traverse(
250 |                     condition.getFirstChild(), output.createChildFlowScope());
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 | 
255 |           if (condition != null) {
256 |             if (condition.isAnd() ||
257 |                 condition.isOr()) {
258 |               // When handling the short-circuiting binary operators,
259 |               // the outcome scope on true can be different than the outcome
260 |               // scope on false.
261 |               //
262 |               // TODO(nicksantos): The "right" way to do this is to
263 |               // carry the known outcome all the way through the
264 |               // recursive traversal, so that we can construct a
265 |               // different flow scope based on the outcome. However,
266 |               // this would require a bunch of code and a bunch of
267 |               // extra computation for an edge case. This seems to be
268 |               // a "good enough" approximation.
269 | 
270 |               // conditionOutcomes is cached from previous iterations
271 |               // of the loop.
272 |               if (conditionOutcomes == null) {
273 |                 conditionOutcomes = condition.isAnd() ?
274 |                     traverseAnd(condition, output.createChildFlowScope()) :
275 |                     traverseOr(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
276 |               }
277 |               newScope =
278 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
279 |                       condition,
280 |                       conditionOutcomes.getOutcomeFlowScope(
281 |                           condition.getType(), branch == Branch.ON_TRUE),
282 |                       branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
283 |             } else {
284 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
285 |               // of the loop.
286 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
287 |                 conditionFlowScope =
288 |                     traverse(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
289 |               }
290 |               newScope =
291 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
292 |                       condition, conditionFlowScope, branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
293 |             }
294 |           }
295 |           break;
296 |       }
297 | 
298 |       result.add(newScope.optimize());
299 |     }
300 |     return result;
301 |   }

77 |       return;

83 |     }

86 |     // at least one inner function because in most browsers, when there is a

351 |     assignNames(varsByFrequency);

359 |       if (newName != null) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1870-1887
Documentation:
/**
   * Merge a block with its parent block.
   * @return Whether the block was removed.
   */
Method code:
1870 |   static boolean tryMergeBlock(Node block) {
1871 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.isBlock());
1872 |     Node parent = block.getParent();
1873 |     // Try to remove the block if its parent is a block/script or if its
1874 |     // parent is label and it has exactly one child.
1875 |     if (isStatementBlock(parent)) {
1876 |       Node previous = block;
1877 |       while (block.hasChildren()) {
1878 |         Node child = block.removeFirstChild();
1879 |         parent.addChildAfter(child, previous);
1880 |         previous = child;
1881 |       }
1882 |       parent.removeChild(block);
1883 |       return true;
1884 |     } else {
1885 |       return false;
1886 |     }
1887 |   }

===== M2070 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

/**
   * Performs the line-by-line parsing of the given fileContents. This method
   * strips out JavaScript comments and then uses the abstract parseLine()
   * method to do the line parsing.
   *
   * @param filePath The path to the file being parsed. Used for reporting parse
   *     exceptions.
   * @param fileContents A reader for the contents of the file.
   */
Method code:
119 |   void doParse(String filePath, Reader fileContents) {
120 |     this.filePath = filePath;
121 |     parseSucceeded = true;
122 | 
123 |     BufferedReader lineBuffer = new BufferedReader(fileContents);
124 | 
125 |     // Parse all lines.
126 |     String line = null;
127 |     lineNum = 0;
128 |     boolean inMultilineComment = false;
129 | 
130 |     try {
131 |       while (null != (line = lineBuffer.readLine())) {
132 |         ++lineNum;
133 |         try {
134 |           String revisedLine = line;
135 |           if (inMultilineComment) {
136 |             int endOfComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/");
137 |             if (endOfComment != -1) {
138 |               revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(endOfComment + 2);
139 |               inMultilineComment = false;
140 |             } else {
141 |               revisedLine = "";
142 |             }
143 |           }
144 | 
145 |           if (!inMultilineComment) {
146 |             while (true) {
147 |               int startOfLineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("//");
148 |               int startOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("/*");
149 |               if (startOfLineComment != -1 &&
150 |                   (startOfMultilineComment == -1 ||
151 |                    startOfLineComment < startOfMultilineComment)) {
152 |                 revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(0, startOfLineComment);
153 |                 break;
154 |               } else if (startOfMultilineComment != -1) {
155 |                 int endOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/",
156 |                     startOfMultilineComment + 2);
157 |                 if (endOfMultilineComment == -1) {
158 |                   revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(
159 |                       0, startOfMultilineComment);
160 |                   inMultilineComment = true;
161 |                   break;
162 |                 } else {
163 |                   revisedLine =
164 |                       revisedLine.substring(0, startOfMultilineComment) +
165 |                       revisedLine.substring(endOfMultilineComment + 2);
166 |                 }
167 |               } else {
168 |                 break;
169 |               }
170 |             }
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           if (!revisedLine.isEmpty()) {
174 |             // This check for shortcut mode should be redundant, but
175 |             // it's done for safety reasons.
176 |             if (!parseLine(revisedLine) && shortcutMode) {
177 |               break;
178 |             }
179 |           }
180 |         } catch (ParseException e) {
181 |           // Inform the error handler of the exception.
182 |           errorManager.report(
183 |               e.isFatal() ? CheckLevel.ERROR : CheckLevel.WARNING,
184 |               JSError.make(filePath, lineNum, 0 /* char offset */,
185 |                   e.isFatal() ? PARSE_ERROR : PARSE_WARNING,
186 |                   e.getMessage(), line));
187 |           parseSucceeded = parseSucceeded && !e.isFatal();
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (IOException e) {
191 |       errorManager.report(CheckLevel.ERROR,
192 |           JSError.make(filePath, 0, 0 /* char offset */,
193 |               PARSE_ERROR, "Error reading file: " + filePath));
194 |       parseSucceeded = false;
195 |     }
196 |   }

/**
     * Users may specify JS inputs via the legacy {@code --js} option, as well
     * as via additional arguments to the Closure Compiler. For example, it is
     * convenient to leverage the additional arguments feature when using the
     * Closure Compiler in combination with {@code find} and {@code xargs}:
     * <pre>
     * find MY_JS_SRC_DIR -name '*.js' \
     *     | xargs java -jar compiler.jar --manage_closure_dependencies
     * </pre>
     * The {@code find} command will produce a list of '*.js' source files in
     * the {@code MY_JS_SRC_DIR} directory while {@code xargs} will convert them
     * to a single, space-delimited set of arguments that are appended to the
     * {@code java} command to run the Compiler.

     * Note that it is important to use the
     * {@code --manage_closure_dependencies} option in this case because the
     * order produced by {@code find} is unlikely to be sorted correctly with
     * respect to {@code goog.provide()} and {@code goog.requires()}.
     */

/**
   * Determines whether we know enough about the given value to be able
   * to collapse it into subsequent expressions.
   *
   * For example, we can collapse booleans and variable names:
   * <code>
   * x = 3; y = x; // y = x = 3;
   * a = true; b = true; // b = a = true;
   * <code>
   * But we won't try to collapse complex expressions.
   *
   * @param value The value node.
   * @param isLValue Whether it's on the left-hand side of an expr.
   */
Method code:
76 |   private boolean isCollapsibleValue(Node value, boolean isLValue) {
77 |     switch (value.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.GETPROP:
79 |         // Do not collapse GETPROPs on arbitrary objects, because
80 |         // they may be implemented setter functions, and oftentimes
81 |         // setter functions fail on native objects. This is OK for "THIS"
82 |         // objects, because we assume that they are non-native.
83 |         return !isLValue || value.getFirstChild().isThis();
84 | 
85 |       case Token.NAME:
86 |         return true;
87 | 
88 |       default:
89 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value);
90 |     }
91 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VariableReferenceCheck.ReferenceCheckingBehavior.checkVar(NodeTraversal,Var,List<Reference>)

Original range: 104-197
Documentation:
/**
     * If the variable is declared more than once in a basic block, generate a
     * warning. Also check if a variable is used in a given scope before it is
     * declared, which suggest a likely error. Relies on the fact that
     * references is in parse-tree order.
     */
Method code:
104 |     private void checkVar(NodeTraversal t, Var v, List<Reference> references) {
105 |       blocksWithDeclarations.clear();
106 |       boolean isDeclaredInScope = false;
107 |       boolean isUnhoistedNamedFunction = false;
108 |       Reference hoistedFn = null;
109 | 
110 |       // Look for hoisted functions.
111 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
112 |         if (reference.isHoistedFunction()) {
113 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(reference.getBasicBlock());
114 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
115 |           hoistedFn = reference;
116 |           break;
117 |         } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(
118 |             reference.getNode().getParent())) {
119 |           isUnhoistedNamedFunction = true;
120 |         }
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       for (Reference reference : references) {
124 |         if (reference == hoistedFn) {
125 |           continue;
126 |         }
127 | 
128 |         BasicBlock basicBlock = reference.getBasicBlock();
129 |         boolean isDeclaration = reference.isDeclaration();
130 | 
131 |         boolean allowDupe =
132 |             SyntacticScopeCreator.hasDuplicateDeclarationSuppression(
133 |                 reference.getNode(), v);
134 |         if (isDeclaration && !allowDupe) {
135 |           // Look through all the declarations we've found so far, and
136 |           // check if any of them are before this block.
137 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
138 |             if (declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
139 |               // TODO(johnlenz): Fix AST generating clients that so they would
140 |               // have property StaticSourceFile attached at each node. Or
141 |               // better yet, make sure the generated code never violates
142 |               // the requirement to pass aggressive var check!
143 |               String filename = NodeUtil.getSourceName(reference.getNode());
144 |               compiler.report(
145 |                   JSError.make(filename,
146 |                       reference.getNode(),
147 |                       checkLevel,
148 |                       REDECLARED_VARIABLE, v.name));
149 |               break;
150 |             }
151 |           }
152 |         }
153 | 
154 |         if (isUnhoistedNamedFunction && !isDeclaration && isDeclaredInScope) {
155 |           // Only allow an unhoisted named function to be used within the
156 |           // block it is declared.
157 |           for (BasicBlock declaredBlock : blocksWithDeclarations) {
158 |             if (!declaredBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(basicBlock)) {
159 |               String filename = NodeUtil.getSourceName(reference.getNode());
160 |               compiler.report(
161 |                   JSError.make(filename,
162 |                       reference.getNode(),
163 |                       AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_DECL, v.name));
164 |               break;
165 |             }
166 |           }
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         if (!isDeclaration && !isDeclaredInScope) {
170 |           // Don't check the order of refer in externs files.
171 |           if (!reference.getNode().isFromExterns()) {
172 |             // Special case to deal with var goog = goog || {}
173 |             Node grandparent = reference.getGrandparent();
174 |             if (grandparent.isName()
175 |                 && grandparent.getString() == v.name) {
176 |               continue;
177 |             }
178 | 
179 |             // Only generate warnings if the scopes do not match in order
180 |             // to deal with possible forward declarations and recursion
181 |             if (reference.getScope() == v.scope) {
182 |               String filename = NodeUtil.getSourceName(reference.getNode());
183 |               compiler.report(
184 |                   JSError.make(filename,
185 |                                reference.getNode(),
186 |                                checkLevel,
187 |                                UNDECLARED_REFERENCE, v.name));
188 |             }
189 |           }
190 |         }
191 | 
192 |         if (isDeclaration) {
193 |           blocksWithDeclarations.add(basicBlock);
194 |           isDeclaredInScope = true;
195 |         }
196 |       }
197 |     }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 440-510
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
440 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
441 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
442 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
443 | 
444 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
445 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
446 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
447 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
448 | 
449 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
450 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
451 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
452 | 
453 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
454 |       if (a.newName != null) {
455 |         continue;
456 |       }
457 | 
458 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
459 |         continue;
460 |       }
461 | 
462 |       String newName;
463 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
464 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
465 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
466 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
467 |       } else {
468 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
469 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
470 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
471 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
472 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
473 |       }
474 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
475 |     }
476 | 
477 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
478 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
479 |     // follows:
480 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
481 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
482 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
483 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
484 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
485 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
486 |     //    compressible.
487 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
488 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
489 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
490 | 
491 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
492 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
493 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
494 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
495 | 
496 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
497 |       // generated names of the same length.
498 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
499 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
500 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
501 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
502 |       }
503 | 
504 |       // Now, make the assignments
505 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
506 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
507 |         ++i;
508 |       }
509 |     }
510 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 517-548
Documentation:
/**
   * Remove duplicate exits.  If the node following the exit node expression
   * has the same effect as exit node, the node can be removed.
   * For example:
   *   "if (a) {return f()} return f();" ==> "if (a) {} return f();"
   *   "if (a) {throw 'ow'} throw 'ow';" ==> "if (a) {} throw 'ow';"
   *
   * @param n An follow control exit expression (a THROW or RETURN node)
   * @return The replacement for n, or the original if no change was made.
   */
Method code:
517 |   private Node tryRemoveRedundantExit(Node n) {
518 |     Node exitExpr = n.getFirstChild();
519 | 
520 |     Node follow = ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(n);
521 | 
522 |     // Skip pass all the finally blocks because both the fall through and return
523 |     // will also trigger all the finally blocks.
524 |     Node prefinallyFollows = follow;
525 |     follow = skipFinallyNodes(follow);
526 |     if (prefinallyFollows != follow) {
527 |       // There were finally clauses
528 |       if (!isPure(exitExpr)) {
529 |         // Can't replace the return
530 |         return n;
531 |       }
532 |     }
533 | 
534 |     if (follow == null && (n.isThrow() || exitExpr != null)) {
535 |       // Can't complete remove a throw here or a return with a result.
536 |       return n;
537 |     }
538 | 
539 |     // When follow is null, this mean the follow of a break target is the
540 |     // end of a function. This means a break is same as return.
541 |     if (follow == null || areMatchingExits(n, follow)) {
542 |       n.detachFromParent();
543 |       reportCodeChange();
544 |       return null;
545 |     }
546 | 
547 |     return n;
548 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 830-857
Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }
837 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
838 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }
857 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CreateSyntheticBlocks.Callback.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CreateSyntheticBlocks.java
Original range: 169-215
Documentation:

Method code:
169 |     @Override
170 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
171 |       if (!n.isCall() || !n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
172 |         return;
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
176 |       String callName = callTarget.getString();
177 | 
178 |       if (startMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
179 |         if (!parent.isExprResult()) {
180 |           compiler.report(
181 |               t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, startMarkerName));
182 |           return;
183 |         }
184 |         markerStack.push(parent);
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       if (!endMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
189 |         return;
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       Node endMarkerNode = parent;
193 |       if (!endMarkerNode.isExprResult()) {
194 |         compiler.report(
195 |             t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, endMarkerName));
196 |         return;
197 |       }
198 | 
199 |       if (markerStack.isEmpty()) {
200 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
201 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
202 |         return;
203 |       }
204 | 
205 |       Node startMarkerNode = markerStack.pop();
206 |       if (endMarkerNode.getParent() != startMarkerNode.getParent()) {
207 |         // The end marker isn't in the same block as the start marker.
208 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
209 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
210 |         return;
211 |       }
212 | 
213 |       // This is a valid marker set add it to the list of markers to process.
214 |       validMarkers.add(new Marker(startMarkerNode, endMarkerNode));
215 |     }

/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * ECMA-262, Edition 5.
     *
     * It would be nice if Rhino would eventually take care of this for
     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.
     */
Method code:
553 |     private void parseDirectives(Node node) {
554 |       // Remove all the directives, and encode them in the AST.
555 |       Set<String> directives = null;
556 |       while (isDirective(node.getFirstChild())) {
557 |         String directive = node.removeFirstChild().getFirstChild().getString();
558 |         if (directives == null) {
559 |           directives = Sets.newHashSet(directive);
560 |         } else {
561 |           directives.add(directive);
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 | 
565 |       if (directives != null) {
566 |         node.setDirectives(directives);
567 |       }
568 |     }

1647 |       }

1655 |                           "interface", functionPrivateName));

547 |   private boolean addParameter(FunctionParamBuilder builder,
548 |       JSType paramType, boolean warnedAboutArgList,

550 |     boolean emittedWarning = false;
551 |     if (isOptional) {

/**
   * Try to minimize NOT nodes such as !(x==y).
   *
   * Returns the replacement for n or the original if no change was made
   */

600 |   private Node tryMinimizeNot(Node n) {
601 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
602 | 
603 |     Node notChild = n.getFirstChild();
604 |     // negative operator of the current one : == -> != for instance.
605 |     int complementOperator;

620 |       default:

===== M2276 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.topologicalStableSort(List<T>,Multimap<T, T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java
Original range: 239-288
Documentation:

Method code:
239 |   private static <T> List<T> topologicalStableSort(
240 |       List<T> items, Multimap<T, T> deps) {
241 |     if (items.size() == 0) {
242 |       // Priority queue blows up if we give it a size of 0. Since we need
243 |       // to special case this either way, just bail out.
244 |       return Lists.newArrayList();
245 |     }
246 | 
247 |     final Map<T, Integer> originalIndex = Maps.newHashMap();
248 |     for (int i = 0; i < items.size(); i++) {
249 |       originalIndex.put(items.get(i), i);
250 |     }
251 | 
252 |     PriorityQueue<T> inDegreeZero = new PriorityQueue<T>(items.size(),
253 |         new Comparator<T>() {
254 |       @Override
255 |       public int compare(T a, T b) {
256 |         return originalIndex.get(a).intValue() -
257 |             originalIndex.get(b).intValue();
258 |       }
259 |     });
260 |     List<T> result = Lists.newArrayList();
261 | 
262 |     Multiset<T> inDegree = HashMultiset.create();
263 |     Multimap<T, T> reverseDeps = ArrayListMultimap.create();
264 |     Multimaps.invertFrom(deps, reverseDeps);
265 | 
266 |     // First, add all the inputs with in-degree 0.
267 |     for (T item : items) {
268 |       Collection<T> itemDeps = deps.get(item);
269 |       inDegree.add(item, itemDeps.size());
270 |       if (itemDeps.isEmpty()) {
271 |         inDegreeZero.add(item);
272 |       }
273 |     }
274 | 
275 |     // Then, iterate to a fixed point over the reverse dependency graph.
276 |     while (!inDegreeZero.isEmpty()) {
277 |       T item = inDegreeZero.remove();
278 |       result.add(item);
279 |       for (T inWaiting : reverseDeps.get(item)) {
280 |         inDegree.remove(inWaiting, 1);
281 |         if (inDegree.count(inWaiting) == 0) {
282 |           inDegreeZero.add(inWaiting);
283 |         }
284 |       }
285 |     }
286 | 
287 |     return result;
288 |   }

587 |       // 1) If we infer the return type of f too widely, then we won't be able

589 |       // 2) If we infer the return type of f too narrowly, then we won't be
590 |       //    able to override f in subclasses.
591 |       // So we only infer in cases where the user doesn't expect to write
592 |       // @return annotations--when it's very obvious that the function returns
593 |       // nothing.
594 |       if (!contents.mayHaveNonEmptyReturns() &&
595 |           !contents.mayHaveSingleThrow() &&
596 |           !contents.mayBeFromExterns()) {
597 |         returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
598 |         returnTypeInferred = true;
599 |       }
600 |     }
601 | 
602 |     if (returnType == null) {
603 |       returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
604 |     }
605 | 
606 |     if (parametersNode == null) {
607 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
608 |           "All Function types must have params and a return type");
609 |     }
610 | 
611 |     FunctionType fnType;
612 |     if (isConstructor) {
613 |       fnType = getOrCreateConstructor();
614 |     } else if (isInterface) {
615 |       fnType = typeRegistry.createInterfaceType(
616 |           fnName, contents.getSourceNode());
617 |       if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
618 |         typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
619 |       }
620 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
621 |     } else {
622 |       fnType = new FunctionBuilder(typeRegistry)
623 |           .withName(fnName)
624 |           .withSourceNode(contents.getSourceNode())
625 |           .withParamsNode(parametersNode)
626 |           .withReturnType(returnType, returnTypeInferred)
627 |           .withTypeOfThis(thisType)
628 |           .withTemplateKeys(templateTypeNames)
629 |           .build();
630 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
631 |     }
632 | 
633 |     if (implementedInterfaces != null) {
634 |       fnType.setImplementedInterfaces(implementedInterfaces);
635 |     }
636 | 
637 |     if (extendedInterfaces != null) {
638 |       fnType.setExtendedInterfaces(extendedInterfaces);
639 |     }
640 | 
641 |     typeRegistry.clearTemplateTypeNames();
642 | 
643 |     return fnType;
644 |   }

   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.

Method code:
120 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
121 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
122 |     // just bail out early here.
123 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
124 |       return this;
125 |     }
126 | 
127 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
128 | 
129 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
130 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
131 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
132 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
133 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
134 |     }
135 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
136 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
137 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
138 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
139 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
140 |         }
141 |       } else {
142 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
143 |           return this;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
147 |         // own bizarre sub-lattice. See the comments on
148 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
149 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
150 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
151 |           FunctionType other =
152 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
153 |           FunctionType supremum =
154 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
155 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
156 |           result = null;
157 |           return this;
158 |         }
159 | 
160 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
161 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
162 |         // one another.
163 |         int currentIndex = 0;
164 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
165 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
166 |           boolean removeCurrent = false;
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType() ||
176 |               alternate.hasAnyTemplateTypes() ||
177 |               current.hasAnyTemplateTypes()) {
178 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
179 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
180 |               return this;
181 |             }
182 |           } else {
183 | 
184 |             // Because "Foo" and "Foo.<?>" are roughly equivalent
185 |             // parameterized types, special care is needed when building the
186 |             // union. For example:
187 |             //   Object is consider a subtype of Object.<string>
188 |             // but we want to leave "Object" not "Object.<string>" when
189 |             // building the subtype.
190 |             //
191 | 
192 |             if (alternate.isParameterizedType() || current.isParameterizedType()) {
193 |               // Cases:
194 |               // 1) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Object ==> Object
195 |               // 2) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Array ==> Array
196 |               // 3) alternate:Object.<string> and
197 |               //    current:Array ==> Array|Object.<string>
198 |               // 4) alternate:Object and current:Array.<string> ==> Object
199 |               // 5) alternate:Array and current:Array.<string> ==> Array
200 |               // 6) alternate:Array and
201 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Array|Object.<string>
202 |               // 7) alternate:Array.<string> and
203 |               //    current:Array.<number> ==> Array.<?>
204 |               // 8) alternate:Array.<string> and
205 |               //    current:Array.<string> ==> Array.<string>
206 |               // 9) alternate:Array.<string> and
207 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Object.<string>|Array.<string>
208 | 
209 |               if (!current.isParameterizedType()) {
210 |                 if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
211 |                   // case 1, 2
212 |                   return this;
213 |                 }
214 |                 // case 3: leave current, add alternate
215 |               } else if (!alternate.isParameterizedType()) {
216 |                 if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
217 |                   // case 4, 5
218 |                   removeCurrent = true;
219 |                 }
220 |                 // case 6: leave current, add alternate
221 |               } else {
222 |                 Preconditions.checkState(current.isParameterizedType()
223 |                     && alternate.isParameterizedType());
224 |                 ParameterizedType parameterizedAlternate = alternate.toMaybeParameterizedType();
225 |                 ParameterizedType parameterizedCurrent = current.toMaybeParameterizedType();
226 | 
227 |                 if (parameterizedCurrent.wrapsSameRawType(parameterizedAlternate)) {
228 |                   JSType alternateTypeParameter = parameterizedAlternate.getParameterType();
229 |                   JSType currentTypeParameter = parameterizedCurrent.getParameterType();
230 |                   if (currentTypeParameter.isEquivalentTo(parameterizedCurrent)) {
231 |                     // case 8
232 |                     return this;
233 |                   } else {
234 |                     // TODO(johnlenz): should we leave both types?
235 |                     // case 7: add a merged alternate
236 |                     // We currently merge to the parameterized types to "unknown"
237 |                     // which is equivalent to the raw type.
238 |                     JSType merged = parameterizedCurrent
239 |                         .getReferencedObjTypeInternal();
240 |                     return addAlternate(merged);
241 |                   }
242 |                 }
243 |                 // case 9: leave current, add alternate
244 |               }
245 |               // Otherwise leave both parameterized types.
246 |             } else if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
247 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
248 |               return this;
249 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
250 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
251 |               removeCurrent = true;
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 | 
255 |           if (removeCurrent) {
256 |             it.remove();
257 | 
258 |             if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
259 |               functionTypePosition = -1;
260 |             } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
261 |               functionTypePosition--;
262 |               currentIndex--;
263 |             }
264 |           }
265 |           currentIndex++;
266 |         }
267 | 
268 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
269 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
270 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
271 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
272 |         }
273 | 
274 |         alternates.add(alternate);
275 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
276 |       }
277 |     } else {
278 |       result = null;
279 |     }
280 |     return this;
281 |   }

/**
   * @returns false iff the result of the expression is not consumed.
   */
Method code:
3149 |   static boolean isExpressionResultUsed(Node expr) {
3150 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider sharing some code with trySimpleUnusedResult.
3151 |     Node parent = expr.getParent();
3152 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
3153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
3154 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
3155 |         return false;
3156 |       case Token.CAST:
3157 |         return isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3158 |       case Token.HOOK:
3159 |       case Token.AND:
3160 |       case Token.OR:
3161 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3162 |             ? true : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3163 |       case Token.COMMA:
3164 |         Node gramps = parent.getParent();
3165 |         if (gramps.isCall() &&
3166 |             parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
3167 |           // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
3168 |           // call to an eval. See ECMA-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's OK for the first
3169 |           // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
3170 |           // an eval. This we pretend that this is "used".
3171 |           if (expr == parent.getFirstChild() &&
3172 |               parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
3173 |               expr.getNext().isName() &&
3174 |               "eval".equals(expr.getNext().getString())) {
3175 |             return true;
3176 |           }
3177 |         }
3178 | 
3179 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3180 |             ? false : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3181 |       case Token.FOR:
3182 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
3183 |           // Only an expression whose result is in the condition part of the
3184 |           // expression is used.
3185 |           return (parent.getChildAtIndex(1) == expr);
3186 |         }
3187 |         break;
3188 |     }
3189 |     return true;
3190 |   }

/**
   * Expect the type to be anything but the null or void type. If the
   * expectation is not met, issue a warning at the provided node's
   * source code position. Note that a union type that includes the
   * void type and at least one other type meets the expectation.
   * @return Whether the expectation was met.
   */
Method code:
256 |   boolean expectNotNullOrUndefined(
257 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type, String msg, JSType expectedType) {
258 |     if (!type.isNoType() && !type.isUnknownType() &&
259 |         type.isSubtype(nullOrUndefined) &&
260 |         !containsForwardDeclaredUnresolvedName(type)) {
261 | 
262 |       // There's one edge case right now that we don't handle well, and
263 |       // that we don't want to warn about.
264 |       // if (this.x == null) {
265 |       //   this.initializeX();
266 |       //   this.x.foo();
267 |       // }
268 |       // In this case, we incorrectly type x because of how we
269 |       // infer properties locally. See issue 109.
270 |       // http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/issues/detail?id=109
271 |       //
272 |       // We do not do this inference globally.
273 |       if (n.isGetProp() &&
274 |           !t.inGlobalScope() && type.isNullType()) {
275 |         return true;
276 |       }
277 | 
278 |       mismatch(t, n, msg, type, expectedType);
279 |       return false;
280 |     }
281 |     return true;
